types.name: AnimationHandler
types.summary: One Animator-driven diff unit on a [[UniTextAnimationBridge]]. A Unity Animator writes serialized fields directly, bypassing the property setters that normally raise [[UniTextDirty]]; a handler caches a baseline of the values it watches and, after each apply, re-issues the invalidation those setters would have.
types.remarks: Add handlers to the bridge's inspector list. Built-ins cover the component's own fields ([[UniTextFieldsAnimationHandler]], [[UniTextWorldFieldsAnimationHandler]]); author your own by subclassing this for any other component-level diff. The bridge binds every handler on enable. Diffing runs once per OnDidApplyAnimationProperties — keep it allocation-free in steady state.

methods.name: OnBind
methods.summary: Snapshots the watched values as the comparison baseline and caches any per-bind metadata.

methods.name: OnUnbind
methods.summary: Drops any live binding held beyond [[Host]]. Default: nothing.

methods.name: OnDiff
methods.summary: Diffs watched values, refreshes their baselines, and raises the matching granular invalidation.

properties.name: Host
properties.summary: The component this handler diffs against, or before [[Bind]].

types.name: AssetRevealHandlerProvider
types.summary: Resolves names through an explicit [[UniTextRevealHandlers]] asset reference.
attributes: TypeDescription("Resolves names through an explicit UniTextRevealHandlers asset reference.")

types.name: BounceModifier
types.summary: Periodic hops off the baseline: glyphs jump and land with a sharpened half-sine, staying put between hops. Drive [[Phase]] to animate.
attributes: TypeDescription("Glyphs hop off the baseline; drive Phase to animate.")

properties.name: Amplitude
properties.summary: Hop height in pixels.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Hops per phase unit.

properties.name: Spread
properties.summary: Phase offset between adjacent clusters.

types.name: BurstRevealHandler
types.summary: Launches glyphs from deterministic radial directions into their final cells.
attributes: TypeDescription("Bursts glyphs inward from different radial directions.")

properties.name: Distance
properties.summary: Initial radial distance in pixels.

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Peak deterministic starting rotation in degrees.

properties.name: StartScale
properties.summary: Uniform scale at the reveal frontier.

types.name: ChaosRevealHandler
types.summary: Combines deterministic direction, scale, rotation and colour variation per glyph.
attributes: TypeDescription("Throws every glyph in through a different deterministic transformation.")

properties.name: Distance
properties.summary: Peak initial distance in pixels.

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Peak initial rotation in degrees.

properties.name: Color
properties.summary: Strength of the random colour flash.

types.name: CompositeRevealHandler
types.summary: Applies several reveal handlers in authored order while occupying one modifier slot.
attributes: TypeDescription("Stacks several appearance effects in order.")

methods.name: Apply
methods.summary: Applies every child against its own duration inside this composite's slot: a shorter child settles early, a child at zero starts settled, and a duration at or beyond the composite's rides the slot timeline — the slot length itself always comes from the composite's Duration.

types.name: DominoRevealHandler
types.summary: Raises a glyph from a bottom corner like a falling domino in reverse.
attributes: TypeDescription("Swings glyphs upright from either bottom corner.")

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Starting rotation in degrees.

properties.name: FromRight
properties.summary: Whether the glyph hinges on its bottom-right corner.

types.name: DropRevealHandler
types.summary: Drops a glyph onto its baseline with bounce, tilt and landing squash.
attributes: TypeDescription("Drops glyphs from above and bounces them onto the baseline.")

properties.name: Height
properties.summary: Initial height above the final position, in pixels.

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Initial tilt in degrees.

properties.name: Squash
properties.summary: Peak landing squash.

types.name: EasedRevealHandler
types.summary: Base for handlers whose authored easing remaps [[Progress]].

methods.name: Progress
methods.summary: Returns the current appearance progress after the authored easing curve.

properties.name: Easing
properties.summary: Progress curve used by this appearance effect.

types.name: FadeRevealHandler
types.summary: Fades a glyph from an authored opacity.
attributes: TypeDescription("Fades each glyph into its authored colour.")

properties.name: StartOpacity
properties.summary: Opacity at the reveal frontier.

types.name: FlipRevealHandler
types.summary: Unfolds a glyph around its horizontal or vertical axis.
attributes: TypeDescription("Flips glyphs open horizontally or vertically.")

properties.name: Axis
properties.summary: Axis that starts edge-on.

types.name: FloatModifier
types.summary: Slow two-axis drift on smooth noise — glyphs hover as if suspended in air. Low [[spread]] makes neighbors drift together; high values decouple them.
attributes: TypeDescription("Smooth hovering drift; drive Phase to animate.")

properties.name: Amplitude
properties.summary: Peak drift in pixels.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Noise steps per phase unit.

properties.name: Spread
properties.summary: Noise offset between adjacent clusters — drift coherence along the text.

types.name: GeometricRevealHandler
types.summary: Base for eased effects that transform the glyph quad around a fixed point, which the author chooses. A subclass whose effect reads best from elsewhere sets Pivot in its own constructor, which only seeds the default an author then overrides.

methods.name: PivotPoint
methods.summary: The authored pivot resolved against the current glyph quad.

methods.name: ApplyScale
methods.summary: Scales the current glyph quad around the authored pivot.

methods.name: ApplyRotation
methods.summary: Rotates the current glyph quad around the authored pivot.

methods.name: ApplySkewX
methods.summary: Applies horizontal shear to the current glyph quad around the authored pivot.

properties.name: Pivot
properties.summary: Fixed point this effect's scale, rotation and shear turn around, normalized over the glyph quad: (0,0) its bottom-left, (1,1) its top-right, outside the unit square beside the glyph.

types.name: GlitchModifier
types.summary: RGB-split glitch bursts: during a burst the glyph doubles into magenta and cyan copies pushed in opposite directions under a crisp original, with horizontal jerks and rare blink-outs. Re-rolls [[Rate]] times per phase unit; deterministic per phase, so scrubbing reproduces the same bursts. A colour glyph under the Apply policy gets the jerks, the blink-outs and silhouette fringes; its picture stays in its own layer.
attributes: TypeDescription("RGB-split glitch bursts; drive Phase to animate.")

methods.name: OnEmitQuad
methods.summary: The two tinted copies keep the face's per-vertex alpha so fades carry over; the zero-offset face clone re-draws the original on top of them within this modifier's layer, which is what keeps the glyph crisp between its colour fringes.

properties.name: Intensity
properties.summary: Fraction of glyphs glitching at any moment (0 none, 1 constant chaos).

properties.name: Split
properties.summary: Peak distance of the magenta/cyan copies from the glyph, in pixels.

properties.name: Amplitude
properties.summary: Peak horizontal jerk in pixels.

properties.name: Rate
properties.summary: Corruption re-rolls per phase unit.

properties.name: Phase
properties.summary: Animation input in abstract time units. Wholly external — a driver, tween, or Animator writes it; the modifier only renders it.

types.name: GlitchRevealHandler
types.summary: Corrupts a glyph with jitter, shear, chromatic tint and opacity flicker.
attributes: TypeDescription("Glitches glyphs through chromatic jitter and shear.")

properties.name: Amplitude
properties.summary: Peak positional corruption in pixels.

properties.name: Shear
properties.summary: Peak horizontal shear.

properties.name: Flicker
properties.summary: Opacity instability during appearance.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Corruption changes across one appearance.

types.name: GlyphParamModifier<TParams>
types.summary: Base for phase-driven glyph modifiers: resolves each range's parameters through the cascade into a TParams set and hands it, with the range's resolved phase, to [[OnGlyph]] for every rendered glyph the range covers. Renders one exact state per phase value; never animates on its own. Parameters re-resolve before every mesh rebuild, so driving them re-renders the mesh without re-applying ranges.
types.remarks: Ranges of every modifier sharing the key land in one per-cluster axis — a cluster renders the parameter set of the range applied last, and the glyph pass runs once for it.

methods.name: MarkParamsDirty
methods.summary: Raises the invalidation of a parameter the per-rebuild refresh re-resolves: the mesh regenerates from the current values without re-applying ranges. Every TParams field's state callback points here.

methods.name: ResolveParams
methods.summary: Resolves this range's parameter set through the cascade. Runs on the main thread, at range application and again before every mesh rebuild — implementations read state and cause no side effects.

methods.name: OnGlyph
methods.summary: Transforms the current glyph quad for the resolved parameter set and phase. May run on a worker thread — no Unity API calls.

properties.name: Phase
properties.summary: Animation input in abstract time units. Wholly external — a driver, tween, or Animator writes it; the modifier only renders it. Setting it costs nothing while no range is active.

properties.name: AttributeKey
properties.summary: Key for the per-cluster parameter-set index buffer (see [[AttributeKeys]]). Unique per modifier type.

types.name: GlyphQuad
types.summary: Vertex-level operations on one glyph quad (4 vertices at a base index, order BL-TL-TR-BR) for modifiers that transform glyphs during [[onGlyph]].

methods.name: Center
methods.summary: Geometric center of the quad.

methods.name: Rotate
methods.summary: Rotates the quad around a pivot. Positive radians rotate counter-clockwise.

types.name: InlineRevealHandlerProvider
types.summary: Inline list of named reveal handlers edited directly on the modifier.
attributes: TypeDescription("Inline list of named reveal handlers edited directly on the modifier.")

types.name: IRevealHandlerProvider
types.summary: Named-catalog source of [[RevealHandlerEntry]] appearance effects.

types.name: ModifierFieldsAnimationHandler
types.summary: Animates modifier fields from a Unity Animator: diffs every state field of every modifier in the host's styles and raises each field's own declared invalidation. Rebinds itself when the style graph changes.
types.remarks: A field whose change notification requires a value transition is not diffed — drive it through its parameter surface ([[UniTextDriver]], ownership) instead.
attributes: TypeDescription("Every state field of every modifier on the host.")

types.name: PendulumModifier
types.summary: Glyphs swing around their top edge like hanging signs: rotation = sin(Phase·frequency + cluster·spread)·angle around the top-center pivot.
attributes: TypeDescription("Glyphs swing from their top edge; drive Phase to animate.")

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Peak swing in degrees.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Swings per phase unit.

properties.name: Spread
properties.summary: Phase offset between adjacent clusters.

types.name: PopRevealHandler
types.summary: Springs a glyph from zero scale past its final size and settles.
attributes: TypeDescription("Pops glyphs in with a configurable overshoot.")

properties.name: Overshoot
properties.summary: Back-easing overshoot; 0 removes the overshoot.

properties.name: Pivot
properties.summary: Fixed point of the scale transform, normalized over the glyph quad.

types.name: PulseModifier
types.summary: Scale pulsation around each glyph's center: scale = 1 + sin(Phase·frequency + cluster·spread)·amount.
attributes: TypeDescription("Glyphs pulse in scale; drive Phase to animate.")

properties.name: Amount
properties.summary: Peak scale deviation: 0.15 pulses between 85% and 115%.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Pulses per phase unit.

properties.name: Spread
properties.summary: Phase offset between adjacent clusters.

types.name: RainRevealHandler
types.summary: Drops glyphs from staggered heights with deterministic wind and tilt.
attributes: TypeDescription("Rains glyphs down with per-glyph wind and tilt.")

properties.name: Height
properties.summary: Base falling distance in pixels.

properties.name: Wind
properties.summary: Peak horizontal wind drift in pixels.

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Peak starting tilt in degrees.

types.name: RevealFlipAxis
types.summary: Axis collapsed by a flip reveal.

types.name: RevealGlyphInfo
types.summary: Reveal state of one rendered glyph, delivered mid mesh build. Mutate the current quad through [[generator]] (faceBaseIdx, Vertices, Colors) to animate its appearance any way you want.

methods.name: RevealGlyphInfo
methods.summary: Creates the state of a glyph riding the frontier envelope, taking [[Progress]] from front minus ordinal.

methods.name: WithProgress
methods.summary: The same glyph on an explicit timeline — what a handler wrapping other handlers gives a child to run progress of its own. Keep 1 as the settled glyph, or the child never resolves to the identity transform.

methods.name: WithFront
methods.summary: The same glyph against a restated frontier, its [[Progress]] derived from the new front the way the envelope derives it — what a handler that re-times the frontier itself, rather than one glyph's timeline, hands on.

properties.name: Progress
properties.summary: Normalized appearance state, 1 being the settled glyph in both directions: an appearing glyph runs 0 → 1, a [[hiding]] one 1 → 0. Serialized handlers receive their one-shot timeline; [[GlyphRevealing]] subscribers receive the fractional frontier envelope derived from [[front]] minus [[ordinal]].

fields.name: generator
fields.summary: Mesh generator mid-build, positioned on the glyph's quad.

fields.name: text
fields.summary: The text being built. Reach the layout through it — [[GetRangeBounds]] over [[unit]] gives the unit's settled box, which is what an effect that moves a whole word or line as one body needs.

fields.name: cluster
fields.summary: Codepoint index of the glyph's cluster.

fields.name: unit
fields.summary: Codepoint span of the unit the glyph belongs to — every cluster of it shares this glyph's [[ordinal]] and [[Progress]]. One cluster wide while the frontier counts in clusters.

fields.name: ordinal
fields.summary: Reveal order of the glyph's cluster within its range, 0-based.

fields.name: count
fields.summary: Revealable clusters in the range.

fields.name: front
fields.summary: Fractional reveal frontier in ordinal units, growing 0 → [[count]].

fields.name: hiding
fields.summary: Whether the glyph is leaving the visible part of its range rather than entering it.

types.name: RevealHandler
types.summary: Serializable glyph-appearance policy for [[RevealModifier]]. Custom handlers must transform only the current quad supplied to [[Apply]], remain worker-thread safe, and resolve to the identity transform at [[Progress]] = 1.

methods.name: Apply
methods.summary: Transforms the current glyph quad for its normalized appearance state.

methods.name: ResolvePivot
methods.summary: Resolves a normalized pivot against the current glyph quad, (0,0) being its bottom-left corner and (1,1) its top-right, as everywhere else in Unity. Values outside the unit square land outside the glyph, which is what an effect orbiting a point beside the glyph wants. Bilinear, so a sheared or rotated quad keeps the pivot where the glyph's own axes put it.

methods.name: ApplyOffset
methods.summary: Offsets the current glyph quad without changing its final layout cell.

methods.name: ApplyScale
methods.summary: Scales the current glyph quad around a normalized pivot.

methods.name: ApplyRotation
methods.summary: Rotates the current glyph quad around a normalized pivot.

methods.name: ApplyFade
methods.summary: Multiplies the current glyph quad's authored alpha by a normalized opacity.

methods.name: ApplyTint
methods.summary: Blends a multiplicative tint into the current glyph quad's authored colour.

methods.name: ApplySkewX
methods.summary: Applies horizontal shear to the current glyph quad around a normalized pivot.

properties.name: Duration
properties.summary: Seconds this effect takes to play for one glyph; 0 makes the change instant.

properties.name: SupportedUnits
properties.summary: Granularities this effect is meaningful at. A reveal counting in one outside the set still plays the effect — the mismatch is reported, not corrected — so declare what the effect reads: an effect that only transforms its own quad accepts every granularity, while one that treats [[unit]] as a body needs [[Grouping]].

types.name: RevealHandlerEntry
types.summary: Named appearance effect of an [[IRevealHandlerProvider]] catalog, selected per range by the tag parameter (<reveal=name>). An empty name marks the entry used by ranges that select no name.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Name matched against the tag parameter (case-insensitive); empty serves ranges that select no name.

properties.name: Handler
properties.summary: Appearance effect applied to ranges that select this entry.

properties.name: HideHandler
properties.summary: Effect played while a cluster of this entry leaves the visible part of its range; unset replays [[Handler]] itself, which every effect supports since [[Progress]] is the settled glyph at 1 in both directions.

types.name: RevealModifier
types.summary: Shows only the leading part of each covered range and hides the rest — the engine piece behind typewriter-style text reveal.
types.remarks: Visibility is governed by the [[Front]] parameter together with [[Collapse]]: set the [[Front]] field, author it in markup (<reveal=fade,50%>), or own it per range. The first tag parameter selects the appearance effect by [[RevealHandlerEntry]] name (<reveal=fade>). Clusters are revealed in logical order, whole grapheme clusters at a time — along one shared text-order frontier, or independently per range when [[PerRange]] is on. A cluster covered by overlapping ranges belongs to the innermost one — it alone governs the cluster's visibility and appearance effect. Line breaks are never hidden, so the line structure stays stable while text reveals. Appearance is binary by default; add named entries or subscribe [[GlyphRevealing]] to animate it. A receding frontier animates too: the cluster keeps its place in the mesh — and, where its range collapses, in layout — until its hide effect finishes. [[Collapse]] is a parameter like the rest, so one modifier serves ranges that differ in it: <reveal=,4abs,line,true> clamps a body out of the layout while <reveal=fade,0> elsewhere merely holds text back from the mesh. A collapsing range is settled a pipeline stage earlier than a drawing one, so its frontier moves through a re-parse where the other moves on a mesh rebuild.
attributes: TypeDescription("Shows a controllable fraction of the text, hiding the rest.")

methods.name: VisibleRangeIn
methods.summary: Codepoint span shown by the ranges lying inside span, empty while they show nothing — what [[VisibleRange]] answers for one part of a modifier whose ranges differ. Pair it with a labelled span to ask after the range an author named.

methods.name: AdvanceTime
methods.summary: Advances appear/hide phases by explicit seconds — the tick source for the [[Manual]] clock; other clocks ignore it.

properties.name: Provider
properties.summary: Source of named reveal handlers for <reveal=name> ranges; the entry with an empty name serves ranges that select no name.
attributes: Tooltip("Source of named reveal handlers for <reveal=name> tags handled by this modifier.")

properties.name: HandlerName
properties.summary: Default [[RevealHandlerEntry]] name used by ranges whose tag carries no parameter; empty selects the provider's unnamed entry. A per-range value overrides it.

properties.name: Front
properties.summary: Reveal frontier: a percentage of the frontier axis, or an absolute position in [[Unit]]s (fractional values blend the frontier unit; positions beyond the length show everything). In markup a bare number is the percentage — an absolute position carries the abs suffix, so four lines is 4abs and plain 4 is four percent of them. Addresses one shared text-order frontier, or each range independently when [[PerRange]] is on.

properties.name: Unit
properties.summary: What one step of [[Front]] covers. Changing it rewrites an absolute [[Front]] to the number of new units the same text takes, so the revealed text stays put — two clusters become the one line holding them, and a front of two hundred clusters spanning five lines becomes five. A percentage needs no rewrite. A per-range value counts only where each range fills on its own: with [[PerRange]] off there is a single frontier axis, and one axis carries one numbering — the modifier's own.

properties.name: Collapse
properties.summary: When, hidden clusters are taken out of the layout and the text reflows (CSS display: none); when, they keep their space and are only not drawn (CSS visibility: hidden). Ranges may differ: one that collapses is decided a stage earlier than one that only stops drawing, so its frontier moves through a re-parse where the other moves on a mesh rebuild.

properties.name: ReserveFor
properties.summary: Label of the range the last shown line keeps room for, so what follows the frontier lands beside it instead of below: the line gives its tail back — at a break opportunity, whole words — until the labelled range fits. Its room is measured, never declared, so the language, the font, a size or spacing effect on it change nothing here.

properties.name: Clock
properties.summary: Time source appear/hide phases advance on. Manual advances only through [[AdvanceTime]]; a clock change mid-flight restarts running phases.
attributes: Tooltip("Time source for appear/hide phases; Manual advances only through code.")

properties.name: PerRange
properties.summary: When, every range fills independently and simultaneously. When (the default), covered ranges reveal one after another in text order: [[Front]] addresses one shared frontier over the union of covered clusters (each counted once, nesting shares positions).

properties.name: VisibleRange
properties.summary: Codepoint span of the covered text the frontier currently shows, empty while it shows nothing. Reaches from the first shown cluster to the last, so a frontier over several ranges reports the extent it covers rather than each range's own share — ask [[VisibleRangeIn]] for one range's own. Line breaks, which no frontier hides, do not carry the span past what it reveals.

properties.name: IsClipping
properties.summary: Whether the frontier is holding any covered cluster back.

events.name: GlyphRevealing
events.summary: Fires for every rendered glyph of a covered range during mesh build, carrying the glyph's reveal state — the receptor for custom appearance animation (fade, scale-in, drop-in, or anything else): mutate the current quad through [[generator]]. While subscribed, the frontier cluster renders with a fractional [[Progress]] instead of popping in whole. May run on a worker thread — no Unity API calls inside handlers.

types.name: RollingModifier
types.summary: Characters roll on a cyclic glyph wheel: every covered character found in [[Wheel]] renders as its wheel position minus the effective roll, with the fractional part shown as two stacked wheel glyphs sliding through the character's cell (one em of travel per step, clipped to the wheel's ink band). The default digit wheel is an odometer; a letter wheel with a trailing space is a split-flap board. Characters outside the wheel pass through untouched. Drive [[Roll]] toward 0 to settle on the real text; at 0 the modifier costs nothing.
attributes: TypeDescription("Characters roll on a glyph wheel — odometer digits, split-flap letters; drive Roll toward 0.")

properties.name: Roll
properties.summary: Wheel steps still to travel. Negative values roll the opposite direction. Setting it costs nothing while no range is active.

properties.name: Spread
properties.summary: Roll reduction per rolling character within a range — later characters settle later.

properties.name: Wheel
properties.summary: Cyclic wheel alphabet, in rolling order (BMP characters only). Only characters found here roll.

types.name: ScaleRevealHandler
types.summary: Grows or shrinks a glyph from an authored two-axis scale.
attributes: TypeDescription("Scales glyphs in from a configurable size and pivot.")

properties.name: StartScale
properties.summary: Scale at the reveal frontier.

properties.name: Fade
properties.summary: Whether opacity follows reveal progress.

types.name: ScrambleModifier
types.summary: Decode effect: unresolved characters render as random glyphs from [[Charset]] and settle into the real text left-to-right as [[Progress]] grows. [[Phase]] churns the random picks. Both inputs are external and deterministic; the layout never reflows — replacements draw in the real glyphs' cells.
attributes: TypeDescription("Characters decode from random glyphs; drive Progress and Phase.")

properties.name: Progress
properties.summary: Resolved fraction of each range: 0 fully scrambled, 1 real text (and zero per-frame cost).

properties.name: Rate
properties.summary: Random re-picks per phase unit.

properties.name: Charset
properties.summary: Glyph pool for unresolved characters (BMP characters only).

properties.name: Phase
properties.summary: Animation input in abstract time units churning the random picks. Wholly external — a driver, tween, or Animator writes it.

types.name: ShakeModifier
types.summary: Per-glyph jitter: each glyph gets a pseudo-random offset and tilt that re-rolls [[rate]] times per phase unit. Deterministic — the same phase always renders the same jitter, so scrubbing and rewinding work.
attributes: TypeDescription("Random per-glyph jitter; drive Phase to animate.")

properties.name: Amplitude
properties.summary: Peak positional jitter in pixels.

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Peak tilt in degrees. 0 keeps glyphs upright.

properties.name: Rate
properties.summary: Jitter re-rolls per phase unit.

types.name: ShakeRevealHandler
types.summary: Shakes a glyph with deterministic, progressively damped jitter.
attributes: TypeDescription("Shakes glyphs into place with deterministic jitter.")

properties.name: Amplitude
properties.summary: Peak positional jitter in pixels.

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Peak angular jitter in degrees.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Noise changes across one appearance.

types.name: SkewRevealHandler
types.summary: Straightens a glyph from a horizontal shear.
attributes: TypeDescription("Skews glyphs into place from a selected pivot.")

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Starting shear angle in degrees.

types.name: SlideRevealHandler
types.summary: Moves a glyph into place from an authored offset.
attributes: TypeDescription("Slides glyphs into place from any direction.")

properties.name: Offset
properties.summary: Position offset at the reveal frontier, in pixels.

properties.name: Fade
properties.summary: Whether opacity follows reveal progress.

types.name: SpinModifier
types.summary: Continuous rotation of each glyph around its center: rotation = (Phase·frequency + cluster·spread) full turns.
attributes: TypeDescription("Glyphs rotate around their centers; drive Phase to animate.")

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Full turns per phase unit.

properties.name: Spread
properties.summary: Turn offset between adjacent clusters.

types.name: SpinRevealHandler
types.summary: Rotates and scales a glyph into place around an authored pivot.
attributes: TypeDescription("Spins glyphs into place with optional scale and fade.")

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Rotation at the reveal frontier, in degrees.

properties.name: StartScale
properties.summary: Uniform scale at the reveal frontier.

properties.name: Fade
properties.summary: Whether opacity follows reveal progress.

types.name: SpiralRevealHandler
types.summary: Pulls a glyph inward along a shrinking spiral.
attributes: TypeDescription("Spirals glyphs into place while scaling and rotating them.")

properties.name: Radius
properties.summary: Initial orbit radius in pixels.

properties.name: Turns
properties.summary: Orbit turns before settling.

properties.name: Spread
properties.summary: Angular offset between adjacent clusters, in radians.

properties.name: StartScale
properties.summary: Uniform scale at the reveal frontier.

types.name: StretchRevealHandler
types.summary: Settles a glyph from a tall, narrow or wide, flat silhouette.
attributes: TypeDescription("Stretches glyphs into their final proportions.")

properties.name: StartWidth
properties.summary: Horizontal scale at the reveal frontier.

properties.name: StartHeight
properties.summary: Vertical scale at the reveal frontier.

types.name: SwingRevealHandler
types.summary: Lets a glyph swing from its top edge and damp into place.
attributes: TypeDescription("Swings glyphs from their top edge with damped motion.")

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Initial swing angle in degrees.

properties.name: Oscillations
properties.summary: Complete swings before settling.

types.name: TintRevealHandler
types.summary: Transitions a glyph from a colour flash into its authored colour.
attributes: TypeDescription("Introduces glyphs through a coloured flash.")

properties.name: StartTint
properties.summary: Multiplicative colour at the reveal frontier.

properties.name: StartOpacity
properties.summary: Opacity at the reveal frontier.

types.name: UniTextRevealHandlers
types.summary: Project asset carrying a shared set of named reveal handlers.

types.name: WaveModifier
types.summary: Vertical sine wave traveling along the text: offset = sin(Phase·frequency + cluster·spread)·amplitude. Drive [[Phase]] to animate; a fixed phase renders that exact wave snapshot.
attributes: TypeDescription("Vertical sine wave along the text; drive Phase to animate.")

properties.name: Amplitude
properties.summary: Peak vertical offset in pixels.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Oscillations per phase unit.

properties.name: Spread
properties.summary: Phase offset between adjacent clusters — how far the wave travels along the text.

types.name: WaveRevealHandler
types.summary: Floats a glyph through damped vertical ripples before it settles.
attributes: TypeDescription("Ripples glyphs into place along a damped wave.")

properties.name: Amplitude
properties.summary: Peak vertical displacement in pixels.

properties.name: Cycles
properties.summary: Wave cycles across one appearance.

properties.name: Spread
properties.summary: Phase offset between adjacent clusters.

types.name: WobbleModifier
types.summary: Jelly-like rocking: each glyph tilts back and forth around its center, rotation = sin(Phase·frequency + cluster·spread)·angle.
attributes: TypeDescription("Glyphs rock around their centers; drive Phase to animate.")

properties.name: Angle
properties.summary: Peak tilt in degrees.

properties.name: Frequency
properties.summary: Oscillations per phase unit.

properties.name: Spread
properties.summary: Phase offset between adjacent clusters.

types.name: BindEntry
types.summary: One entry in the bind map: the modifier type plus its schema.

types.name: ClipboardCopyContext
types.summary: Read-only selection payload handed to [[SerializeCopy]].

properties.name: Editable
properties.summary: The editable field that initiated the copy operation.

properties.name: SelectedSource
properties.summary: Selection serialized in the source field's own markup syntax.

properties.name: SelectedPlainText
properties.summary: Text written to the plain-text clipboard channel.

properties.name: SelectionStart
properties.summary: Selection start in the active editing view, measured in codepoints.

properties.name: SelectionLength
properties.summary: Selection length in the active editing view, measured in codepoints.

properties.name: VisibleText
properties.summary: Canonical visible document text covered by the selection.

properties.name: Spans
properties.summary: Persistent formatting clipped to [[VisibleText]].

types.name: ClipboardModifierBindMap
types.summary: Static registry of per-type clipboard schemas: which HTML elements, Markdown delimiters, and canonical source tag each [[BaseModifier]] type speaks. The schema is type-level metadata — instances have no say in it — so it lives here, not on the modifier: modifiers stay clipboard-ignorant, registration is explicit (no assembly scan, nothing for IL2CPP stripping to break), and the first paste costs nothing. Built-ins are pre-registered; integrator modifiers join via [[Register{T}]].
types.remarks: Consulted by [[TagHtmlClipboardAdapter]] and [[MarkdownClipboardAdapter]] on copy (schema of each range's modifier) and on paste, where the canonical tag / marker of each format is matched against the destination's styles: a format the field renders is kept, one it does not is stripped to plain.

methods.name: GetSchema
methods.summary: The schema registered for the modifier's type, or.

methods.name: GetSchema
methods.summary: The schema registered for the type, or.

methods.name: Register
methods.summary: Registers a clipboard schema for a modifier type. Built-ins are pre-registered; call once (a static initializer is a good place) for an integrator modifier — without registration its ranges copy as plain text and rich pastes strip its formatting to plain text. A schema needs a [[CanonicalTagName]] or [[MatchesSourceTagName]] to land — anything else is rejected with a warning; repeat registrations of the same type are no-ops. Main thread only.

methods.name: EnsureInitialized
methods.summary: Forces built-in registration if it has not happened yet. Idempotent.

properties.name: Entries
properties.summary: Every registered modifier schema entry, in registration order.

types.name: ClipboardPasteContent
types.summary: Visible paste text and its resolved destination formatting.

methods.name: ClipboardPasteContent
methods.summary: Creates attributed paste content. Every span must fit inside text and start and end on Unicode scalar boundaries.

properties.name: Text
properties.summary: The exact visible text to insert.

properties.name: Spans
properties.summary: Destination formatting in UTF-16 coordinates relative to [[Text]].

types.name: ClipboardPasteContext
types.summary: Read-only payload handed to [[DeserializePaste]]. Carries the editor so adapters can resolve external formatting against the destination's styles.

properties.name: Editable
properties.summary: The editor that initiated the paste.

types.name: ClipboardSpan
types.summary: One persistent formatting annotation clipped to UTF-16 coordinates within [[VisibleText]].

methods.name: ClipboardSpan
methods.summary: Creates one formatting range in UTF-16 coordinates. The range must be non-empty; modifier and rule identify the destination style.

properties.name: Offset
properties.summary: UTF-16 offset from the start of the copied visible text.

properties.name: Length
properties.summary: Length in UTF-16 code units.

properties.name: Modifier
properties.summary: The modifier applied to this attributed range.

properties.name: Signature
properties.summary: Stable modifier identity used by the native UniText clipboard format.

properties.name: Rule
properties.summary: The parse rule that owns this attributed range.

properties.name: SourceToken
properties.summary: The source rule's externally known syntax token, when it has one.

properties.name: Parameter
properties.summary: The formatting parameter carried by the source annotation.

properties.name: IsAtomic
properties.summary: Whether the span represents one indivisible replacement rather than a styled range.

types.name: CssValueFormat
types.summary: The value shape a CSS property carries, selecting the built-in converters that bridge UniText's unit grammar and CSS in both directions on the [[InlineStyle]] channels.

fields.name: Verbatim
fields.summary: The parameter is already a valid CSS value and vice versa (font-family, color names / hex).

fields.name: Length
fields.summary: A CSS length (font-size, letter-spacing): px/%/em pass through (a bare UniText px number gains px on copy; CSS pt/rem approximate to px on paste); deltas and keywords have no rendering.

fields.name: LineHeight
fields.summary: A CSS line-height: like [[Length]], but a unitless CSS value is the multiplier form and maps to UniText em.

fields.name: Color
fields.summary: A CSS color: rgb()/rgba() functions convert to hex on paste; hex and named colors pass through.

types.name: IClipboardAdapter
types.summary: Per-format clipboard pipeline stage. Copy adapters translate the canonical attributed selection into an external format; paste adapters translate that format into attributed destination content. The editor's [[Copy]] walks every registered adapter to build a multi-format clipboard write; on [[Paste]] the highest-[[Priority]] adapter whose [[Format]] is present on the clipboard wins.
types.remarks: Format mapping (semantic ↔ external markup) is declared per modifier type in [[ClipboardModifierBindMap]]; adapters are the orchestration layer that walks the active modifier set + a serializer / parser for the format. This matches the design used by ProseMirror (MarkType.toDOM/parseDOM), Lexical (LexicalNode.exportDOM/importDOM), and CKEditor 5 (model ↔ view converters): the syntactic shape is per-format, the semantic effect is per-modifier, and the adapter is the bridge. Built-in adapters registered by default on every [[UniTextEditable]]: [[PlainTextClipboardAdapter]] — universal floor; always wins when nothing richer is present. [[UniTextSourceClipboardAdapter]] — perfect-fidelity round-trip via the vendor-tree format [[UniTextSource]]. [[TagHtmlClipboardAdapter]] — HTML channel (paste from browsers / Word / Notion; copy as HTML). [[MarkdownClipboardAdapter]] — Markdown channel. The built-in set above is fixed per field.

methods.name: SerializeCopy
methods.summary: Serialize the current selection into this adapter's clipboard format. Returns the text payload to attach under [[Format]]'s identifier, or / empty to skip this format in the multi-format write (e.g. an HTML adapter with no applicable modifiers in the selection).

methods.name: DeserializePaste
methods.summary: Deserialize external clipboard payload into visible text and resolved destination spans. Returns to abort and let the pipeline fall through to the next-best format on the clipboard.

properties.name: Format
properties.summary: Clipboard format this adapter writes on copy and accepts on paste. The editor uses this to populate the multi-format write and to pick the appropriate adapter on paste.

properties.name: Priority
properties.summary: Selection priority on paste. Higher wins. Built-in priorities: [[UniTextSourceClipboardAdapter]]=100 (lossless), HTML=50, Markdown=40, [[PlainTextClipboardAdapter]]=0 (floor). Custom adapters that should preempt the built-ins use values above 100.

types.name: MarkdownClipboardAdapter
types.summary: Markdown ↔ attributed UniText content via modifier-declared markers. Priority 40 — beats plain text, loses to HTML and UniText source. Covers inline emphases — bold **...**, italic *...*, strikethrough ~~...~~, plus any paste-side alias markers a schema declares (_ / __) — and inline links [text](url) (the [[LinkModifier]] parameter is the URL; angle-bracket URLs (<url>) are read, titles are dropped). Inline code, headings, lists, and blockquotes stay deferred — they need a backing code / block modifier the engine does not yet model.

fields.name: Instance
fields.summary: Shared stateless instance. Map building reads the editor passed in via context.

types.name: MarkdownSyntaxKind
types.summary: How a modifier's Markdown form is written: a symmetric wrapping delimiter ([[Wrap]] — **bold**) or the inline link syntax ([[Link]] — [text](url), where the URL is the modifier parameter).

types.name: MediaContent
types.summary: Media offered to a [[MediaReceived]] hook — from a clipboard paste, a drag-and-drop, or a picker (see [[Source]]), before the text-adapter pipeline runs. A handler probes the formats it cares about — image blobs via [[GetData]], files via [[GetFiles]] / [[ReadFile]] — and sets [[Handled]] to consume it; left unhandled, a paste falls through to the normal text channels. [[MediaInputBehavior]] is the inherit-and-override entry point.

methods.name: Has
methods.summary: Whether format is present.

methods.name: GetData
methods.summary: Raw bytes for format, or if absent.

methods.name: GetFiles
methods.summary: File references (paths or URIs), or if none. Get one's bytes with [[ReadFile]].

methods.name: ReadFile
methods.summary: Reads the bytes behind a reference from [[GetFiles]], resolved the way the platform requires. if unreadable.

methods.name: ReadFileAsync
methods.summary: Async variant of [[ReadFile]] — the right call for anything that can be large (video, archives): the file IO runs off the main thread. Resolves to if unreadable.

properties.name: Editable
properties.summary: The editor the media is going into.

properties.name: Source
properties.summary: Whether this arrived by paste, drop, or picker.

properties.name: Handled
properties.summary: Set to consume the media and skip the text channels. Sticky once set.

properties.name: HasFiles
properties.summary: Whether file references are present.

types.name: MediaSource
types.summary: How media reached the field — lets a single [[MediaContent]] handler tell a clipboard paste, a drag-and-drop, and a picker selection apart when it cares, and treat them the same when it doesn't.

types.name: ModifierClipboardSchema
types.summary: Per-modifier-type declaration of how the modifier's semantic effect maps onto external clipboard formats, registered in [[ClipboardModifierBindMap]] to opt the type into HTML / Markdown round-trip; the active clipboard adapters ([[IClipboardAdapter]]) walk this schema set when serializing copy and matching elements on paste.
types.remarks: The schema is the semantic ↔ external-syntax bridge. Source-side syntax (... for [[TagParseRule]], **...** for a Markdown rule) stays a rule-side concern — multiple rules can drive the same modifier, and only the rule knows its own tag name. The modifier owns the external mapping because the external mapping is determined by what the modifier means, not by how it is written in UniText source. Industry parallels: ProseMirror's MarkSpec.toDOM/parseDOM and Lexical's LexicalNode.exportDOM/importDOM put the external-format mapping on the semantic unit, not on the parser — UniText follows the same shape.

methods.name: DoHtml
methods.summary: Shortcut for a schema that only declares an HTML representation. Suits the common case of inline modifiers paired with a single open/close element pair.

methods.name: HtmlInline
methods.summary: Shortcut for parameterless inline modifiers with HTML representation only. The first recognised element name builds the open and close tags. Pass synonyms (e.g. "b", "strong") after the primary element.

methods.name: InlineFormat
methods.summary: Shortcut for parameterless inline modifiers with both HTML and Markdown representations. The HTML side mirrors [[HtmlInline]]; the Markdown side wraps the inner text with markdownMarker on both ends (e.g. ** for bold, * for italic, ~~ for strikethrough).

methods.name: InlineFormatStyled
methods.summary: Inline format recognised by its semantic elements AND by CSS on a span (the Google-Docs clipboard convention), where the CSS off-value also CANCELS a semantic element match — the Docs <b style="font-weight:normal"> fragment wrapper must not bold its content. Copy emits the first element; markdown may be for HTML-only formats (underline).

methods.name: MarkdownDelimited
methods.summary: Shortcut for a schema that only declares a Markdown representation. Same open and close marker for both sides (e.g. ** for bold, * for italic).

methods.name: InlineStyle
methods.summary: Shortcut for parameterised modifiers that map to a single CSS property on a <span>. Copy emits <span style="PROP:VALUE"> with the modifier's tag parameter as VALUE; paste recognises any <span> whose style attribute carries PROP: and returns the property value back as the UniText tag parameter. Used by color, size, letter-spacing, line-height, etc. valueFormat selects the value converters bridging UniText's unit grammar and CSS in both directions — values with no valid rendering on the other side are skipped, never emitted invalid or fed unparseable into a rule.

methods.name: InlineMatchingElements
methods.summary: Shortcut for modifiers whose UniText tag name matches the HTML element name directly (one schema covers <sup>/<sub>, <mark>, <kbd>, etc.). The active style's tag name is spliced into the open and close tag templates via the literal placeholder {tagName}, so the same modifier can drive multiple paired styles (one Style for sup, another for sub) without separate schemas.

methods.name: InlineStyleValue
methods.summary: Shortcut for parameterless modifiers whose presence is signalled by a fixed CSS property/value pair on a <span> — e.g. uppercase via text-transform:uppercase, small-caps via font-variant:small-caps. Copy emits a literal <span style="PROP:VALUE">; paste matches a <span> whose style declares the same property with the same value (case-insensitive comparison).

methods.name: InlineWithAttribute
methods.summary: Shortcut for inline modifiers that map to a single HTML attribute on a dedicated element — e.g. <a href="URL"> for link, <abbr title="…"> for abbreviation, <cite> for citation. Copy emits <ELEMENT ATTR="VALUE">; paste returns the attribute value back as the UniText tag parameter.

methods.name: ExtractAttribute
methods.summary: Reads a single HTML attribute value from a raw element attribute slice. Handles surrounding whitespace (including the newline-separated attributes Word emits), both quote styles around the value, and name substrings inside other attribute names or values (data-style, class="header-style") — a candidate that fails the boundary or = check moves on to the next occurrence instead of giving up. The value is entity-decoded. Returns when the attribute is not present.

methods.name: ExtractCssProperty
methods.summary: Reads a single CSS property value from a raw element attribute slice: locates the real style attribute via [[ExtractAttribute]] (boundary-checked and entity-decoded), then scans its semicolon-separated declarations for property with a word-boundary check (so font-size never matches inside x-font-size). Returns when the property is not present.

properties.name: Html
properties.summary: HTML element mapping. when the modifier has no HTML representation.

properties.name: Markdown
properties.summary: Markdown delimiter mapping. when the modifier has no Markdown representation.

properties.name: CanonicalTagName
properties.summary: UniText source-side tag name for this modifier — the name the paste gate matches against the field's styles. E.g. "b" for bold, "color" for color, "link" for links. Differs from [[RecognizedElements]] when the HTML element name does not match the conventional UniText tag (color uses <span style="color:..."> in HTML but <color=...> in UniText source). when the modifier has no canonical tag.

properties.name: MatchesSourceTagName
properties.summary: When set, the modifier's UniText tag names ARE its HTML element names, per style ([[InlineMatchingElements]]): copy emits the matched style's own tag as the element via the {tagName} template placeholder, and paste of an element applies only the style whose tag equals it. Such a schema has no single [[CanonicalTagName]] — one modifier drives several paired styles (sup and sub).

properties.name: OpenTagTemplate
properties.summary: HTML open tag emitted on copy. May contain the literal placeholder {value} for the modifier's tag parameter.

properties.name: CloseTag
properties.summary: HTML close tag emitted on copy. Typically the matching </element>.

properties.name: RecognizedElements
properties.summary: Case-insensitive HTML element names this schema matches on paste. Never; never empty.

properties.name: ExtractParameter
properties.summary: Optional callback that derives the UniText modifier parameter from the raw attribute slice of a matched HTML element on paste. Receives the substring between the element name and the closing > — e.g. for <span style="color:red"> the callback receives style="color:red". Returns the parameter value to splice into the UniText source tag (e.g. "red"), or when the element does not actually express this modifier (in which case the adapter keeps the inner content but does not wrap it). callback means the modifier is parameterless.

properties.name: ToCss
properties.summary: Optional converter applied to the modifier's tag parameter before it substitutes {value} on copy. Returning skips this schema's wrapper for the span (the content still copies) — invalid CSS is never emitted. converter means the parameter is already a valid CSS value.

properties.name: HasValuePlaceholder
properties.summary: Whether [[OpenTagTemplate]] carries the {value} placeholder — such a schema cannot emit without a parameter.

types.name: ModifierMarkdownSchema
types.summary: Markdown form a modifier produces on copy and recognises on paste. Wrapping formats use a delimiter pair (bold **, italic *, strike ~~); the link form ([[LinkSyntax]]) carries the modifier parameter as the URL of [text](url).

properties.name: OpenMarker
properties.summary: Delimiter emitted before the inner text on copy. Empty for [[Link]].

properties.name: CloseMarker
properties.summary: Delimiter emitted after the inner text on copy. Empty for [[Link]].

properties.name: AliasMarkers
properties.summary: Alternative symmetric delimiters recognised on paste for the same format — CommonMark's underscore aliases (_ for *, __ for **). Copy always emits [[OpenMarker]]/[[CloseMarker]]. Never; empty when the format has one syntax.

properties.name: Kind
properties.summary: Which Markdown syntax this modifier maps to.

fields.name: LinkSyntax
fields.summary: The [text](url) link form; the modifier parameter is the URL.

types.name: PlainTextClipboardAdapter
types.summary: Universal-floor clipboard adapter. Writes the selection as [[PlainText]] on copy and accepts plain text on paste. Always registered on every [[UniTextEditable]]; integrators rarely need to remove or replace it — it is the format every external clipboard consumer understands, the guaranteed last-resort path for both directions.
types.remarks: Priority is 0: every richer adapter wins on paste when its format is present, and falls back to this one when nothing better is available. On copy the payload is exactly the text visible inside the selection. Rich channels independently carry the canonical visible text and formatting spans.

fields.name: Instance
fields.summary: Shared stateless instance. The adapter holds no per-editor state.

types.name: PlainTextPastePolicy
types.summary: How a [[UniTextEditable]] interprets plain-text paste — the only channel whose markup-vs-literal intent is unknown because the format carries no semantic spans.

fields.name: Auto
fields.summary: Pick by [[MarkupVisibility]]: Raw parses, every other mode is literal.

fields.name: Literal
fields.summary: Insert verbatim — markup characters become literal text, never parsed.

fields.name: Parse
fields.summary: Reparse with this field's own rules, as if the text were typed.

types.name: TagHtmlClipboardAdapter
types.summary: HTML clipboard adapter. Converts between the selection's span model and the [[Html]] external format using the per-type schemas registered in [[ClipboardModifierBindMap]] ([[Html]]).
types.remarks: Copy renders the attributed document's shared visible-text-and-spans model — each span resolves its HTML schema by modifier identity, so whatever syntax authored the styling (tags or markers), the HTML carries it. On paste every modifier that declares an HTML schema contributes the mapping HTML element name(s) → the style's rule; the map covers only the formats the field has a style for; elements with no mapping are stripped, their inner content survives. Priority is 50: [[UniTextSourceClipboardAdapter]] (100, perfect-fidelity) wins for UniText → UniText pastes; HTML wins over plain text for paste from external rich-text apps (Word, Notion, Slack, Chrome) and from UniText into them. Paste input is treated as hostile per [[ClipboardBudget]]: the parser is a single-pass tokenizer with an explicit open-element stack (no recursion, no rescans), oversized payloads degrade to the same pass with no element map (plain text out), and nesting past the depth cap flattens. Inter-element whitespace collapses to one space the way CSS renders it (literal only inside <pre>), so pretty-printed Word / Outlook CF_HTML pastes without spurious blank lines and indent runs.

fields.name: Instance
fields.summary: Shared stateless instance. Map building reads the editor passed in via context.

types.name: UniTextSourceClipboardAdapter
types.summary: Native UniText round-trip adapter. Carries the selection as a structured [[UniTextClipboardFragment]] (visible text + markup spans keyed by modifier [[Signature]]) under [[UniTextSource]] (application/vnd.lightside.unitext, RFC 6838 vendor tree).
types.remarks: Fidelity is semantic, not byte-for-byte: copy records the attributed document's visible text and persistent spans; paste resolves each span directly to the destination modifier and rule, dropping it to plain text when the destination has no such modifier and never leaking raw tags. Inline objects round-trip as a one-character Object Replacement Character span. Priority is 100, above HTML (50) and Markdown (40): UniText → UniText keeps the native fragment. External apps that do not recognise the format fall back to [[PlainTextClipboardAdapter]].

fields.name: Instance
fields.summary: Shared stateless instance. Map building reads the editor passed in via context.

types.name: BlockingObjects
types.summary: Physics systems consulted for occlusion between the camera and a text hit.

fields.name: None
fields.summary: No occlusion check. Other raycasters (if present) still participate via distance sort.

fields.name: TwoD
fields.summary: Check 2D colliders (Physics2D).

fields.name: ThreeD
fields.summary: Check 3D colliders (Physics).

fields.name: All
fields.summary: Check both 2D and 3D colliders.

types.name: CachedTransformData
types.summary: Snapshot of main-thread state captured before parallel processing — Unity APIs ([[rect]], etc.) cannot be touched from worker threads.

fields.name: name
fields.summary: Component name for worker-safe diagnostics. Captured on the first rebuild in players; always fresh in the editor.

fields.name: rect
fields.summary: The padded inner rect ([[GetPaddedRect]]) snapshotted on the main thread.

fields.name: visibleYMin
fields.summary: Local-space visible band from [[VisibleWindow]], padded with the culling hysteresis margin; ±infinity when culling is off.

fields.name: visibleYMax
fields.summary: Local-space visible band from [[VisibleWindow]], padded with the culling hysteresis margin; ±infinity when culling is off.

types.name: DriverLoop
types.summary: Legacy playhead repeat modes.

types.name: FitStep
types.summary: One budget of the auto-size fit ladder: an adjustment the component spends, in list order, before reducing the font size. Each step maps a fraction of its configured budget onto the shared [[FitBudgets]] the layout core consumes.

types.name: GlyphScaleFitStep
types.summary: Compresses glyphs horizontally, up to a limit, before the font size shrinks — the hz / InDesign glyph-scaling lever. Quads and advances narrow together, so the text keeps its height while gaining columns.
types.remarks: Values beyond ~2–3% visibly distort letterforms (vertical strokes thin while horizontal ones keep their weight) and stretch SDF effects anisotropically; print systems cap this lever at 2%.
attributes: TypeDescription("Compresses glyph width (hz-style) before the font size shrinks.")

properties.name: MaxCompression
properties.summary: Largest allowed width reduction, in percent. 2 matches the pdfTeX/InDesign norm.
attributes: Tooltip("Maximum glyph-width compression, in percent. Above 3% letterforms visibly distort.")

types.name: IUniTextResolver
types.summary: Hook that can override the source text of a [[UniTextBase]] before it is parsed, shaped and laid out — without touching the serialized text field.
types.remarks: Typical use cases: editor-time localization preview (swap keys for translated strings without dirtying scenes or prefabs), runtime localization bound to a language signal, or any derived-text scenario where the authored text is a template or key. Assign via [[TextResolver]]. When a resolver is attached and [[TryResolve]] returns, the component renders the override; the serialized text remains untouched, so scenes and prefabs are not marked dirty. Threading — same two-phase contract as [[BaseModifier]]: [[PrepareForParallel]] always runs on the main thread. Override to cache values from Unity APIs that are main-thread-only (localization tables, ScriptableObject lookups, AssetDatabase in editor). [[TryResolve]] may run on a worker thread when batched parallel processing is active. Do not call Unity APIs directly from it — read from caches populated in [[PrepareForParallel]]. To trigger a rebuild when your external source changes (language switch, scriptable object edit, etc.) call owner.SetDirty(UniTextDirty.Text) — the owner is supplied to [[OnAttached]].

methods.name: OnAttached
methods.summary: Called after the resolver has been assigned to owner. Use this to cache the owner reference and subscribe to any external signal that should trigger a re-resolve (e.g. a localization language-changed event).

params.name: owner
params.description: The component this resolver is now attached to.

methods.name: OnDetached
methods.summary: Called when the resolver is replaced, cleared, or its owner is destroyed. Unsubscribe from any signals registered in [[OnAttached]].

params.name: owner
params.description: The component this resolver is being detached from.

methods.name: PrepareForParallel
methods.summary: Called on the main thread before parallel processing begins, once per rebuild. Override to cache values from Unity APIs that are main-thread-only so that [[TryResolve]] can read them without touching the Unity API.

methods.name: TryResolve
methods.summary: Produces the effective text to feed into the parsing pipeline.
methods.remarks: May be invoked on a worker thread when batched parallel processing is active. Do not call Unity APIs directly — populate caches in [[PrepareForParallel]] and read them here.
methods.returns: to use result as the text to render; to pass source through unchanged.

params.name: source
params.description: The current source text of the owner (the serialized text field or the buffer set via [[SetText]]).

params.name: result
params.description: When the method returns, receives the override text. The memory must remain valid until the next [[TryResolve]] call on this component or until [[OnDetached]] is invoked.

types.name: LineHeightFitStep
types.summary: Compresses line height, down to a limit, before the font size shrinks. Line boxes keep their glyphs; only the vertical advance between lines contracts.
attributes: TypeDescription("Compresses line height before the font size shrinks.")

properties.name: MinScale
properties.summary: Smallest allowed line-height fraction of the natural value, in percent.
attributes: Tooltip("Minimum line height, as a percentage of the natural line height.")

types.name: TextMeasureOptions
types.summary: Box constraints and setting overrides for [[MeasureText]]. Every null field falls back to the component's current value, so default measures the current text, as configured, at its natural unconstrained size. Overrides behave exactly like the matching component settings (with [[autoSize]] on, [[fontSize]] is ignored and [[minFontSize]] / [[maxFontSize]] drive the fit). Dimensions are outer ([[Padding]] included).

fields.name: text
fields.summary: Markup text to measure. Null — the component's current text.

fields.name: maxWidth
fields.summary: Wrap width. Null — unconstrained.

fields.name: maxHeight
fields.summary: Box height: with auto-size the font shrinks to fit [[maxWidth]] × this before measuring, like in a real rect. Null — unconstrained. Does not affect flow without auto-size.

types.name: TextOverrideSource
types.summary: Possible sources of a runtime override on top of the serialized [[Text]] — i.e. reasons the rendered text may diverge from what is stored in the scene or prefab. Flags may combine (e.g. [[SetText]] | [[Resolver]] when SetText assigned a runtime buffer and a resolver further substitutes that buffer's content).

fields.name: None
fields.summary: No override — [[RenderedText]] equals [[RawText]] equals the serialized text field.

fields.name: SetText
fields.summary: One of the SetText overloads on [[UniTextBase]] assigned a runtime source, so [[RawText]] diverges from the serialized [[Text]] field.

fields.name: Resolver
fields.summary: An attached [[IUniTextResolver]] returned a substitute from [[TryResolve]] on the last rebuild, so [[RenderedText]] is the resolver's output rather than [[RawText]].

types.name: TrackingFitStep
types.summary: Tightens letter spacing, up to a limit, before the font size shrinks. The reduction applies uniformly to every non-zero glyph advance.
attributes: TypeDescription("Tightens letter spacing before the font size shrinks.")

properties.name: MaxCompression
properties.summary: Largest allowed tracking reduction, in em. Apple-style tightening sits near 0.02.

types.name: UniText
types.summary: Canvas-space text component. Renders into a [[Canvas]] via [[CanvasRenderer]] with full Unicode support — bidirectional scripts (Arabic, Hebrew), complex shaping (Devanagari, Thai), proper line breaking, color emoji, and a markup system via [[ParseRule]].
types.remarks: For world-space text (no Canvas), use [[UniTextWorld]].

methods.name: SetMaterialDirty
methods.summary: Translates Canvas masking notifications into a UniText appearance rebuild.

methods.name: SetClipRect
methods.summary: Sets the clipping rectangle for masking, applying to all sub-mesh renderers. Mask removal reaches a clippable only through this call (never [[Cull]]), so an invalid rect also resets [[VisibleWindow]] and the clip-cull state — otherwise the mesh would stay windowed and culled with no mask to excuse it.

methods.name: SetClipSoftness
methods.summary: Sets soft clipping edges for smooth mask transitions on all sub-mesh renderers.

methods.name: Cull
methods.summary: Culls against the actual rendered mesh bounds rather than the [[RectTransform]] (whose corners serve until a mesh exists). Glyphs can extend beyond the rect (long words, overflow, outline/glow, modifier transforms), so the default rect-corner test would hide still-visible meshes.

methods.name: OnCullingChanged
methods.summary: Restores the effective cull — the union of clip-culling and render suppression — on every culling change, so a direct [[cull]] write from outside never lifts a [[Hide]] or scene-visibility state.

properties.name: CanvasRenderers
properties.summary: Gets all canvas renderers used for sub-meshes.

properties.name: RenderRoot
properties.summary: Single hidden child holding every visible render object this component spawns — glyph sub-meshes and inline media. Kept before user-authored children, after the optional internal mask stamp, so the text composites below nested graphics. Highlights still self-order around it ("Behind" before, "Above" after). One node is positioned instead of each renderer. Main thread only — creates a GameObject.

types.name: UniTextAnimationBridge
types.summary: Bridges a Unity Animator to a [[UniTextBase]]: Animator writes hit serialized fields directly and bypass the property setters that normally invalidate the text pipeline, so this turns them back into the correct [[UniTextDirty]] invalidation.
types.remarks: A sibling capability component, like UniTextSelectable: add it to a GameObject that already has a [[UniText]] or [[UniTextWorld]]. Its presence enables animation diffing; without it the host does no per-frame diff work, so non-animated text pays nothing. All animation is opt-in through [[Handlers]]: add the field handler for your component ([[UniTextFieldsAnimationHandler]] for a [[UniText]], [[UniTextWorldFieldsAnimationHandler]] for a [[UniTextWorld]]) to animate its own fields, and [[ModifierFieldsAnimationHandler]] to animate the fields of any modifier in the host's styles. Per-range animation goes through the parameter surface ([[UniTextDriver]], ownership) instead.

properties.name: TextComponent
properties.summary: The text component this animator drives. Same GameObject; lazily resolved so layout queries work identically in edit and play mode (single runtime path, no edit-time branch).

types.name: UniTextBase
types.summary: Shared base for UniText components — handles text processing (Unicode, BiDi, shaping, line breaking, modifiers, emoji, font fallback, variable fonts). Concrete subclasses supply the rendering backend: [[UniText]] (Canvas) and [[UniTextWorld]] (world-space).
types.remarks: Implements Unity [[EventSystem]] interfaces on the base class so both [[UniText]] (driven by GraphicRaycaster) and [[UniTextWorld]] (driven by PhysicsRaycaster/Physics2DRaycaster with a collider) receive the same events through the same code path. Event surface. [[TextClicked]] — single-tap activation. Consumable: setting [[Consumed]] suppresses propagation of the Unity click to the parent UI hierarchy. Multi-tap detection (double = word, triple = line) is the consumer's responsibility — the host emits one event per click without aggregating. [[ContextRequested]] — unified context-menu request. Triggered by right-click on desktop or long-press on touch / pen (matches HTML contextmenu, WinUI ContextRequested, SwiftUI.contextMenu). Consumable. [[TextLongPressProgress]] — fires every frame while a primary press from a touch / pen pointer is held in place, with progress in [0, 1]. Notification only. Mouse holds do not emit progress. [[HoverChanged]] — hover position changed; [[None]] when the pointer leaves. Notification only. The base class deliberately does NOT implement the uGUI drag interfaces — a plain label must never capture drags from an enclosing ScrollRect. Drag-to-select lives on [[UniTextSelectable]], which implements the drag handlers on the same GameObject and applies the touch-scroll-vs-select policy. It equally does NOT implement [[IPointerClickHandler]]. An input module resolves a click against the click handler found under the pointer at press and again at release, so a label holding that role becomes the click target of every press over it and an enclosing Selectable is activated only when press and release land on the label itself. The release is resolved here instead: this component's own click first, then the enclosing hierarchy's click by the same rule and independent of this component's gesture state. Which side dispatches that hierarchy click depends on the module. One that records PointerEventData.pointerClick already targets the host and dispatches it itself; this component only suppresses it, by clearing that field. One that resolves the click against pointerPress — where this component sits, as the press handler — can never reach the host, so the click is dispatched from here. Clearing eligibleForClick is not a suppression lever: InputSystemUIInputModule reads it into its click decision before it sends the pointer-up, and would dispatch a second click regardless. Emitted [[TextPointerEvent]] instances are REUSED across emissions — consumers must not retain them beyond the callback.

methods.name: CaptureTextSnapshot
methods.summary: Captures immutable rendered text and its range-coordinate revision. The component must have completed at least one parse after its current style graph was attached.

methods.name: GetRangeText
methods.summary: Copies one validated rendered-codepoint range into a stable UTF-16 string. This is the shared representation used by range actions and external export adapters.

methods.name: FindAll
methods.summary: Finds every occurrence of query in the rendered text, writing one codepoint range per match into results (left to right, non-overlapping). Returns the number of matches written; stops early when results is full. Ranges feed [[MutableRangeSource]] and [[GetRangeBounds]] directly. Allocation-free for queries up to 64 UTF-16 chars. Main thread.
methods.remarks: Case-insensitive comparisons use the engine's bundled Unicode simple case mappings — per-codepoint and locale-independent. Multi-codepoint foldings (German ß ↔ ss) and locale-specific rules (Turkish dotless i) do not match; culture-sensitive [[StringComparison]] values behave as their ordinal counterparts.

methods.name: SetText
methods.summary: Sets text content from a char array without allocating a string. Ideal for frequently updated text (timers, scores, etc.).

methods.name: SetText
methods.summary: Sets the text to render without writing to the serialized text field. The change is visible at runtime and in edit mode without marking the scene or prefab as dirty — suitable for editor-time preview (localization) or transient runtime substitution.
methods.remarks: Unlike the [[Text]] setter, this method does not normalize line endings and does not persist the value. For derived text reacting to an external signal, consider [[TextResolver]] instead.

params.name: source
params.description: The text buffer to render. Must remain valid until the next text assignment on this component.

methods.name: SetText
methods.summary: Sets the text to render without writing to the serialized text field. Convenience overload equivalent to SetText(source.AsMemory()). The change does not mark the scene or prefab as dirty.

params.name: source
params.description: The text to render. is treated as empty.

methods.name: SetText
methods.summary: Sets the text to render from a [[StringBuilder]] without writing to the serialized text field and without allocating a [[string]]. The contents are copied into a pooled internal buffer, so the supplied [[StringBuilder]] may be mutated freely after the call.
methods.remarks: Allocation-free per call once the internal scratch buffer has grown to the required capacity. If you already keep your text in a [[char]] array, prefer [[SetText]] to skip the copy.

params.name: source
params.description: The text source. is treated as empty.

methods.name: SetText
methods.summary: Sets the text to render from a character span without writing to the serialized text field and without allocating a [[string]]. The span is copied into a pooled internal buffer, so its backing storage may be reused or released immediately after the call — making this the safe bridge from a pool-rented builder such as ZString's Utf16ValueStringBuilder.AsSpan().
methods.remarks: Allocation-free per call once the internal scratch buffer has grown to the required capacity. Unlike [[SetText]], this does not retain the caller's memory, so a builder whose buffer returns to a pool on dispose is safe to use.

params.name: source
params.description: The text to render. An empty span clears the text.

methods.name: GetPaddedRect
methods.summary: The [[rect]] with [[Padding]] applied: origin shifted by (Left, Bottom), size shrunk by (Left+Right, Bottom+Top), clamped to non-negative. Main-thread only.

methods.name: SetAppearanceDirty
methods.summary: Rebuilds presentation data from cached glyph positions without reporting glyph movement.

methods.name: SetDirty
methods.summary: Marks the specified pipeline stages dirty, conservatively assuming a mesh rebuild may move glyph faces.

methods.name: SetDirty
methods.summary: Marks pipeline work dirty and declares the observable outputs that may change when it commits.

methods.name: SetAllDirty
methods.summary: Ignores Unity's aggregate Graphic invalidation; use [[SetDirty]].

methods.name: SetVerticesDirty
methods.summary: Ignores Unity's Graphic mesh queue; use [[SetDirty]].

methods.name: SetMaterialDirty
methods.summary: Ignores Unity's Graphic material queue unless a rendering backend overrides it.

methods.name: AddRule
methods.summary: Adds a standalone parse rule (one that operates without a modifier, e.g. <noparse>). The rule must report [[IsStandalone]] as.

params.name: rule
params.description: The standalone rule to add.

methods.name: RemoveRule
methods.summary: Removes a standalone rule previously added via [[AddRule]].
methods.returns: if the rule was found and removed.

params.name: rule
params.description: The rule to remove.

methods.name: RefreshFrameTick
methods.summary: Aligns the [[Updating]] subscription with [[NeedsFrameTick]]; call after any change to the state it reads. Off the main thread the refresh is deferred and applied when the processing sweep completes.

methods.name: OnFrameTick
methods.summary: Runs the component's per-frame work from [[Updating]] while [[NeedsFrameTick]] holds. Overrides run their own work after the base call.

methods.name: UpdateRendering
methods.summary: Applies generated mesh data to the rendering backend (CanvasRenderer or MeshRenderer sub-meshes).

methods.name: ClearAllRenderers
methods.summary: Clears all sub-mesh renderers (without destroying GameObjects).

methods.name: ApplyVisibility
methods.summary: Applies the current [[RenderSuppressed]] state to the rendering backend. Must only toggle drawing — cull for Canvas, batch membership (degenerate indices) for world — never tear down or rebuild, so the user [[Show]]/[[Hide]] and the scene-visibility eye share one allocation-free, non-structural path.

methods.name: OnSetDirty
methods.summary: Called after SetDirty. Override to trigger Canvas layout rebuild.

methods.name: OnDeInit
methods.summary: Called during DeInit for subclass-specific cleanup (e.g., stencil materials).

methods.name: Show
methods.summary: Re-shows text previously hidden with [[Hide]]. Reuses the already-built layout and mesh, so it is allocation-free and instant — no re-parse, shaping, layout or mesh rebuild. No-op if already visible.

methods.name: Hide
methods.summary: Hides the text while keeping its built layout, mesh and pooled buffers intact: stops drawing and pointer hit-testing without tearing down the pipeline. Prefer this over disabling the GameObject/component or assigning empty text for text shown and hidden repeatedly (pooled lists, tooltips, HUD) — those force a full pipeline rebuild on every re-show, whereas [[Show]] after [[Hide]] is free. No-op if already hidden.

methods.name: CollectRangeEntries
methods.summary: Collects per-line geometric runs of positioned glyphs whose clusters fall inside [startCluster, endCluster). Output bounds are in mesh-local coordinates with X clamped to each line's measured extent. One [[LineRangeEntry]] is emitted per contiguous run within a line — multiple entries per line are possible if the matched clusters are non-contiguous in visual order.

params.name: startCluster
params.description: Cluster start (inclusive).

params.name: endCluster
params.description: Cluster end (exclusive).

params.name: output
params.description: Pooled list to receive entries (cleared before use).

methods.name: GetRangeBounds
methods.summary: Gets bounding rectangles for a cluster range. One [[Rect]] per contiguous run of glyphs within a line that falls inside [startCluster, endCluster). Trailing whitespace at line ends is excluded (CSS Text §4.1.3). Empty wrapped lines whose break codepoint lies inside the range receive a synthetic narrow rect for caret/selection rendering. Wrapper over [[CollectRangeBounds]] in [[LineBox]] mode.

methods.name: Units
methods.summary: The text's units of unit granularity, in logical order. Enumerating allocates nothing; nothing is computed until it is.

methods.name: Units
methods.summary: The units of unit granularity inside range, in logical order, each clipped to the range. Out-of-bounds parts of the range are dropped.

methods.name: CountUnits
methods.summary: How many units of unit granularity the text holds.

methods.name: CountUnits
methods.summary: How many units of unit granularity range holds. A unit the range only partly covers counts as one.

methods.name: TryGetLabeled
methods.summary: Codepoint span of the range the author anchored with #label, whatever modifier's tag carries it — the whole-text counterpart of a modifier's own WhereLabel query, for a caller that knows the name but not the owner. The first such range in text order answers when a name was used more than once.

methods.name: UnitAt
methods.summary: The unit of unit granularity holding codepointIndex, or an empty range at that index when the text does not reach it.

methods.name: EnsureFirstPassComplete
methods.summary: Ensures the first pass (parsing, BiDi, shaping) has run. No-op in the normal pipeline (Phase 1 already ran). Enables LayoutRebuilder.ForceRebuildLayoutImmediate to work outside the pipeline.

methods.name: MeasureText
methods.summary: Measures the size text occupies under the given constraints and setting overrides — the displayed text, layout and mesh are left untouched.
methods.remarks: Runs the component's full pipeline: styles and modifiers, font fallback, direction, word wrap; the text resolver is bypassed. Every non-null override in options acts exactly as if set on the component (auto-size fits the font into maxWidth × maxHeight like into a real rect). Overrides live in a detached measurement state; component fields are never rewritten, and layout caches plus [[UniTextDirty]] are restored afterwards. Dimensions are outer ([[Padding]] included), so the result maps directly to a RectTransform. Measuring another [[text]] re-parses and re-shapes both texts — cache the result instead of calling every frame. Main thread only.

methods.name: EnsureLayoutComputed
methods.summary: Main layout pass. Computes the "preferred" state — [[cachedPreferredHeight]] and an initial [[cachedEffectiveFontSize]] — for the current rect width. Cached by width only: result is independent of rect.height.
methods.remarks: Main-thread only. Canvas variant invokes this from [[CalculateLayoutInputVertical]]; world-space variant has it called implicitly by [[EnsureLayoutFit]].

methods.name: EnsureLayoutFit
methods.summary: Full layout: main pass then, if needed, shrinks [[cachedEffectiveFontSize]] under the current rect.height. Main-pass state comes from the width cache; second pass is cached by rect.height so repeat calls within a frame are free.
