methods.remarks: Main-thread only. Canvas variant invokes this from [[SetLayoutVertical]]; world-space variant from the render pipeline before mesh generation.

methods.name: GetModifier
methods.summary: Returns the first modifier of type T attached to this component — local [[Styles]] first, then [[StylePresets]] runtime copies, including [[CompositeModifier]] children — or if none.
methods.remarks: The returned reference is the live runtime instance — mutating its public properties is the canonical way to retune modifier behavior at runtime; each setter routes through [[SetDirty]] with the minimum-necessary flag.

methods.name: GetModifier
methods.summary: Returns the first modifier assignable to modifierType, or. Same search scope as [[GetModifier{T}]].

methods.name: TryGetModifier
methods.summary: Try-get form of [[GetModifier{T}]].

methods.name: TryGetModifier
methods.summary: Same lookup as [[GetModifier{T}]], also returning the [[Style]] that owns the found modifier (for a match inside a [[CompositeModifier]] — the composite's style).

methods.name: GetModifiers
methods.summary: Collects every modifier of type T into results (cleared first) and returns the count. Same search scope as [[GetModifier{T}]].

params.name: includeChildren
params.description: When true, a matched [[CompositeModifier]] is still descended into so its children are collected alongside it — needed when T is a base type (e.g. [[BaseModifier]]) the composite itself satisfies, which would otherwise hide its children. When false (default) a match is returned as a unit and its children are skipped.

methods.name: HasModifier
methods.summary: Returns true if any style on this component has a modifier of type T.

methods.name: HasModifier
methods.summary: Returns true if any style on this component has a modifier assignable to modifierType.

methods.name: TryGetStyle
methods.summary: Finds the first style whose modifier is of type T.

methods.name: TryGetStyle
methods.summary: Finds the first style whose modifier is assignable to modifierType.

methods.name: TryGetWholeTextStyle
methods.summary: Finds the first whole-text style (range..) whose modifier is of type T.

methods.name: TryGetWholeTextStyle
methods.summary: Finds the first whole-text style whose modifier is assignable to modifierType.

methods.name: GetStylesOfType
methods.summary: Enumerates every style whose modifier is of type T, local first.

methods.name: GetStylesOfType
methods.summary: Enumerates every style whose modifier is assignable to modifierType, local first.

methods.name: IsWholeTextStyle
methods.summary: True when the style targets the entire text — either it has no source (the canonical no-constraint form created by [[WholeText]]) or it carries a [[FixedRangeSource]] whose single entry resolves to the full range.

methods.name: IsWholeTextSource
methods.summary: True only for a [[FixedRangeSource]] instance that covers the full text. Use [[IsWholeTextStyle]] when checking a style — that variant also accepts the canonical source-less form.

methods.name: SetWholeText
methods.summary: Adds or updates a whole-text style of modifier type T. If an existing local whole-text style exists, its parameter is updated in place; otherwise a new style is added to [[Styles]].

methods.name: SetWholeText
methods.summary: Adds or updates a whole-text style for modifierType, creating a new modifier via factory when none is found locally.

methods.name: ClearWholeText
methods.summary: Removes the first local whole-text style whose modifier is of type T. Returns true if a style was removed.

methods.name: ClearWholeText
methods.summary: Removes the first local whole-text style whose modifier is assignable to modifierType.

methods.name: ToggleWholeText
methods.summary: Inverts the presence of a whole-text style of type T. Adds the style with parameter when absent, removes it when present. Returns true if the style is present after the call.

methods.name: ToggleWholeText
methods.summary: Inverts the presence of a whole-text style for modifierType, creating a new modifier via factory when adding.

methods.name: GetWholeTextParameter
methods.summary: Returns the parameter of the first whole-text style of type T, or null.

methods.name: GetWholeTextParameter
methods.summary: Returns the parameter of the first whole-text style of modifierType, or null.

methods.name: EnsureStyleFor
methods.summary: Ensures the component has a [[Style]] whose modifier is of type T and whose rule covers rule.
methods.remarks: Use when one semantic modifier (e.g. [[ItalicModifier]]) needs to react to multiple input syntaxes — UniText source tags <i>, Markdown markers *…*, GitHub Flavored <em> in pasted HTML. The modifier is created on demand; subsequent calls reuse the same modifier instance and merge the new rule via [[CompositeParseRule]], so all configured rules drive the same underlying modifier output. Rule equality is structural for [[TagRule]] (by tag name) and [[MarkdownWrapRule]] (by marker); other rule types are compared by reference. Equivalent rules are skipped so repeated calls are idempotent.

methods.name: EnsureStyleFor
methods.summary: Non-generic overload of [[EnsureStyleFor{T}]] that uses an externally-constructed modifier when the component does not already have one of the same type.

methods.name: HitTestRange
methods.summary: Range hit test: returns the glyph (and its cluster) under the point. Inclusive of the whole glyph bounding box — clicks anywhere on glyph N return cluster N. Use for entity queries: links, hashtags, mentions, hover-style ranges where left-half vs. right-half of a glyph is irrelevant. Not for caret placement — use [[HitTestCaret]] for that, since caret semantics need the edge-snap (left half → before-glyph, right half → after-glyph).

params.name: localPosition
params.description: Position in local [[RectTransform]] space.

params.name: maxDistance
params.description: Closest-glyph fallback distance when the point is outside every glyph's bounding box. Pass 0 to disable the fallback.

methods.name: HitTestRange
methods.summary: Range hit test from screen coordinates. Overload around [[HitTestRange]] that performs the screen-to-local conversion.

methods.name: HitTestCaret
methods.summary: Caret hit test: returns the codepoint cluster where a caret should be placed for the given screen point. Snaps to the nearest glyph edge on the line determined by the point's vertical coordinate — left half of glyph N → cluster N (caret before the glyph), right half → cluster N+1 (caret after the glyph). Use for caret placement, drag-extend selection, click-to-position. Not for entity detection — clicks at the right edge of a link's last glyph would snap past the link's range; use [[HitTestRange]] for that.

params.name: screenPosition
params.description: Pointer position in screen space.

params.name: eventCamera
params.description: Camera for screen-to-local conversion ( for screen-space-overlay canvases).

methods.name: HitTestCaret
methods.summary: Caret hit test that also reports the affinity bit. Affinity matters at soft-wrap boundaries: a codepoint shared by two lines may render at the right edge of the previous line (upstream) or the left edge of the next line (downstream).

methods.name: IsOverText
methods.summary: Whether the point lies over laid-out text: inside a line's vertical band and within that line's content extent — the web line-box model (gaps between words on a line count as text, the empty area past the line's end does not). Drives hover affordance (I-beam cursor). For caret placement use [[HitTestCaret]], which snaps from any distance instead of rejecting.

methods.name: ResolveEventCamera
methods.summary: Resolves the camera to use for screen-to-local conversion based on the event source.
methods.remarks: Canvas variant returns null for ScreenSpaceOverlay and canvas.worldCamera otherwise; world-space variant returns the raycaster camera from the event data.

properties.name: Font
properties.summary: Optional primary font overriding the first font-stack family.
attributes:
Tooltip("Optional primary font. When set, overrides the primary picked from Font Stack; " +
                 "Font Stack still serves as fallback for missing characters. Leave empty to use " +
                 "Font Stack's first family.")

properties.name: FontStack
properties.summary: Optional primary and fallback font collection.
attributes:
Tooltip("Optional font collection. Provides the primary (when Font is unset) and the " +
                 "fallback chain for characters the primary doesn't have. Leave empty for a " +
                 "single-font setup.")

properties.name: Padding
properties.summary: Inner inset between the [[RectTransform]] edge and the text layout area. Components: x = Left, y = Bottom, z = Right, w = Top. The hit-test and raycast area remains the full RectTransform.
attributes:
Tooltip("Inner inset (Left, Bottom, Right, Top) that shrinks the text area inside the " +
                 "RectTransform. Useful for outline/shadow bleed or caret/IME insets. The raycast " +
                 "area is not affected — it stays the full RectTransform.")

properties.name: HorizontalAlignment
properties.summary: Gets or sets the horizontal text alignment.
attributes: Tooltip("Horizontal text alignment within the container.")

properties.name: VerticalAlignment
properties.summary: Gets or sets the vertical text alignment.
attributes: Tooltip("Vertical text alignment within the container.")

properties.name: UseGlobalStylePreset
properties.summary: Whether this component applies the project-wide style preset.
attributes:
Tooltip("Apply the project-wide StylePreset from Project Settings on top of local " +
                 "Styles / Style Presets. Disable to opt this component out of global rules " +
                 "(e.g. debug overlays where markup would interfere).")

properties.name: RenderMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the text rendering mode used for glyph coverage.
attributes: Tooltip("SDF: rounded corners on outline/underlay effects. MSDF: sharp corners.")

properties.name: CurrentDirtyFlags
properties.summary: Gets the current dirty flags indicating what needs rebuilding.

properties.name: BeforeGenerateMesh
properties.summary: Runs after glyph positioning and before mesh generation.

properties.name: TextProcessor
properties.summary: Gets the text processor instance handling shaping and layout.

properties.name: MeshGenerator
properties.summary: Gets the mesh generator instance.

properties.name: FontProvider
properties.summary: Gets the font provider managing font assets and fallbacks.

properties.name: Buffers
properties.summary: Gets the buffer container for text processing.

properties.name: RawText
properties.summary: The runtime source text — the last value assigned via [[Text]] or any SetText overload, before any resolver substitution. Zero-alloc.

properties.name: ResolvedText
properties.summary: Gets the substitute produced by the attached [[TextResolver]] on the last rebuild, or an empty memory when no resolver is attached or [[TryResolve]] returned. Zero-alloc. Test [[TextOverride]] for [[Resolver]] to know if this value is in use.

properties.name: RenderedText
properties.summary: Gets the text actually fed into the parsing / shaping / layout pipeline: the resolver's output if one is active, otherwise [[RawText]]. Zero-alloc. Still contains markup; for the markup-stripped form use [[CleanText]].

properties.name: CleanText
properties.summary: Gets [[RenderedText]] with parsed markup removed. Zero-alloc. The backing buffer is pooled and may be rewritten on the next parse — do not store the span; call new string(span) if you need a stable string.

properties.name: CodepointCount
properties.summary: Number of codepoints in the rendered text (markup resolved). 0 before the first rebuild. This is the codepoint space shared by [[RenderedCodepoints]], [[FindAll]] results, highlight-layer ranges and the range-geometry queries.

properties.name: RenderedCodepoints
properties.summary: The rendered text as Unicode codepoints — the codepoint space highlight layers and range geometry index into. Zero-alloc. The backing buffer is pooled and rewritten on the next rebuild — do not store the span. For the UTF-16 form use [[CleanText]].

properties.name: TextOverride
properties.summary: Combination of flags describing which runtime source(s) are currently overriding the serialized [[Text]]. Flags may combine — for example, [[SetText]] | [[Resolver]] when a SetText buffer feeds an attached resolver that further substitutes the text.

properties.name: TextResolver
properties.summary: Gets or sets a resolver that may override the source text before parsing without modifying the serialized text field. Useful for editor-time localization preview and runtime text-binding without dirtying scenes or prefabs. See [[IUniTextResolver]] for the contract.

properties.name: ResultSize
properties.summary: Gets the computed size of the rendered text.

properties.name: ResultGlyphs
properties.summary: Gets the positioned glyphs after processing.

properties.name: PrimaryFont
properties.summary: Gets the effective primary font: the explicit [[Font]] if set, otherwise [[PrimaryFont]] from [[FontStack]].

properties.name: CurrentFontSize
properties.summary: Gets the current effective font size (accounts for auto-sizing).

properties.name: Text
properties.summary: Gets or sets the serialized source text. The getter returns the serialized field as-is and has no side effects — use [[RenderedText]] to observe what is actually being rendered when an override (SetText buffer or [[TextResolver]]) is active.
properties.remarks: The setter normalizes CRLF to LF, writes both the serialized field and the runtime source buffer, and clears any prior SetText override. It does not affect an attached [[TextResolver]].

properties.name: VisibleWindow
properties.summary: Local-space window that bounds mesh emission: paragraphs fully outside it produce no quads. Layout, selection, caret and hit-testing are unaffected — only rendering is windowed. renders everything. Canvas components feed it from the mask clip rect automatically; set it explicitly for custom virtualized scrollers, in this RectTransform's local space.

properties.name: Language
properties.summary: BCP 47 language tag for this text (e.g. zh-Hans, ja, en-US). Picks the correct font variant for the script and enables the OpenType locl feature. Per-range overrides via <lang=...>...</lang> take priority.

properties.name: NeedsFrameTick
properties.summary: Gets whether the component currently requires a per-frame tick. Overrides extend the demand with their own per-frame state and call [[RefreshFrameTick]] whenever that state changes.

properties.name: IsWorldSpace
properties.summary: Whether this text renders in world space (a scene mesh) rather than in a Canvas. Consumers that adapt to render space query this instead of testing for a concrete component type; [[UniTextWorld]] overrides it to.

properties.name: RenderRoot
properties.summary: Transform under which this component parents its generated render children (glyph sub-meshes, inline media). Main thread only — the Canvas backend lazily creates a hidden container.

properties.name: IsVisible
properties.summary: Whether the text is currently drawn and hit-testable. Setting this is equivalent to calling [[Show]] () or [[Hide]] ().

properties.name: GlyphCount
properties.summary: Gets the total number of glyphs.

properties.name: TextSpan
properties.summary: Codepoint span of the whole processed text — the rendered text after parsing, which is what every structure and range API addresses.

properties.name: UseParallel
properties.summary: Gets or sets whether parallel processing is enabled for multiple components.

properties.name: PreferredHeight
properties.summary: Height the text content needs inside the padded inner rect (accounts for auto-sizing). Does not include vertical [[Padding]] — this is the content-box height, matching CSS height with box-sizing: content-box. The ILayoutElement contract adds vertical padding so ContentSizeFitter sizes the outer RectTransform to fit content + padding.

properties.name: ContextRequested
properties.summary: Occurs when the user has requested a context menu. Triggered by either the secondary pointer button (right-click on desktop) or by holding a touch / pen press in place past [[LongPressDuration]]. Mirrors the HTML contextmenu / WinUI ContextRequested / SwiftUI.contextMenu pattern of one event with multiple platform-appropriate triggers. Fires anywhere on the component's raycast surface (a field's menu must open over its empty area too) — [[Hit]] is a no-hit result off-glyph. Consumable. Callbacks run by ascending order and all receive the event even after it is consumed. The range router uses [[RangeInteractionEventOrder]], ordinary subscriptions default to zero, and selection / editing defaults use [[ComponentDefaultEventOrder]].

properties.name: PointerPressed
properties.summary: Occurs when the primary button has been pressed, before any click resolution. The press anchor for gesture pipelines: caret placement and focus acquisition happen here (click events fire only after release). Resolve the caret cluster from [[ScreenPosition]] via [[HitTestCaret]]; the bundled [[Hit]] is the bounding-box hit. Callbacks run by ascending order and all receive the event even after it is consumed. The range router uses [[RangeInteractionEventOrder]], ordinary subscriptions default to zero, and selection / editing defaults use [[ComponentDefaultEventOrder]].

properties.name: LastHoverResult
properties.summary: Last hover hit test result. Tracked only while [[HoverChanged]] has subscribers — without them the per-move hit test is skipped and this stays [[None]].

fields.name: fontSize
fields.summary: Gets or sets the base font size in points.

fields.name: wordWrap
fields.summary: Gets or sets whether word wrapping is enabled.
attributes: Tooltip("Enable word wrapping at container boundaries.")

fields.name: autoSize
fields.summary: Gets or sets whether automatic font sizing is enabled.
attributes: Tooltip("Automatically adjust font size to fit container.")

fields.name: minFontSize
fields.summary: Gets or sets the minimum font size for auto-sizing.

fields.name: maxFontSize
fields.summary: Gets or sets the maximum font size for auto-sizing.

fields.name: cachedTransformData
fields.summary: Cached transform data captured before parallel processing.

fields.name: cachedEffectiveFontSize
fields.summary: Cached effective font size after auto-sizing. Zero means layout has not been computed; consumers fall back to maxFontSize/fontSize as appropriate.

fields.name: cachedPreferredHeight
fields.summary: Cached preferred height — what the text wants at its unconstrained (main-pass) size. Not updated by the second pass: parent layout groups read this as "desired height", which must stay stable even when the rect is smaller than desired.

fields.name: RangeInteractionEventOrder
fields.summary: Built-in range-routing order; lower values intercept it.

fields.name: ComponentDefaultEventOrder
fields.summary: Built-in selection/editing order; default subscribers run first.

events.name: Rebuilding
events.summary: Occurs when text is about to be rebuilt.

events.name: RectHeightChanged
events.summary: Occurs when the RectTransform height has changed.

events.name: DirtyFlagsChanged
events.summary: Occurs when dirty flags have changed, indicating what needs rebuilding.

events.name: FrameUpdated
events.summary: Occurs once per frame while the component is enabled, from [[Updating]] immediately before script Update callbacks. In edit mode an active subscription keeps the editor pumping frames until removed. Subscribing and unsubscribing are safe from this component's processing on worker threads (modifier lifecycle raised during the sweep); the tick subscription then settles on the main thread when the sweep completes.

events.name: LayoutCommitted
events.summary: Occurs when THIS component's mesh has been applied in a processing sweep (main thread, layout and glyph geometry are final for the frame). Fires only when this component actually reprocessed — consumers reacting to layout changes (coordinate maps, caret geometry, auxiliary geometry, overlay positioning) subscribe here and never pay for other components' updates.

events.name: Committed
events.summary: Occurs after this component commits a processing pass and identifies which observable outputs changed.

events.name: Animated
events.summary: Occurs after Unity's Animator applied animated property values to this component. The Animator writes serialized fields directly, bypassing the property setters that raise [[UniTextDirty]], so nothing invalidates on its own — attach a [[UniTextAnimationBridge]] with the handlers for the fields you animate, or subscribe here and run your own diff, calling [[SetDirty]] with the matching flags.

events.name: TextClicked
events.summary: Occurs when a primary-button click has been confirmed anywhere on this component's raycast surface — [[Hit]] is a no-hit result when no glyph is under the pointer. Subscribers set [[Consumed]] to suppress propagation of the underlying Unity click to the parent UI hierarchy.

events.name: TextLongPressProgress
events.summary: Occurs every frame while a touch / pen pointer is being held in place after the initial press, with progress climbing from 0 to 1 over [[LongPressDuration]]. Stops once the press resolves into a [[ContextRequested]] event or is cancelled by movement / release. Mouse holds do not emit. Notification only.

events.name: PointerLongPressProgress
events.summary: Pointer-aware long-press progress carrying contact identity and coordinates. [[TextLongPressProgress]] remains the hit-only compatibility projection.

events.name: HoverChanged
events.summary: Occurs when the hover position has changed. Fires with [[None]] when the pointer leaves the text entirely. Notification only.

events.name: PointerReleased
events.summary: Occurs when the primary button has been released, paired with [[PointerPressed]]. Touch gesture recognisers resolve tap / long-press release here.

events.name: PointerEntered
events.summary: Occurs when this surface has become the topmost raycast target under the pointer (paired with [[PointerExited]] when it ceases to be). Tracks the actual hovered element, not mere rect containment, so an occluding child / overlapping graphic with a raycast target suppresses it. [[Hit]] is not computed — consumers needing a hit re-test from the position.

events.name: PointerMoved
events.summary: Occurs for pointer movement over this event surface and carries an exact pointer identity. Unlike [[HoverChanged]], it is not limited to mouse-style semantic hover.

types.name: UniTextCommitChanges
types.summary: Observable result categories changed by one completed text-pipeline pass.

fields.name: None
fields.summary: No observable output changed.

fields.name: Content
fields.summary: Parsed text, shaping, ranges, or their associated data changed.

fields.name: Layout
fields.summary: Line breaking or positioned glyph placement changed.

fields.name: GlyphGeometry
fields.summary: Final glyph faces changed after mesh modifiers.

fields.name: Appearance
fields.summary: Mesh paint, material inputs, or auxiliary presentation changed without moving glyph faces.

fields.name: All
fields.summary: Every observable output category may have changed.

types.name: UniTextDirty
types.summary: Which stage of the text pipeline a change invalidates. Each flag names the coarsest work that must rerun; higher stages subsume every cheaper one below. SetDirty re-enters the pipeline at the coarsest flag set, so pick the least expensive stage that still captures the change.

fields.name: None
fields.summary: No rebuild needed.

fields.name: Mesh
fields.summary: Rebuild the mesh (vertices, UVs, colours, indices) from cached glyph positions. The cheapest stage.

fields.name: Positions
fields.summary: Re-place glyphs within their existing line breaks — alignment, justification, vertical metrics.

fields.name: Layout
fields.summary: Re-break lines and reflow. Font-size changes live here: they alter advances, so lines recompute.

fields.name: Text
fields.summary: Re-parse and re-shape: the text content changed.

fields.name: Font
fields.summary: Font asset changed. Resets the font provider and mesh generator, then fully rebuilds.

fields.name: Direction
fields.summary: Base text direction changed.

fields.name: FullRebuild
fields.summary: Text, font, or direction changed — a full re-parse and reshape.

fields.name: All
fields.summary: Everything needs rebuilding.

types.name: UniTextDriver
types.summary: Sequences parameter animation over the sibling text component: each clip owns one modifier parameter across the ranges its query matches and ramps every member between two endpoint values inside its own window on the shared timeline. Clips run in order, overlap freely, and may drive different parameters of different modifiers.
types.remarks: The playhead advances on the chosen clock and is fully scrubbable: set [[Progress]] from code, an Animator, or a Timeline to render any exact state. Ownership follows each clip's query across text edits and releases on disable, returning every range to its cascade. Scrubbing and playback work in edit mode; automatic playback on enable starts only in play mode.

methods.name: Play
methods.summary: Starts or resumes playback; a finished finite run restarts at its beginning for positive speed or its end for negative speed.

methods.name: Pause
methods.summary: Pauses playback, keeping the current state.

methods.name: Stop
methods.summary: Stops playback and returns the playhead to the beginning.

methods.name: Seek
methods.summary: Moves the playhead to a normalized 0..1 position and renders that state.

methods.name: Advance
methods.summary: Advances the playhead by explicit seconds — the tick source for the Manual clock.

methods.name: Rebind
methods.summary: Releases and rebuilds every clip's ownership against the current styles. Before the text component has initialized its style graph this is a deferred no-op; the graph's build signal re-enters it.

properties.name: Duration
attributes: Tooltip("Fixed timeline length in seconds; clips still extend it. 0 derives it from the clips alone.")

properties.name: Speed
properties.summary: Playhead speed multiplier; negative values run backwards.

properties.name: IsPlaying
properties.summary: Whether the playhead is advancing.

properties.name: Playhead
properties.summary: Position on the timeline in seconds: where the sequence evaluates, so a [[PingPong]] return reads as the mirrored position and never as a phase past the end. Setting it seeks the forward pass and renders that state; [[Progress]] is the same position normalized.

properties.name: Progress
properties.summary: Normalized playhead over the timeline, 0..1. Setting it renders that exact state — scrubbing, rewinding and external timelines all work.

properties.name: TimelineLength
properties.summary: Seconds the full timeline lasts: the latest clip end for the current members, or the authored fixed length when that is longer.

types.name: UniTextDriverClip
types.summary: One clip of a [[UniTextDriver]] sequence: a window on the driver's timeline that owns one parameter across the ranges its query matches, ramping every member between two endpoint values.
types.remarks: Outside its window a clip holds its boundary value — [[From]] before the start, [[To]] after the end. A Replace clip holds only until the playhead passes the start of another Replace clip of the same parameter and priority — the latest started clip drives; Add, Multiply and Custom clips compose alongside freely. Releasing the driver returns the parameters to their cascades. With [[Stagger]] above zero the members ramp one after another in text order, and the clip lasts memberDuration + stagger × (members − 1).

methods.name: SetTarget
methods.summary: Binds the clip to a modifier parameter; the editor picker routes through this.

properties.name: Start
attributes: Tooltip("Second on the driver's timeline this clip starts at.")

properties.name: Query
attributes: Tooltip("Ranges this clip drives; filters follow text edits.")

properties.name: Composition
attributes: Tooltip("How the driven values combine with each range's cascade result.")

properties.name: Priority
attributes: Tooltip("Contribution priority against other owners of the same parameter.")

properties.name: Stagger
attributes: Tooltip("Seconds between the starts of adjacent members' ramps.")

types.name: UniTextFieldsAnimationHandler
types.summary: Animates a text component's own fields from a Unity Animator: font size, colour, word wrap, auto-size and its min/max, and horizontal/vertical alignment. Add it to the [[UniTextAnimationBridge]] on a [[UniText]]; use [[UniTextWorldFieldsAnimationHandler]] for a [[UniTextWorld]].
attributes: TypeDescription("Component font size, colour, wrap, auto-size, and alignment.")

methods.name: OnBindExtra
methods.summary: Snapshots a subclass's extra fields into the baseline. Mirror of [[OnDiffExtra]].

methods.name: OnDiffExtra
methods.summary: Diffs a subclass's extra fields, refreshing their baseline, and returns the flags to fold into the single [[SetDirty]] the base issues.

types.name: UniTextRenderMode
types.summary: Text rendering mode: SDF (rounded corners on effects) or MSDF (sharp corners).

fields.name: SDF
fields.summary: Single-channel SDF. Naturally rounds corners on outline/underlay effects.

fields.name: MSDF
fields.summary: Multi-channel SDF. Preserves sharp corners on outline/underlay effects.

types.name: UniTextWorld
types.summary: World-space text component. Renders via [[UniTextWorldBatcher]] with full Unicode support — bidirectional scripts, complex shaping, color emoji, markup.
types.remarks: For Canvas-space (UI) text, use [[UniText]].

properties.name: SortingOrder
properties.summary: Gets or sets the sorting order for render ordering.
attributes: Tooltip("Sorting order within the current sorting layer.")

properties.name: SortingLayerID
properties.summary: Gets or sets the sorting layer ID.

properties.name: Lit
properties.summary: Gets or sets whether this text receives scene lighting.
attributes:
Tooltip("Receive scene lighting. Off (default) renders flat/unlit. " +
                 "Per-component, so lit and unlit world text can sit side by side.")

properties.name: CastShadows
properties.summary: Gets or sets whether this text casts shadows onto other objects.
attributes:
Tooltip("Cast shadows onto other objects. Off by default. Batched per sorting context: if any " +
                 "world text sharing the context casts, the shared renderer casts.")

properties.name: Standalone
properties.summary: Gets or sets whether this text renders through a renderer of its own instead of joining the shared batch mesh.
attributes:
Tooltip("Render through this component's own renderer instead of merging into the shared batch mesh. " +
                 "Gives this text its own depth-sorting position, so sprites and other transparent renderers " +
                 "can sort between it and neighbouring texts. Costs one draw call.")

properties.name: Active
properties.summary: All currently enabled [[UniTextWorld]] instances, maintained by OnEnable / OnDisable. Iterate this instead of FindObjectsOfType.

properties.name: RaycastTarget
properties.summary: When, this text receives pointer events (clicks, hover, interactive ranges) from [[UniTextWorldRaycaster]]. Disable for purely decorative text — the raycaster will skip it.

events.name: Activated
events.summary: Occurs when a [[UniTextWorld]] instance has become active (OnEnable).

events.name: Deactivated
events.summary: Occurs when a [[UniTextWorld]] instance has become inactive (OnDisable).

events.name: RenderDataAvailable
events.summary: Occurs when the component's mesh has been generated and render data is available through [[MeshGenerator]].[[CollectRenderData]].

events.name: RenderDataCleared
events.summary: Occurs when the component's render data should be discarded (e.g. empty text, disabled).

events.name: RenderSuppressionChanged
events.summary: Occurs when [[RenderSuppressed]] has toggled (user Hide/Show or scene-visibility). The batcher reads the live state and flips this component's batch membership without a structural rebuild.

events.name: SortingChanged
events.summary: Occurs when a sorting-context input has changed: [[SortingOrder]], [[SortingLayerID]], [[CastShadows]] or [[Standalone]] (all are batch-key components).

events.name: ParentChanged
events.summary: Occurs when the component's transform parent has changed (may invalidate SortingGroup inheritance).

types.name: UniTextWorldFieldsAnimationHandler
types.summary: The [[UniTextFieldsAnimationHandler]] for world-space text: also animates [[SortingOrder]], [[SortingLayerID]], and [[CastShadows]], re-keying the batch when the Animator changes them.
attributes: TypeDescription("UniTextWorld fields, plus sorting order, layer, and shadow casting.")

types.name: UniTextWorldRaycaster
types.summary: World-space pointer raycaster for [[UniTextWorld]] components.
types.remarks: Attach to a [[Camera]] to route pointer events (clicks, hover) to all active [[UniTextWorld]] components visible from that camera. Analogous to [[GraphicRaycaster]] for Canvas, but uses direct ray/plane/rect math instead of colliders — no physics dependency at the text level. Hit detection: rect containment in each component's local [[RectTransform]] rect. The full rect is the clickable area (like Canvas raycastTarget); finer-grained glyph-accurate hit testing happens inside the component's pointer handling via [[HitTestRange]]. Occlusion: results carry distance, so Unity's [[EventSystem]] sorts them against any other raycaster ([[GraphicRaycaster]], PhysicsRaycaster, Physics2DRaycaster) automatically. For scenes without a PhysicsRaycaster but with physical geometry that should block clicks, set [[BlockingObjects]] to TwoD/ThreeD/All — the raycaster will test for blocking colliders between the camera and the hit point before accepting the hit.

properties.name: BlockingMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets which physics systems are consulted for occlusion.

properties.name: BlockingMask
properties.summary: Gets or sets the layer mask for blocking collider queries.

types.name: AlphanumericFilter
types.summary: Filters alphanumeric input: Unicode letters and ASCII digits [0-9].

types.name: AndroidImeFlags
types.summary: Optional Android IME policies combined as flags.

fields.name: None
fields.summary: No additional IME flags.

fields.name: NoPersonalizedLearning
fields.summary: Incognito keyboard mode — disable personalized learning.

fields.name: ForceAscii
fields.summary: Request an ASCII-capable IME.

types.name: AutoCapitalization
types.summary: Automatic capitalization policy requested from native text input.

fields.name: Default
fields.summary: Use the user's system preference.

fields.name: None
fields.summary: No automatic capitalization.

fields.name: Words
fields.summary: Capitalize the first letter of each word.

fields.name: Sentences
fields.summary: Capitalize the first letter of each sentence.

fields.name: AllCharacters
fields.summary: Capitalize all characters.

types.name: AutoCorrection
types.summary: Autocorrection policy requested from native text input.

fields.name: Default
fields.summary: Use the user's system preference.

fields.name: Enabled
fields.summary: Force autocorrection on.

fields.name: Disabled
fields.summary: Force autocorrection off.

types.name: AutofillHint
types.summary: Semantic field purposes exposed to native autofill services.

fields.name: None
fields.summary: Supplies no semantic autofill hint.

types.name: AutoValidateBehavior
types.summary: Re-runs the editor's [[InputValidatorBase]]s on a schedule and writes the result to [[Validation]] for decorators to show. Without it, validation runs only when app code calls [[SetValidation]].
attributes: TypeDescription("Re-run validators automatically (on change, blur, or submit) to drive the error state")

properties.name: Mode
properties.summary: Schedule that triggers validation for this editor.

types.name: AutoValidateMode
types.summary: When an [[AutoValidateBehavior]] re-runs the editor's validators.

fields.name: OnUnfocus
fields.summary: When the field loses focus.

fields.name: Always
fields.summary: On every value change, including before the user has interacted.

types.name: CaretContext
types.summary: Caret context after a change: the modifiers covering the caret (full set plus what entered and left since the previous state), the selection it was computed for, and the source editor for follow-up queries ([[IsStyleActive{T}]], [[TryGetStyleParameter{T}]], caret geometry). The lists are reused between dispatches — read them during the event call, copy if you need to keep them.

properties.name: Active
properties.summary: Every modifier whose span covers the caret (or the whole selection).

properties.name: Entered
properties.summary: Modifiers the caret just entered.

properties.name: Exited
properties.summary: Modifiers the caret just left.

properties.name: Selection
properties.summary: The selection the context was computed for.

properties.name: IsComposing
properties.summary: Whether an IME composition is in progress (toolbars typically disable).

properties.name: Editable
properties.summary: The editor that raised the change.

types.name: CaretContextBehavior
types.summary: Hosts [[CaretContextHandler]]s — composable consumers of [[CaretContextChanged]], each carrying its own serialized settings ([[StyleStateHandler]] for toolbar button state; subclass the handler for floating bubbles or custom context UI). Code-first consumers subscribe [[ContextChanged]] directly.
attributes: TypeDescription("Caret context: composable handlers reacting to the styles at the caret (toolbar state)")

events.name: ContextChanged
events.summary: Occurs when the caret context has changed, once per change with the full payload.

types.name: CaretContextHandler
types.summary: Composable caret-context consumer hosted by [[CaretContextBehavior]]. A handler carries its own serialized settings, receives every frame-coalesced context change, and can query the source editor through [[Editable]] ([[IsStyleActive]], [[TryGetStyleParameter]], caret geometry). Subclass for toolbar state, floating formatting bubbles, context-sensitive hints.

types.name: CaseTransformBehavior
types.summary: Forces typed and pasted text to a fixed letter case as it is entered — uppercase for codes and serials, lowercase for emails / usernames / tags, title case for names. Changes the stored value, not just the rendering.
attributes: TypeDescription("Force input to upper / lower / title case as you type")

properties.name: Case
properties.summary: Case applied to inserted text.
attributes: Tooltip("Case applied to every inserted character.")

types.name: CharacterCounterDecorator
types.summary: Shows the current length — count, or count/limit when a [[LengthLimitBehavior]] publishes a cap — counting in the cap's [[TextLengthUnit]] (grapheme clusters when there is no cap), and recolors once the count reaches the limit. Counts the document SOURCE — the same space [[LengthLimitBehavior]] enforces in, so count and cap always agree; in a field with hidden markup the count therefore includes the markup characters, not just the visible text.
attributes: TypeDescription("Live length count, optionally against the limit")

properties.name: Target
properties.summary: Text component that displays the current count and optional limit.

properties.name: OverflowColor
properties.summary: Colour applied when the count reaches the active limit.
attributes: Tooltip("Color when the count reaches the limit.")

types.name: DecimalFilter
types.summary: Filters decimal input: digits [0-9], at most one decimal separator (.,,, or the current culture's), plus a single leading minus sign when [[AllowNegative]]. The separator is kept as typed — normalization is a commit concern, not the filter's. The negative option also switches the mobile keyboard to a layout that has a minus key — the iOS decimal pad does not.

properties.name: AllowNegative
properties.summary: Whether a single leading minus sign is accepted and a signed-capable keyboard requested.
attributes: Tooltip("Accept a leading minus sign. Also selects a mobile keyboard that has a minus key.")

types.name: DefocusOnCancelBehavior
types.summary: Releases input focus when editing is cancelled by Escape, system back, or EventSystem cancel.
attributes: TypeDescription("Release focus when editing is cancelled")

types.name: EditAction
types.summary: All possible editing actions for an input field. Decouples input (key presses) from execution (text operations).
types.remarks: Values are ordered so that range checks can be used for permission filtering — use the explicit range constants ([[FirstMove]] / [[LastMove]], [[FirstSelect]] / [[LastSelect]]), never member ordering directly: a member inserted mid-enum must extend the constants or it silently changes classification. Text characters do not appear here — they arrive via a separate text input channel.

fields.name: Ignore
fields.summary: Key consumed with no action — blocks the platform key map's default binding.

fields.name: InsertTab
fields.summary: Not produced by the platform key map — Tab is reserved for focus traversal (the web/WPF convention). A behavior may bind it through the KeyResolver hook for multiline fields.

fields.name: FirstMove
fields.summary: First caret-movement action — range constant for permission filtering.

fields.name: LastMove
fields.summary: Last caret-movement action — range constant for permission filtering.

fields.name: FirstSelect
fields.summary: First selection action — range constant for permission filtering.

fields.name: LastSelect
fields.summary: Last selection action — range constant for permission filtering.

types.name: EditingEndReason
types.summary: How an editing session concluded, carried by [[Defocused]]. Integrators switch on it to tell an accepted edit from an abandoned one without correlating [[Submitted]] and [[Cancelled]] against the end of the session themselves.

fields.name: Dismissed
fields.summary: Focus left without a verdict on the content: another field took focus, the pointer landed elsewhere, the platform dismissed the keyboard, or the session was closed programmatically. The text stands as edited.

fields.name: Committed
fields.summary: The user accepted the content and the session ended on that submission.

fields.name: Cancelled
fields.summary: The user abandoned the edit and the session ended on that cancellation.

types.name: EditProposal
types.summary: A full pending edit as an input filter sees it: [[Inserted]] text about to replace [[ReplacedRange]] in the pre-edit [[Document]] (an empty range at the caret for a pure insert). Filters judge the post-state this proposal produces — replacing a selection is legal whenever the result is legal, regardless of what the replaced text contained.

fields.name: Document
fields.summary: Pre-edit document, read-only.

fields.name: ReplacedRange
fields.summary: Codepoint range being replaced. Empty at the caret for a pure insert.

fields.name: Inserted
fields.summary: Replacement text. Empty for a pure deletion.

fields.name: Reason
fields.summary: Why the edit is happening — a [[TextChangeReason]] constant.

types.name: EditShape
types.summary: The shape of one document mutation: [[Removed]] codepoints replaced by [[Inserted]] codepoints at [[Start]]. Produced by every gap-buffer mutation; consumers use it to patch derived indexed state (range maps, cached counts, undo history) instead of recomputing from the whole document.

methods.name: MapIndex
methods.summary: Maps a codepoint index valid before this edit to the equivalent index after it: indices before [[Start]] are unchanged, indices at or after the removed range shift by [[Delta]] (an index exactly at a pure insertion point moves after the inserted text), and indices strictly inside the removed range collapse to [[Start]].

properties.name: Delta
properties.summary: Net change in document codepoint count.

types.name: EmailFilter
types.summary: Filters email-address characters as they are typed: ASCII letters/digits, one @ (not at start),. (not at start, not right after @), and - _ + %. A character filter, not a full RFC 5322 check — pair with a validator for completeness.

types.name: FieldDecorator
types.summary: Base class for state-driven field visuals: placeholder, floating label, supporting text, character counter, or validation feedback. It participates in the ordinary [[InputBehavior]] lifecycle and appears in the editor's behavior type picker.

methods.name: RequestTick
methods.summary: Starts per-frame [[OnTick]] delivery. Idempotent; idle decorators receive no ticks.

methods.name: StopTick
methods.summary: Stops per-frame [[OnTick]] delivery. Safe to call from inside [[OnTick]].

methods.name: OnAttach
methods.summary: Cache target references and capture any original state to restore in [[OnDetach]].

methods.name: OnDetach
methods.summary: Revert anything applied to targets so the editable returns to its undecorated state.

methods.name: OnFieldState
methods.summary: Called whenever focus, text, composition, or validation changes. Drive visuals from state.

methods.name: OnTick
methods.summary: Per-frame hook delivered only between [[RequestTick]] and [[StopTick]]. deltaTime is unscaled.

properties.name: IsAttached
properties.summary: Whether this decorator is currently attached to an enabled editable.

types.name: FieldState
types.summary: Editable-state snapshot pushed to a [[FieldDecorator]] whenever it changes.

methods.name: FieldState
methods.summary: Creates an immutable snapshot delivered to a field decorator.

fields.name: IsEmpty
fields.summary: No committed text and no in-progress composition.

fields.name: IsFocused
fields.summary: Whether the editable currently owns input focus.

fields.name: IsComposing
fields.summary: Whether an IME composition is in progress.

fields.name: LengthLimit
fields.summary: Length cap published by [[LengthLimitBehavior]]; zero means unlimited.

fields.name: Validation
fields.summary: The validation state currently published by the editable's validators.

types.name: FloatingLabelDecorator
types.summary: Animates a label between its resting position (inside the field) and a floated position (typically the top edge), scaling it down on the way; the label stays visible throughout. For a different motion model — a tween library, a path — write your own [[FieldDecorator]].
attributes: TypeDescription("Animate a label from inside the field to a floated position on focus or content")

properties.name: Label
properties.summary: Label whose authored transform is the resting pose.
attributes: Tooltip("The label that floats. Its authored position and scale are the resting state.")

properties.name: FloatedTo
properties.summary: Transform whose position defines the floated pose.
attributes: Tooltip("Where the label moves to when floated — usually a marker RectTransform at the field's top edge.")

properties.name: FloatedScale
properties.summary: Label scale in the floated pose relative to its resting scale.
attributes: Tooltip("Label scale when floated, relative to its resting scale.")

properties.name: Duration
properties.summary: Transition duration in seconds; zero applies the target pose immediately.
attributes: Tooltip("Seconds for the float transition. 0 = instant.")

properties.name: Easing
properties.summary: Curve mapping normalized transition progress to pose interpolation.

properties.name: Name
properties.summary: Stable command name used by toolbar and context-menu calls.
attributes: Tooltip("Name for Toggle(string) lookups from toolbar buttons / context menus.")

properties.name: Target
properties.summary: Style source toggled by this command.

properties.name: Key
properties.summary: Shortcut key combined with the platform primary modifier.
attributes: Tooltip("Shortcut key, combined with the platform primary modifier (Ctrl / Cmd). None = no shortcut.")

properties.name: Shift
properties.summary: Whether the shortcut additionally requires Shift.
attributes: Tooltip("Require Shift in addition to the primary modifier.")

types.name: GraphemeCountCache
types.summary: Incremental grapheme-cluster count for a document — the per-keystroke companion of [[Count]]. The count is cached by [[Version]]; [[PredictCount]] evaluates a pending edit by re-segmenting only a boundary-safe window around it, and [[CommitEdit]] promotes that prediction to the new cached count when the applied [[EditShape]] matches. Any mutation the cache was not told about degrades to one full recount on the next query.
types.remarks: Window edges are placed on boundaries that UAX #29 guarantees regardless of surrounding context (no RI-parity, ZWJ-emoji, or Indic-conjunct chain can cross them), so clusters outside the window are provably unaffected by the edit. When no safe edge exists within [[MaxAnchorScan]] codepoints (a pathological run of joiners), the prediction falls back to per-part arithmetic and the commit invalidates instead.

methods.name: Count
methods.summary: Grapheme-cluster count of the whole document. O(1) while the cached version matches; one full segmentation (pooled, allocation-free steady state) otherwise.

methods.name: PredictCount
methods.summary: Grapheme-cluster count of the document AFTER applying the proposed edit, computed from a boundary-safe window around it — never a whole-document pass while the cache is warm. Follow up with [[CommitEdit]] once the edit is applied so the prediction becomes the cached count.

methods.name: CommitEdit
methods.summary: Applies a mutation to the cached count: an edit matching the last prediction — same shape AND same inserted content (a later hook may have rewritten the text) — promotes it; anything else invalidates, deferring to a full recount on the next query.

methods.name: Invalidate
methods.summary: Discards all cached state.

types.name: IFormatStyleSource
types.summary: Source of the style a [[TextFormattingBehavior]] command toggles. Applies a style already configured on the component, in that style's own markup syntax — it never creates or registers anything, so on a field that has no matching style the command is inert. [[ReferencedStyle]] addresses by modifier type. Implement to add a custom resolution.

methods.name: Toggle
methods.summary: Toggles the style on the selection (or the pending typing style at a caret). Returns whether it is now on.

events.name: Changed
events.summary: Raised after configuration changes that can affect the resolved or emitted style. Mutable custom implementations must raise this for every such change so an owning formatting behavior can reconcile.

types.name: InputBehavior
types.summary: Base class for composable input policies attached to a [[UniTextEditable]].

methods.name: OnEnable
methods.summary: Registers editor hooks when the behavior becomes active.

methods.name: OnDisable
methods.summary: Releases resources and editor hooks when the behavior becomes inactive.

methods.name: NotifyChanged
methods.summary: Reports a value change to the owning state graph.

methods.name: NotifyStructureChanged
methods.summary: Reports an owned-state replacement to the owning state graph.

methods.name: NotifyNestedChanged
methods.summary: Reports a nested-state change to the owning state graph.

methods.name: InvalidateInputSessionConfiguration
methods.summary: Signals that input-session configuration resolved by this behavior has changed.

properties.name: IsEnabled
properties.summary: Indicates whether the behavior is active, including while either lifecycle hook executes.

properties.name: HasChangeSink
properties.summary: Indicates whether authored-state changes can be propagated to an owning state graph.

fields.name: editable
fields.summary: The owning editor, assigned before [[OnEnable]] and retained through [[OnDisable]].

types.name: InputBehaviorPreset
types.summary: Shareable, project-asset container of [[InputBehavior]] entries that editors apply in bulk via [[BehaviorPresets]] — one asset defines a field archetype (chat composer, form field, password) reused across scenes. Each editor instantiates a runtime copy, so per-instance behavior state never leaks into the asset.
types.remarks: Mutating [[Behaviors]] raises [[Changed]]. Live editors replay leaf members into the matching runtime behavior and rebuild only the affected hook-order suffix for structural changes.

events.name: Changed
events.summary: Raised whenever the preset collection or one of its behavior nodes changes. Generated serialized reconciliation and the public mutation methods use this same event.

events.name: DeltaChanged
events.summary: Raised with exact affected-behavior, member, operation, and replay context.

types.name: InputBehaviorPresetChange
types.summary: Describes one exact structural or nested state transition in an input behavior preset.

properties.name: Kind
properties.summary: Gets the scalar or collection operation that committed.

properties.name: Behavior
properties.summary: Gets the affected authored behavior when one is identifiable.

properties.name: Source
properties.summary: Gets the replayable node that owns [[Member]], when scalar replay is available.

properties.name: Member
properties.summary: Gets the exact generated member token for a nested scalar transition.

properties.name: Structural
properties.summary: Gets whether behavior topology or hook ordering changed.

properties.name: Index
properties.summary: Gets the first affected source index, or -1 when no collection index applies.

properties.name: DestinationIndex
properties.summary: Gets the destination index of a move, or -1 for other operations.

types.name: InputCaretRenderer
types.summary: Lightweight UI graphic that renders the text input caret as a filled rectangle. This is the caret extension point: subclass and override [[OnPopulateMesh]] (reading [[CaretRect]] / [[BlinkVisible]]) for custom shapes — block cursor, underline, gradient — then assign via [[CaretRenderer]].
types.remarks: Inherits [[MaskableGraphic]] so the caret participates in [[RectMask2D]] clipping within the input field viewport. Blink behavior: the caret toggles visibility every [[CaretBlinkInterval]] seconds. After [[CaretBlinkTimeout]] seconds of inactivity the caret stops blinking and remains visible. Any user interaction (typing, cursor movement, selection change, focus) should call [[ResetBlink]] to restart the cycle.

methods.name: SetCaretPosition
methods.summary: Updates the caret rectangle in local coordinates and repaints.
methods.remarks: Rebuilds the mesh immediately instead of via [[SetVerticesDirty]]. The caret rect is recomputed in the editable's post-text-mesh callback, which runs during the canvas rebuild pass; a dirty flag registered there is only drawn next frame — the one-frame caret lag after typing. Building the four-vert quad now sidesteps that rebuild-order dependency.

methods.name: ResetBlink
methods.summary: Restarts the blink cycle and forces the caret visible. The editable calls this on every user interaction (typing, cursor movement, selection change, focus gained).

properties.name: PrefersNonBlinkingCaret
properties.summary: Application-wide accessibility flag: when, caret renderers suppress the blink animation and keep the caret continuously visible. Mirrors iOS 17+ "Prefer Non-Blinking Cursor" and the macOS Reduce Motion cursor sub-setting — surface the platform pref here from your integration layer, alongside [[PrefersReducedMotion]].

properties.name: CaretWidthRatio
properties.summary: Caret width as a fraction of the caret's height (which tracks the component's font size), so the caret keeps the same proportion to the text at any canvas scale or resolution. The default renderer draws the rectangle this wide; custom shapes may ignore or reinterpret it.

properties.name: CaretRect
properties.summary: Latest caret rectangle in local coordinates, for subclass mesh builders.

properties.name: BlinkVisible
properties.summary: Current blink phase, for subclass mesh builders: false = the caret is in its invisible half-cycle.

events.name: PrefersNonBlinkingCaretChanged
events.summary: Occurs when [[PrefersNonBlinkingCaret]] has changed so observers can re-arm visuals. [[InputCaretRenderer]] subscribes automatically.

types.name: InputEdit
types.summary: Describes a prospective committed-text replacement passed by reference through [[InputFilter]]. Filters may rewrite its range, replacement, caret, and attributed payload or reject it; composition previews, history replay, and programmatic text assignments do not enter this pipeline.

methods.name: RemoveFormatting
methods.summary: Removes matching formatting from attributed pasted content without changing its text.

properties.name: Reason
properties.summary: Gets the [[TextChangeReason]] associated with the edit.

properties.name: Rejected
properties.summary: Gets whether the edit is rejected; setting it rejects the edit for the rest of the filter chain.

fields.name: text
fields.summary: Replacement text, or an empty string for a deletion.

fields.name: insertCodepointIndex
fields.summary: Codepoint index at which the replacement begins.

fields.name: replacedCodepoints
fields.summary: Number of codepoints replaced at [[insertCodepointIndex]].

fields.name: document
fields.summary: Committed document state preceding the edit.

fields.name: caret
fields.summary: Resulting caret codepoint, or -1 to place it after the inserted text.

types.name: InputFilterBase
types.summary: Base for input filters — they reject characters as they are typed (digits-only, email chars, …) by subscribing to [[InputFilter]]. A separate concern from validation ([[InputValidatorBase]]), which lets input through and judges the whole value for a visible status.
types.remarks: [[Allows]] receives the full [[EditProposal]] and must judge the POST-state: text replacing a selection is acceptable whenever the resulting value is acceptable, even if the pre-state already contained the typed characters (the replaced ones are going away). Native platforms deliver multi-char strings (macOS NSString, Android CharSequence), so handle codepoints, surrogate pairs, and grapheme clusters. Same extensibility pattern as [[BaseModifier]] / [[ParseRule]]: stored via [SerializeReference, TypeSelector]; built-in and custom filters appear in the picker.

methods.name: Allows
methods.summary: Whether the proposed edit may be applied, judged on the post-state it produces. Return to drop it; the editor then discards it without firing TextChanged. Pure deletions never reach this — character filters do not block deleting.

methods.name: DocumentContains
methods.summary: Returns if the document text SURVIVING the proposal (everything outside [[ReplacedRange]]) contains targetCodepoint — the post-state membership test, minus the inserted text the filter is already iterating. O(document length) per call: chunked span scans keep the constant small, but a custom filter calling this per inserted character on a multiline document is O(n) per keystroke.

methods.name: AcceptsLeadingSign
methods.summary: Whether a sign char at insertedCharOffset within [[Inserted]] ends up as a single leading sign in the post-state: first inserted char, nothing surviving before it, no other sign surviving. Shared by the numeric filters.

properties.name: PreferredKeyboardType
properties.summary: Preferred mobile keyboard type. The input field uses this when no [[NativeKeyboardBehavior]] overrides it.

types.name: InputMaskBehavior
types.summary: Formats input live against a pattern — phone (###) ###-####, card #### #### #### ####, date ##/##/####. Slot characters accept input — # a digit, A a letter, * a letter or digit — and every other character is a literal placed automatically. The whole field is re-formatted on every edit — typing, mid-field edits, paste, and deletion all stay aligned; a caret deletion landing on a literal removes the nearest entered character instead, and deleting the last entered character leaves the field empty (no stranded leading literals). The stored text is the formatted value; [[RawText]] returns the entered characters with literals stripped. Slots match single UTF-16 units (BMP): a supplementary-plane character never fills a slot — mask domains (phone, card, date) are BMP by nature, and the one-char-per-slot invariant is what keeps the caret math exact.
attributes: TypeDescription("Format input against a pattern (phone, card, date)")

properties.name: Pattern
properties.summary: Mask pattern whose slots accept digits, letters, or either.
attributes: Tooltip("Mask pattern: '#' digit, 'A' letter, '*' letter or digit; other characters are literals. E.g. (###) ###-####")

properties.name: RawText
properties.summary: The entered characters with literals removed — the raw value behind the mask.

types.name: InputValidatorBase
types.summary: Base for value validators — judge the whole current value and return a [[ValidationState]] (open status + message) that an [[AutoValidateBehavior]] publishes to [[Validation]] for decorators to show. A separate concern from input filtering ([[InputFilterBase]]), which rejects characters as they are typed.

methods.name: Validate
methods.summary: Verdict for the whole current value. An empty [[Status]] means valid.

types.name: IntegerFilter
types.summary: Filters integer input: digits [0-9], plus a single leading minus sign when [[AllowNegative]]. The negative option also switches the mobile keyboard to a layout that has a minus key — the iOS number pad does not.

properties.name: AllowNegative
properties.summary: Whether a single leading minus sign is accepted and a signed-capable keyboard requested.
attributes: Tooltip("Accept a leading minus sign. Also selects a mobile keyboard that has a minus key.")

types.name: ISavedStateProvider
types.summary: Persists and restores transient editor state — text, selection, scroll position, pending IME composition — across host-driven view recreation. The pattern matches Android SavedStateHandle / iOS UIStateRestoration / Web bfcache (pageshow with persisted=true): the platform hands the editor an opaque dictionary on suspend, hands it back on resume.
types.remarks: The platform integration (Android process death restoration, iOS background-app kill, Web bfcache) is P2 work — the interface ships in P1 so integrators wiring their own state-bundle plumbing have a stable contract today.

methods.name: SaveState
methods.summary: Writes editor state into bundle. Keys use the "unitext." prefix to avoid collisions with caller-owned entries.

methods.name: RestoreState
methods.summary: Reads editor state from bundle. Missing or wrongly-typed entries are silently ignored; restoration is best-effort.

types.name: ITextDocument
types.summary: Read-only view of a text document with codepoint-indexed access. Implemented by [[UniTextEditable]]; consumed by generic text-aware features (find / replace, validators, accessibility readers) that should not depend on the concrete editor type.

methods.name: CopyCodepointRange
methods.summary: Copies codepointCount codepoints starting at startCodepoint into destination. Returns the number of UTF-16 chars written.

methods.name: GetCodepointAt
methods.summary: Returns the Unicode codepoint at codepointIndex. Out-of-range indices return 0.

properties.name: CodepointCount
properties.summary: Number of Unicode codepoints in the document. Surrogate pairs count as one.

properties.name: CharCount
properties.summary: Number of UTF-16 chars in the document — the unit Win32 / AppKit / UIKit IMEs and most string APIs use.

properties.name: Version
properties.summary: Monotonically increasing counter incremented on every mutation. Lets consumers cache derived state and invalidate cheaply.

types.name: KeyboardAvoidanceBehavior
types.summary: Keeps the field (or any assigned target) visible above the software keyboard by translating it upward, animated in lockstep with the system keyboard — the classic "lift the form so the keyboard doesn't cover it" reaction.
types.remarks: Translation moves anchoredPosition.y, so the target must not be driven by a layout group on that axis — point [[target]] at the popup / panel root, not a layout child (for layout-driven forms a resize or scroll reaction fits better). On platforms without frame-synced keyboard animation (iOS, Android <30, WebGL) the motion is driven client-side from the event's timing metadata, or [[fallbackDuration]] / [[fallbackEasing]] when the platform provides none.
attributes: TypeDescription("Lift the field / target above the soft keyboard so it stays visible")

properties.name: Target
properties.summary: Rect translated to remain visible; null resolves the field's clipping parent.
attributes: Tooltip("RectTransform translated to stay above the keyboard. Null = the direct clipping parent, or the editor itself when there is none.")

properties.name: KeyboardPadding
properties.summary: Physical gap retained above the keyboard, measured in density-independent pixels.
attributes:
Tooltip("Breathing room kept between the field's visible bottom and the keyboard top, in dp " +
                 "(density-independent pixels) — a constant physical gap across screen densities.")

properties.name: OnlyWhenOverlapping
properties.summary: Whether an already visible target remains at its authored position.
attributes: Tooltip("Skip translation when the target is already fully above the keyboard. Off: also pull the target down so its bottom sits exactly at keyboard top + padding.")

properties.name: FallbackDuration
properties.summary: Client-side animation duration used when the platform supplies no timing.
attributes: Tooltip("Fallback animation duration when the platform did not report one.")

properties.name: FallbackEasing
properties.summary: Client-side easing used when the platform supplies no animation curve.
attributes: Tooltip("Fallback easing used when the platform did not report a system curve.")

types.name: KeyboardBehavior
types.summary: Base for input behaviors that react to the software keyboard's lifecycle — appearing, hiding, animating, or changing frame — while the field is focused. Subclass to build a reaction: keep the field above the keyboard ([[KeyboardAvoidanceBehavior]]), dock a toolbar to the keyboard top, resize a scroll container, dim a backdrop, and so on. Desktop emits no keyboard events, so every subclass is inert there.
types.remarks: The base owns the wiring: it routes [[KeyboardChanged]] into the per-phase hooks below while the owning editor is focused, and drives [[OnKeyboardUpdate]] once per frame. The per-frame tick outlives focus by the tail of a client-side exit animation: while [[IsAnimating]] is set after [[OnFocusLost]], ticks keep coming so the reaction can animate back to rest instead of snapping. Subclasses override the hooks they need and add their own serialized fields. Animation has two paths by platform (see [[OnKeyboardAnimationProgress]] vs [[OnKeyboardUpdate]]); a cross-platform subclass implements both.

methods.name: OnFocusGained
methods.summary: The owning field gained focus. Capture any baseline state to restore on focus loss. If the keyboard is already up (switching fields under an open keyboard) a synthetic [[OnKeyboardWillChangeFrame]] follows immediately so the reaction can position itself.

methods.name: OnFocusLost
methods.summary: The owning field lost focus. Restore any baseline state captured in [[OnFocusGained]].

methods.name: OnKeyboardWillShow
methods.summary: System is about to show the keyboard; e carries the destination rect plus animation duration/easing. Start any client-driven animation here.

methods.name: OnKeyboardAnimationProgress
methods.summary: Per-frame system animation fraction, only on platforms reporting frame-synced animation ([[hasFrameSyncedAnimation]] = Android API 30+). Elsewhere this never fires — animate from [[OnKeyboardUpdate]] instead.

methods.name: OnKeyboardDidShow
methods.summary: The show animation finished and the keyboard is fully visible.

methods.name: OnKeyboardWillHide
methods.summary: System is about to hide the keyboard. Start any client-driven hide animation here.

methods.name: OnKeyboardDidHide
methods.summary: The hide animation finished and the keyboard is fully gone.

methods.name: OnKeyboardWillChangeFrame
methods.summary: Keyboard frame changed without a hide/show cycle — iPad split-keyboard toggle, hardware keyboard connect/disconnect, rotation, language switch, or a field switch under an open keyboard.

methods.name: OnKeyboardUpdate
methods.summary: Per-frame tick (unscaled delta) while focused, plus the tail of a client-side exit animation after focus loss (as long as [[IsAnimating]] holds). Drive client-side animation here on platforms without frame-synced progress (iOS, Android <30, WebGL).

properties.name: IsAnimating
properties.summary: Whether the reaction is mid client-side animation and still needs [[OnKeyboardUpdate]] ticks — including an exit animation started in [[OnFocusLost]] that must finish after focus is already gone. The base keeps the per-frame tick alive while this holds, then releases it, so the field animates to rest rather than snapping.

properties.name: IsTearingDown
properties.summary: True only while the behavior is being disabled/destroyed. An exit reaction must settle to rest immediately here — no further tick can run to animate it.

types.name: KeyboardRequest
types.summary: Describes soft-keyboard traits resolved before an input session opens or refreshes.

fields.name: config
fields.summary: Keyboard traits to apply; null leaves OS defaults.

types.name: KeyboardType
types.summary: Keyboard layouts with defined iOS, Android, and Web mappings.
types.remarks: iOS-only layouts are selected through [[IOSKeyboardTypeOverride]].

fields.name: Default
fields.summary: Use the system default keyboard.

types.name: KeyResolve
types.summary: Describes a key press being resolved before the platform key map is applied.

fields.name: key
fields.summary: The platform-independent key code.

fields.name: modifiers
fields.summary: The modifier keys held for the key press.

fields.name: action
fields.summary: The resolved action; [[None]] until a hook sets it.

types.name: LengthLimit
types.summary: A length cap and the unit it is measured in. [[Max]] of 0 means no cap.

types.name: LengthLimitBehavior
types.summary: Caps the field length and publishes the cap for a counter to show. Excess input is truncated on a boundary (never splitting a surrogate pair, multi-byte codepoint, or grapheme cluster); input with no room left is rejected; deletions always pass. [[Unit]] chooses what a unit of length means — by default [[Graphemes]], so a family emoji counts as one.
attributes: TypeDescription("Cap the field length (grapheme clusters by default) and publish the cap for a counter")

properties.name: Limit
properties.summary: Maximum length in [[Unit]]; zero disables the cap.

properties.name: Unit
properties.summary: Unit used to measure [[Limit]].
attributes: Tooltip("What a unit of length means. Graphemes = user-perceived characters (recommended).")

types.name: LetterCase
types.summary: Letter case enforced by [[CaseTransformBehavior]].

fields.name: Title
fields.summary: Uppercase the first letter of each word; leave the rest as typed (iOS "words" autocapitalize).

types.name: LinkOnPasteBehavior
types.summary: Pasting a bare URL over a non-collapsed selection turns the selection into a link instead of replacing it with the URL text — the ProseMirror / WordPress paste-link convention. Uses the field's own link style (the style whose modifier speaks Markdown link syntax, composites included); with no link style in the component's Styles the URL pastes as plain text. A collapsed caret pastes normally, and non-URL payloads pass through.
attributes: TypeDescription("Paste a URL over selected text to turn the selection into a link")

types.name: MediaInputBehavior
types.summary: Base for handling received media — a clipboard paste, a drag-and-drop, or a picker selection. All three arrive the same way (check [[Source]] when it matters). The hook is subscribed here — subclass and override [[OnImage]] / [[OnFiles]] (or [[OnMedia]] for full control over every format) to do whatever the app needs: upload, insert an inline object, write to disk. Return from an override to consume; otherwise it falls through to the text channels.
types.remarks: File copies (a video, gif, or any file) arrive as references through [[OnFiles]] — read each with [[ReadFile]]. Inline image data arrives through [[OnImage]]. Reading can prompt the user on iOS / Android / web; the hook only fires on an actual paste / drop / pick, which is the consent the platforms expect.

methods.name: OnMedia
methods.summary: Full-control hook — inspect any format on content directly. Return to consume. Default does nothing and lets [[OnFiles]] / [[OnImage]] run.

methods.name: OnFiles
methods.summary: Override to handle file references (image / video / any file). Return if consumed.

methods.name: OnImage
methods.summary: Override to handle a raster image's bytes. Return if consumed.

methods.name: ReadFile
methods.summary: Reads the bytes of a reference from [[OnFiles]], resolved the way the platform requires — a path read on desktop, a content:// resolver on Android, the captured browser blob on web. if unreadable.

methods.name: ReadFileAsync
methods.summary: Off-main-thread variant of [[ReadFile]] — read a dropped video or large file without blocking the frame (upload flows).

types.name: NameFilter
types.summary: Filters name input: Unicode letters, space, hyphen, and apostrophes (incl. U+2019).

types.name: NativeFieldOverlayBehavior
types.summary: Displays a platform-native replica of the editor while preserving [[UniTextEditable]] as the authoritative document and input pipeline on Android, iOS, and WebGL. Other platforms and editors without this behavior use a transparent native input surface; [[NativeKeyboardBehavior]] configures keyboard traits independently.
attributes: TypeDescription("Render an authoritative UniText document through a native field presenter")

properties.name: PresenterId
properties.summary: Gets or sets the registered presenter used when the field becomes active; activation fails when the target platform has no presenter with this identifier.
attributes: Tooltip("Native presenter registered on the active target platform. The built-in 'system' presenter follows the current host appearance.")

properties.name: Identifier
properties.summary: Gets or sets the control identity exposed to platform tooling.
attributes: Tooltip("Stable platform identity (Android tag / iOS accessibility identifier / DOM id).")

properties.name: PresenterData
properties.summary: Gets or sets opaque data interpreted only by the selected presenter.
attributes: Tooltip("Presenter-defined per-field data, such as JSON or another presenter-owned format.")

fields.name: SystemPresenter
fields.summary: Identifies the built-in presenter that follows the current platform appearance.

types.name: NativeKeyboardBehavior
types.summary: Configures the native soft keyboard for the field: layout, return key, capitalization, autofill, and smart features. The single composable home for keyboard traits — the editor reads it when it shows the keyboard. The traits apply both in the default transparent-keyboard mode and when a [[NativeFieldOverlayBehavior]] renders the OS's own field. Password masking is a separate concern ([[PasswordBehavior]]). Desktop has no soft keyboard — the behavior is inert there.
attributes: TypeDescription("Native soft-keyboard traits: layout, return key, autofill, smart features")

properties.name: Keyboard
properties.summary: The keyboard trait bundle the editor hands to the native layer on show.

types.name: NativeKeyboardConfig
types.summary: Native software-keyboard and text-input traits for an editing session.
types.remarks: Every enum defaults to Default = 0, leaving platform policy intact except [[Default]], which follows whether the field accepts line breaks.

methods.name: NativeKeyboardConfig
methods.summary: Creates a keyboard configuration using platform defaults.

properties.name: KeyboardType
properties.summary: Keyboard layout presented by the OS.
attributes: Tooltip("Keyboard layout presented by the OS (number pad, email, URL, etc.).")

properties.name: ReturnKeyType
properties.summary: Action the return key declares, which also selects its label.
attributes:
Tooltip("Action the return key declares (Go, Search, Done, etc.), which also selects its " +
                 "label. A field that accepts line breaks keeps the plain return key and gets a " +
                 "separate button for this action on the native field.")

properties.name: AutoCapitalization
properties.summary: Automatic capitalization behavior.

properties.name: AutoCorrection
properties.summary: Whether the OS autocorrects typed text.
attributes: Tooltip("Whether the OS autocorrects typed text.")

properties.name: SpellChecking
properties.summary: Whether the OS provides inline spell-checking.
attributes: Tooltip("Whether the OS provides inline spell-checking.")

properties.name: AutofillHint
properties.summary: Semantic hint for the OS autofill system.
attributes: Tooltip("Autofill hint for the OS (username, password, email, etc.).")

properties.name: SmartQuotes
properties.summary: Gets or sets automatic quote substitution on iOS.
attributes: Tooltip("Automatically convert straight quotes to curly quotes (iOS only). Set to No for code / regex / API token fields.")

properties.name: SmartDashes
properties.summary: Gets or sets automatic dash substitution on iOS.
attributes: Tooltip("Automatically convert double hyphens to em-dashes (iOS only). Set to No for code / CLI fields.")

properties.name: SmartInsertDelete
properties.summary: Gets or sets automatic whitespace adjustment around edits on iOS.
attributes: Tooltip("Automatically add/remove whitespace around pasted text (iOS only). Set to No for code editors.")

properties.name: EnablesReturnKeyAutomatically
properties.summary: Gets or sets whether iOS enables the return key only for non-empty text.
attributes: Tooltip("Dim the return key when the field is empty (iOS only).")

properties.name: PasswordRules
properties.summary: Gets or sets iOS password-generation rules, or an empty value for none.
attributes: Tooltip("Password generation rules for iOS Password AutoFill (iOS only). Leave empty for no rules.")

properties.name: IOSKeyboardTypeOverride
properties.summary: Gets or sets a supported iOS-only keyboard type name that overrides [[KeyboardType]].
attributes: Tooltip("iOS-only keyboard by UIKeyboardType name (twitter, namePhonePad, asciiCapableNumberPad). Overrides Keyboard Type on iOS; ignored elsewhere.")

properties.name: IOSReturnKeyOverride
properties.summary: Gets or sets a supported iOS-only return-key name that overrides [[ReturnKeyType]].
attributes: Tooltip("iOS-only return key by UIReturnKeyType name (google, yahoo, route, join, emergencyCall, continue). Overrides Return Key Type on iOS; ignored elsewhere.")

properties.name: ImeFlags
properties.summary: Gets or sets optional Android IME policies.
attributes: Tooltip("Additional Android IME flags, such as private-learning suppression or forced ASCII input.")
