types.name: FontFeature
types.summary: One OpenType feature setting: a four-character feature tag and the value shaping applies it with.
types.remarks: A font that does not carry the tag ignores it. Value 0 disables a feature the shaper would otherwise apply by default, such as kern or liga.

methods.name: FontFeature
methods.summary: Creates a setting for a one-to-four character OpenType tag, space-padded to four as the specification requires.

params.name: tag
params.description: OpenType feature tag, for example kern, liga or ss01.

params.name: value
params.description: Applied value; 0 disables the feature.

exceptions.description: tag is not one to four printable ASCII characters.
value is negative.

methods.name: TryParse
methods.summary: Parses one setting written as tag, tag value, -tag or +tag, where the tag may be quoted and the value may follow a space, colon or equals sign. A bare tag reads as 1, a minus-prefixed tag as 0.
methods.returns: when the whole token was consumed as a valid setting.

properties.name: Tag
properties.summary: Packed four-character OpenType tag, first character in the most significant byte.

properties.name: Value
properties.summary: Applied value: 0 disables the feature, 1 enables it, higher values select an alternate the feature defines.

types.name: FontFeatureRegistry
types.summary: Process-wide registry mapping OpenType feature sets to compact byte ids suitable for per-codepoint attribute storage, and back to the settings the shaper needs.
types.remarks: The registry is additive: once a set is registered its id stays stable for the lifetime of the process, which is what lets shaping caches key on the id alone. Id 0 is reserved for "no features". A set is canonical — sorted by tag, one entry per tag — so equal sets always share an id, and the registry holds at most 255 of them. [[Get]] is lock-free and safe on shaping worker threads; registration is not and belongs to the apply phase.

methods.name: Register
methods.summary: Registers the set written as a comma-separated list of settings — kern 0, -kern, +dlig, ss01 2 — and returns its id. Unparseable settings are skipped; a specification that yields none, or a full registry, returns [[Unset]].

methods.name: Register
methods.summary: Registers a set built in code and returns its id, [[Unset]] when the set is empty or the registry is full. Later duplicates of a tag win.

methods.name: Combine
methods.summary: Returns the id of the union of two sets, where second wins a tag both carry. Either side being [[Unset]] returns the other.

methods.name: Get
methods.summary: Returns the settings of a registered id, empty for [[Unset]] or an unknown id.

fields.name: Unset
fields.summary: Id reserved for "no features". [[Get]] returns an empty set for it.

types.name: HorizontalAlignment
types.summary: Specifies horizontal text alignment within the layout bounds.
types.remarks: [[Start]], [[End]] and [[Justify]] are logical: they resolve against each paragraph's own base direction (UAX #9), so a single value produces different edges for differently-directed paragraphs of the same text. [[Left]] and [[Right]] are physical and ignore direction. Mirrors CSS text-align, which carries both families.

fields.name: Start
fields.summary: Align to the paragraph start edge — left in LTR, right in RTL.

fields.name: Center
fields.summary: Center text horizontally.

fields.name: End
fields.summary: Align to the paragraph end edge — right in LTR, left in RTL.

fields.name: Justify
fields.summary: Stretch each line to fill the full available width by distributing extra space according to [[TextJustify]]. The final line of each paragraph is aligned per [[LastLineAlignment]] (defaults to start, matching CSS text-align-last: auto).

fields.name: Left
fields.summary: Align to the left edge whatever the paragraph direction.

fields.name: Right
fields.summary: Align to the right edge whatever the paragraph direction.

types.name: IAttributeData
types.summary: Interface for custom attribute data stored in [[UniTextBuffers]].
types.remarks: Implement this interface to create custom per-text attribute storage for modifiers. Use [[GetOrCreateAttributeData{T}]] to retrieve instances.

methods.name: Prepare
methods.summary: Sizes the storage to count codepoints and clears it. Called for every registered attribute once per parse, before any modifier applies, so a write or read at any codepoint index of the current text is in bounds.

params.name: count
params.description: The codepoint count of the text about to be laid out.

methods.name: Release
methods.summary: Releases all pooled resources back to the pool.

types.name: InjectedGlyph
types.summary: A character resolved for drawing outside the document text — an ellipsis dot, a list marker, a wheel symbol — in the face the surrounding text uses: which glyph to draw and how far the pen moves past it, which is all placing one takes.
types.remarks: The advance is the only metric a resolve answers in every phase. Ink metrics — bearings, extent — belong to the glyph's atlas entry, which exists only once rasterization has run, while injected characters are measured as early as the shaped phase.

properties.name: FontId
properties.summary: Font carrying the glyph.

properties.name: GlyphIndex
properties.summary: Glyph index inside [[FontId]].

properties.name: Advance
properties.summary: Horizontal advance in pixels at the requested size, with the font's advance overrides applied.

types.name: LanguageRegistry
types.summary: Process-wide registry mapping BCP 47 language tags to HarfBuzz language handles and compact byte indices suitable for per-codepoint attribute storage.
types.remarks: HarfBuzz language handles (hb_language_t) are opaque pointers cached internally by HarfBuzz, so equal BCP 47 strings resolve to the same pointer. HarfBuzz maps BCP 47 to OpenType language tags (e.g. zh-Hans → ZHS, ja → JAN) automatically, which drives the locl GSUB feature in pan-CJK fonts. The registry is additive: once a tag is registered, its index stays stable for the lifetime of the process. Index 0 is reserved for "unset" and maps to HB_LANGUAGE_INVALID.

methods.name: Register
methods.summary: Registers a BCP 47 language tag and returns its compact byte index. Returns [[Unset]] for null/empty tags or if the registry is full.

params.name: bcp47
params.description: BCP 47 language tag (e.g. "zh-Hans", "ja", "ko").

methods.name: GetHandle
methods.summary: Returns the HarfBuzz language handle for a registry index, or [[Zero]] if unset.

methods.name: GetTag
methods.summary: Returns the BCP 47 tag for a registry index, or empty string if unset.

fields.name: Unset
fields.summary: Index reserved for "no language set". Maps to IntPtr.Zero.

types.name: LastLineAlignment
types.summary: Specifies how the final line of a justified paragraph (and lines preceding a mandatory break) is aligned. Mirrors CSS Text Module Level 3 text-align-last.
types.remarks: The "last line" of a paragraph is the line ended by a mandatory break (CR / LF / etc.) or the very last line in the document. [[Auto]] matches the CSS default behaviour: when [[Justify]] is active, the last line is aligned to the paragraph start.

fields.name: Auto
fields.summary: CSS default: equivalent to [[Start]] when justification is active.

fields.name: Start
fields.summary: Align to the paragraph start edge (left in LTR, right in RTL).

fields.name: End
fields.summary: Align to the paragraph end edge (right in LTR, left in RTL).

fields.name: Center
fields.summary: Center the last line horizontally.

fields.name: Justify
fields.summary: Justify the last line as well, stretching it to fill the available width.

types.name: LayoutSettings
types.summary: Configuration for text layout and positioning.
types.remarks: Used by [[TextLayout]] to control how text is positioned within the available bounds. Includes settings for maximum dimensions, spacing, and alignment.

properties.name: Default
properties.summary: Gets the default layout settings with unlimited dimensions, top vertical alignment and start horizontal alignment.

fields.name: maxWidth
fields.summary: Maximum width for text layout. Use [[FloatMax]] for unlimited.

fields.name: maxHeight
fields.summary: Maximum height for text layout. Use [[FloatMax]] for unlimited.

fields.name: lineSpacing
fields.summary: Additional spacing between lines (can be negative).

fields.name: defaultLineHeight
fields.summary: Fallback line height when font metrics are unavailable.

fields.name: horizontalAlignment
fields.summary: Horizontal text alignment within the layout bounds.

fields.name: verticalAlignment
fields.summary: Vertical text alignment within the layout bounds.

fields.name: textJustify
fields.summary: How extra space is distributed when [[horizontalAlignment]] is [[Justify]]. Ignored otherwise.

fields.name: lastLineAlignment
fields.summary: How the paragraph-terminating line is aligned when [[horizontalAlignment]] is [[Justify]]. Ignored otherwise.

fields.name: justifyWordSpaceMin
fields.summary: Smallest word-separator width justification compression may reach, as a fraction of natural width.

fields.name: justifyWordSpaceMax
fields.summary: Largest word-separator width justification expansion spends before the letter and glyph levers engage, as a fraction of natural width. Residual expansion beyond every budget still lands on word separators.

fields.name: justifyLetterSpaceMin
fields.summary: Largest letter-spacing reduction justification compression may spend, in em (non-positive).

fields.name: justifyLetterSpaceMax
fields.summary: Largest letter-spacing addition justification expansion may spend, in em (non-negative).

fields.name: justifyGlyphScaleMin
fields.summary: Smallest glyph-width fraction justification compression may reach; 1 disables the glyph lever.

fields.name: justifyGlyphScaleMax
fields.summary: Largest glyph-width fraction justification expansion may reach; 1 disables the glyph lever.

fields.name: overEdge
fields.summary: Top edge metric for text box trimming.

fields.name: underEdge
fields.summary: Bottom edge metric for text box trimming.

fields.name: leadingDistribution
fields.summary: How extra leading from line-height is distributed relative to the content area.

fields.name: measureTrailingWhitespace
fields.summary: Whether trailing spaces and tabs participate in alignment and reported extents without changing line breaking.

fields.name: lineHeightMode
fields.summary: How each line's height is determined relative to the fonts it contains.

fields.name: lineHeightScale
fields.summary: Line height as a multiple of font size when [[lineHeightMode]] is [[Scaled]]. Ignored otherwise.

fields.name: DefaultLineHeightMode
fields.summary: Project-wide default line-height mode seeded into [[Default]]. Mirrored from [[DefaultLineHeightMode]] and pushed from the main thread, so worker-thread layout reads it without touching Resources.

fields.name: DefaultLineHeightScale
fields.summary: Project-wide default line-height scale seeded into [[Default]]. Mirrored from [[LineHeightScale]].

types.name: LeadingDistribution
types.summary: Controls how extra leading from line-height is distributed relative to the content area.
types.remarks: Different platforms use different models: [[HalfLeading]] — CSS standard: split equally above and below. [[LeadingAbove]] — Figma / iOS: all extra space above the line. [[LeadingBelow]] — Android View / legacy: all extra space below the line.

fields.name: HalfLeading
fields.summary: Extra leading split equally above and below (CSS half-leading model).

fields.name: LeadingAbove
fields.summary: All extra leading placed above the line (Figma model).

fields.name: LeadingBelow
fields.summary: All extra leading placed below the line (Android View model).

types.name: LineBreakType
types.summary: Specifies the type of line break opportunity according to UAX #14.

fields.name: None
fields.summary: No break allowed at this position.

fields.name: Optional
fields.summary: Break is allowed but not required (soft break).

fields.name: Mandatory
fields.summary: Break is required at this position (hard break after CR, LF, etc.).

types.name: LineHeightContext
types.summary: Mutable vertical advance for one line.

fields.name: lineIndex
fields.summary: Zero-based line index.

fields.name: startCluster
fields.summary: First cluster belonging to the line.

fields.name: endCluster
fields.summary: Exclusive end cluster of the line.

fields.name: fontSize
fields.summary: Font size used by the current layout pass.

fields.name: lineAdvance
fields.summary: Resolved vertical advance.

types.name: LineHeightMode
types.summary: How a line's height is determined relative to the fonts it contains.

fields.name: Content
fields.summary: Line grows to fit the tallest font on it, including fallback fonts (CSS line-height: normal).

fields.name: Primary
fields.summary: Height comes from the primary font only; fallback glyphs never enlarge the line (Android fallbackLineSpacing=false).

fields.name: Scaled
fields.summary: Every line is exactly scale × fontSize regardless of content; tall glyphs may overlap (CSS fixed line-height, Flutter forceStrutHeight).

types.name: LineHeightModeContext
types.summary: Mutable line-height mode and scale for one line.

fields.name: lineIndex
fields.summary: Zero-based line index.

fields.name: startCluster
fields.summary: First cluster belonging to the line.

fields.name: endCluster
fields.summary: Exclusive end cluster of the line.

fields.name: mode
fields.summary: Resolved line-height mode.

fields.name: scale
fields.summary: Resolved line-height scale.

types.name: LineRangeEntry
types.summary: A contiguous run of positioned glyphs within a single line whose clusters fall inside a queried range. Bounds are in local mesh coordinates (relative to the text origin), with X clamped to the line's measured extent.

fields.name: lineIdx
fields.summary: Index of the line in buffers.lines.

fields.name: firstGlyphIdx

types.name: TextProcessor
types.summary: Processes Unicode text through script analysis, BiDi reordering, shaping, and layout.
types.remarks: [[TextProcessor]] is the main entry point for the text processing pipeline. It orchestrates multiple Unicode algorithms to produce correctly shaped and positioned glyphs. Processing pipeline: Parsing — converts UTF-16 to codepoints Script analysis (UAX #24) — identifies script per codepoint BiDi algorithm (UAX #9) — determines text direction and reordering Itemization — splits text into runs by script, direction, and font Shaping — converts codepoints to positioned glyphs via HarfBuzz Line breaking (UAX #14) — determines line break opportunities Layout — positions glyphs according to alignment settings Performance: The processor caches intermediate results. Use invalidation methods only when necessary to avoid redundant processing.

methods.name: GetMaxLineWidth
methods.summary: Gets the maximum width among all lines, considering explicit line breaks.
methods.remarks: Measurement-only — does not mutate [[EnsureLines]] / [[EnsurePositions]] caches. Layout queries fired by Unity's ILayoutElement contract (and any other host that calls this on a frame between mesh-build and consumption) must not invalidate the rendered glyph state, otherwise [[PositionedGlyphs]] consumers — hit-test, caret rendering, link click — observe an empty span until the next mesh rebuild. Word wrapping is ignored; mandatory line breaks remain effective. Measured over the text as authored — pristine widths, every mandatory break standing — and never over a hidden layout, which is what a host asking this before it hands the text a width depends on: a width that answered for the current collapse would move whenever the collapse it decides moves, and settle only a frame later.
methods.returns: The maximum line width at the shaping font size, or 0 if no valid data.

methods.remarks: Requires [[HasValidFirstPassData]] to be. Performance: re-breaks lines once per candidate the search cannot answer from the line set it already holds.

methods.name: ReserveLineSpace
methods.summary: Reserves extra leading on one side of a specific line for boundary decorations (over/under ruby, etc.): over above the line, under below it. Added to that line's outer gap, or to the block edge for the first/last line. Largest request per side wins. Called from a modifier's line-height callback.

methods.name: ReserveLineWidth
methods.summary: Reserves width shaping units beside every line for something the text holds room for rather than wraps — a label a frontier keeps a place for, and its like. Added to the width the text reports, so a host sizing to that width leaves the room instead of handing back exactly the text and forcing whoever reserves to take it out of the content. Largest request wins, and requests last until the next parse re-declares them. Called from a modifier's shaped-phase callback, over widths no allocated width can move — a reserve answering to the width it helps decide would chase itself.

methods.name: AddLineGap
methods.summary: Adds a signed amount to the gap between lineIndex and the following line — negative pulls them together, down to full overlap; the gap never inverts. Requests sum, unlike the largest-wins [[ReserveLineSpace]], so a caller composing several of its own values resolves them before calling. Out-of-range indices are ignored, which is what keeps block edges untouched. Called from a modifier's line-height callback.

properties.name: Parsed
properties.summary: Runs after parsing and before shaping, in ascending subscriber order.

properties.name: Analyzed
properties.summary: Runs once bidi levels, scripts, break opportunities, grapheme breaks and word boundaries are final, and before itemization reads them. The phase for work that needs analysis results yet must still reach shaping — hiding clusters from it, above all.

properties.name: Shaped

properties.name: LinesBroken

properties.name: LayoutComplete
properties.summary: Runs after final glyph positions have been calculated.

properties.name: OnCalculateLineHeight
properties.summary: Mutates the vertical advance calculated for each line.

types.remarks: Controls how the last line contributes to the total text height. Matches CSS text-box-edge under-edge values and Figma Vertical Trim.

types.summary: Walks the units of a range, yielding each one's codepoint span. Clipped to the range: the first and last unit carry only the part the range covers.

methods.name: MoveNext
methods.summary: Advances to the next unit; false once the range is spent.

properties.name: Current

types.name: TextUnitExtensions

methods.name: Has

fields.name: None

fields.name: All

fields.name: Grouping
fields.summary: The granularities holding more than one cluster — those a per-glyph effect cannot express.

types.name: TextUnitSequence
types.summary: The units of one stretch of processed text, in logical order. Enumerating allocates nothing and reads the pass's own analysis, so a query costs one walk of the range and no text work.
types.remarks: A snapshot of nothing: the sequence holds the component, not its buffers, and resolves them on [[GetEnumerator]]. Enumerate it inside the frame you obtained it in — a rebuild between the two gives the next enumeration the new text, and a rebuild during one is a programming error the enumerator does not guard against.

methods.name: GetEnumerator

properties.name: Count

types.name: UnicodeData
types.summary: Provides access to Unicode character properties and the global data provider.
types.remarks: Contains common Unicode codepoint constants (whitespace, control characters, BiDi marks) and helper methods for character classification. The static [[Provider]] property gives access to the full Unicode property database for script, line break, and grapheme cluster information.

methods.name: IsMandatoryBreakChar
methods.summary: Returns true if the codepoint is a line or paragraph separator that produces a mandatory break (UAX #14 classes BK, CR, LF, NL) and should not be shaped.

methods.name: StripMandatoryBreaks
methods.summary: Removes every mandatory break character (the [[IsMandatoryBreakChar]] set) from the string, returning the same instance when there is nothing to strip.

methods.name: IsCrlfAt
methods.summary: Whether index holds the carriage return of a CRLF pair — the sequence UAX #14 LB5 and UAX #29 GB3 refuse to break, and which every line-ending rule counts as one terminator rather than two.

methods.name: NormalizeNewlines
methods.summary: Rewrites every CRLF pair and every remaining lone carriage return as a single line feed, returning the same instance when the text holds no carriage return.

methods.name: NormalizeNewlines
methods.summary: Copies source into destination with every CRLF pair and every lone carriage return rewritten as a single line feed, returning the number of chars written. destination must be at least as long as source.

methods.name: IsC0ControlOrDelete
methods.summary: Returns true if the codepoint is a C0 control character (U+0000..U+001F) or DELETE (U+007F).

methods.name: IsJustifiableWordSeparator
methods.summary: Returns true if the codepoint is a word-separator character eligible for stretching under CSS-style inter-word justification (CSS Text Module Level 3 §6.4.1).
methods.remarks: Modelled on Blink/WebKit/Gecko behaviour: includes ASCII space (U+0020), TAB (U+0009, treated as space for justification), the CJK ideographic space (U+3000), and other Unicode general-category Zs space separators. Explicitly excludes the non-breaking variants — NBSP (U+00A0), NARROW NBSP (U+202F), FIGURE SPACE (U+2007) — which carry "do not break / do not stretch" semantics.

methods.name: GetSimpleUppercase
methods.summary: Returns the simple uppercase mapping for a codepoint, falling back to the codepoint itself when no mapping is defined. Backed by UnicodeData.txt so behavior is identical across Mono/IL2CPP/standard.NET — unlike char.ToUpperInvariant, which has gaps for codepoints such as Greek final sigma U+03C2.
methods.remarks: "Simple" means a single-codepoint default mapping that ignores locale and the conditional rules in SpecialCasing.txt (Turkish dotless I, Lithuanian dot-above, German ß → SS, etc.). Use this in custom BaseModifier implementations for predictable case conversion.

methods.name: GetSimpleLowercase
methods.summary: Returns the simple lowercase mapping for a codepoint, falling back to the codepoint itself when no mapping is defined. See [[GetSimpleUppercase]] for the rationale.

methods.name: GetSimpleTitlecase
methods.summary: Returns the simple titlecase mapping for a codepoint, falling back to the codepoint itself when no mapping is defined. Differs from uppercase only for digraph letters such as U+01C5 (ǅ) — uppercase Ǆ, titlecase ǅ, lowercase ǆ.

methods.name: GetGeneralCategory
methods.summary: Returns the Unicode General Category of a codepoint. Useful for filtering codepoints in custom modifiers — apply only to letters (Lu/Ll/Lt/Lm/Lo), skip combining marks (Mn/Mc/Me), select punctuation (Pc/Pd/Ps/Pe/Pi/Pf/Po), and so on.

methods.name: IsLetter
methods.summary: when the codepoint is a Unicode letter (general category L*). Uses the baked category table, so it is consistent across Mono/IL2CPP and covers supplementary letters that char.IsLetter(char) cannot reach.

methods.name: IsWhiteSpace
methods.summary: when the codepoint is whitespace per char.IsWhiteSpace. All Unicode whitespace lies in the BMP, so supplementary codepoints are never whitespace.

methods.name: GetScript
methods.summary: Returns the Unicode Script of a codepoint (UAX #24). Useful for script-conditional modifiers — for example applying a stylistic effect only to Devanagari or only to Han. Values [[Common]] and [[Inherited]] are shared across scripts (punctuation, combining marks).

methods.name: IsExtendedPictographic
methods.summary: Returns when the codepoint has the Extended_Pictographic property (UTS #51). Distinct from emoji presentation: pictographic glyphs that may render either as text or as emoji depending on context.

methods.name: IsEmojiPresentation
methods.summary: Returns when the codepoint defaults to emoji-style presentation (UTS #51 Emoji_Presentation). Use this to skip emoji glyphs in text-only effects (color, gradient, outline) without relying on the live mesh-pass font.IsColor flag.

methods.name: IsEmojiModifierBase
methods.summary: Returns when the codepoint is an emoji that accepts a skin-tone modifier (U+1F3FB..U+1F3FF) immediately after it (UTS #51 Emoji_Modifier_Base).

methods.name: IsDefaultIgnorable
methods.summary: Returns when the codepoint has the Default_Ignorable_Code_Point property (formatting characters, variation selectors, ZWJ/ZWNJ, etc.). Custom modifiers that walk codepoints to compute statistics or apply effects should typically skip these.

methods.name: DecodeAt
methods.summary: Decodes one Unicode scalar and reports the consumed UTF-16 code units; an unpaired surrogate becomes [[ReplacementCharacter]] and consumes one unit.

methods.name: SizeAt
methods.summary: Returns the number of UTF-16 code units occupied at index: two for a valid surrogate pair, otherwise one.

methods.name: MapCharsToCodepoints
methods.summary: Maps ascending UTF-16 char indices to codepoint indices in one text walk. Indices may repeat; out-of-range input clamps to the end. Output may alias the input span.

methods.name: MapCodepointsToChars
methods.summary: Maps ascending codepoint indices to UTF-16 char indices in one text walk. Indices may repeat; past-the-end input clamps to text.Length. Output may alias the input span.

methods.name: EncodeUtf16
methods.summary: Encodes a Unicode scalar into UTF-16: one code unit in high for BMP codepoints (low is 0), a surrogate pair otherwise. Returns the number of code units written (1 or 2).

methods.name: EncodeUtf16
methods.summary: Encodes a Unicode scalar as UTF-16 into dst starting at at: one char for BMP codepoints, a surrogate pair otherwise. Returns the number of chars written (1 or 2).

methods.name: EnsureInitialized
methods.summary: Initializes the required Unicode tables or throws when their project data is unavailable or invalid.

properties.name: IsInitialized
properties.summary: Returns whether the required Unicode tables have been initialized.

fields.name: ObjectReplacementCharacterString
fields.summary: String form of [[ObjectReplacementCharacter]] for insertion APIs.

types.name: UniTextBuffers
types.summary: Container for all intermediate and final buffers used during text processing.
types.remarks: [[UniTextBuffers]] holds all data produced during the text processing pipeline: codepoints, BiDi levels, text runs, shaped glyphs, line breaks, and positioned glyphs. Performance: All buffers use [[PooledBuffer{T}]] for zero-allocation operation in steady state. Call [[EnsureRentBuffers]] before processing and [[EnsureReturnBuffers]] when done.

methods.name: IsRtlLevelAt
methods.summary: Whether the codepoint's resolved BiDi embedding level (UAX #9) is RTL — odd level. False when levels are absent or the index is out of range; the one home of the parity convention.

methods.name: RequestVirtualCodepoint
methods.summary: Requests atlas warm-up for a codepoint rendered outside the document text (decoration-line _, list bullets, ellipsis). The glyph is prepared in every font the text resolves to, so an injected character can be drawn in the face of the text around it, plus the font stack's own choice for it. Deduplicated — the buffer is shared across modifiers and survives granular re-applies, so a per-range or per-frame caller must not append the same codepoint unboundedly.

methods.name: RequestVirtualGlyph
methods.summary: Requests atlas warm-up for an exact glyph in a registered font. Deduplicated because the shared buffer survives granular modifier re-applies; a repeated request keeps the larger silhouette-field reach (fieldExtent, see [[ColorGlyphField]]).

methods.name: TryResolveInjectedGlyph
methods.summary: Resolves a character drawn outside the document text against the face the text at cluster resolved to, so a bold, italic, overridden or variable face carries into the injected glyph; falls back to the font stack when that face lacks the character. Declare the character through [[RequestVirtualCodepoint]] in any phase before glyph rasterization, or the resolved glyph has no atlas entry to draw from.
methods.returns: when no font carries the character.

params.description: The provider that issued the text's font ids.

params.name: fontSize

methods.name: FontIdForCluster
methods.summary: The font id the text at cluster resolved to, or 0 outside every shaped run.

methods.name: ActivateChannel
methods.summary: Registers holder as an active writer of key and returns the channel owning that key's pipeline passes, creating it from factory on the first writer. Returns when the key carries no pass.

params.name: holder

params.name: owner

params.name: factory

methods.name: GetOrCreateAttributeData
methods.summary: Gets or creates typed attribute data for the specified key, incrementing its reference count. The matching [[ReleaseAttributeData]] call decrements; the underlying data is freed only when the count reaches zero. This lets multiple modifier instances safely share one keyed channel — destroying one no longer pulls the buffer out from under the rest.
methods.returns: The existing or newly created attribute data instance.

params.name: key
params.description: The unique key identifying this attribute data.

typeParameters.name: T
typeParameters.description: The attribute data type, must implement [[IAttributeData]].

methods.name: PrepareAttribute
methods.summary: Registers this modifier's keyed attribute and sizes it to the codepoint count. Sizing runs on registration only; from there on [[PrepareAttributes]] owns it, once per parse.

methods.name: AddFontFeatures
methods.summary: Merges an OpenType feature set into every codepoint of a range, so shaping applies it there. Features already written to a codepoint are kept, and a tag both sets carry takes featureSet's value. [[Unset]] writes nothing.

params.name: range
params.description: The codepoint range the set applies to.

params.name: featureSet
params.description: A [[FontFeatureRegistry]] id.

exceptions.description: The range does not fit the current text.

methods.name: PrepareAttributes
methods.summary: Sizes every registered attribute to the current codepoint count and clears it. Runs once per parse, after decoding and before any modifier applies: an attribute owned by a modifier that did not re-initialize this parse is still indexed by the codepoints of the current text.

methods.name: GetAttributeData
methods.summary: Gets typed attribute data for the specified key if it exists.
methods.returns: The attribute data if found; otherwise,.

params.name: key

methods.name: ReleaseAttributeData
methods.summary: Decrements the reference count for key's attribute data and releases the underlying buffer only when the count drops to zero. Pairs one-to-one with [[GetOrCreateAttributeData{T}]].

params.name: key
params.description: The unique key identifying the attribute data to release.

methods.name: GetGlyphScale
methods.summary: Gets the scale factor to convert from shaping font size to target font size.
methods.returns: The scale factor to apply to glyph positions and advances.

params.name: targetFontSize
params.description: The desired font size.

methods.name: EnsureRentBuffers
methods.summary: Ensures all buffers are rented from the pool with appropriate initial capacity.
methods.remarks: Call this method before starting text processing. If buffers are already rented, this method returns immediately. Performance: Capacities are estimated from text length and rounded to power-of-two values for efficient pooling.

params.name: textLength
params.description: The expected text length for capacity estimation.

methods.name: EnsureReturnBuffers
methods.summary: Returns all rented buffers back to the pool.
methods.remarks: Call this method when text processing is complete and the buffers are no longer needed. This releases memory back to the pool for reuse by other instances.

methods.name: Reset
methods.summary: Resets all buffer counts to zero without releasing pooled memory.
methods.remarks: Use this method between processing passes to reuse buffers for new text without the overhead of returning and re-renting from the pool.

methods.name: EnsureCodepointCapacity
methods.summary: Ensures codepoint-related buffers have at least the specified capacity.

params.name: required
params.description: The minimum required codepoint capacity.

methods.name: PrepareStartMargins
methods.summary: Lazily allocates [[startMargins]] to fit the current codepoint count and zero-initializes any region not yet prepared in this pass.
methods.remarks: Call this from modifiers before writing start margins (e.g., for list indentation). Idempotent within a pass — subsequent calls with the same codepoint count are no-ops.

properties.name: GraphemeBreaksOrEmpty

properties.name: WordBoundariesOrEmpty
properties.summary: [[wordBoundaries]] as a span, or empty until the pipeline has produced them.

properties.name: HasLineAdvances
properties.summary: Whether every line carries the advance and prefix a Y coordinate is resolved against. False between a line break and the layout that follows it, when a caller must fall back to the metrics it can measure itself rather than read the fields.

fields.name: codepoints
fields.summary: Parsed Unicode scalar values; unpaired UTF-16 surrogates become [[ReplacementCharacter]].

fields.name: runs
fields.summary: Pre-shaping runs (segmented by script, direction, font) — per-pass scratch of the paragraphs that actually re-shaped; cache-hit paragraphs contribute none. Read only by shaping; consume [[shapedRuns]] for whole-text run data.

fields.name: shapedRuns
fields.summary: Shaped runs with glyph ranges and metrics.

fields.name: shapedGlyphs
fields.summary: Shaped glyphs with glyph IDs, advances, and offsets.

fields.name: cpWidths
fields.summary: Width of each codepoint for line breaking calculations.

fields.name: breakOpportunities
fields.summary: Line break types per codepoint (UAX #14).

fields.name: graphemeBreaks
fields.summary: Grapheme cluster boundaries per codepoint (UAX #29).

fields.name: wordBoundaries
fields.summary: Word boundaries per codepoint position (UAX #29 plus dictionary tailoring).

fields.name: lines
fields.summary: Computed text lines after line breaking.

fields.name: orderedRuns
fields.summary: Runs reordered for visual display within each line.

fields.name: positionedGlyphs
fields.summary: Final positioned glyphs ready for rendering.

fields.name: segmentBreaks
fields.summary: Segment-level line break opportunities in codepoint space; filled by modifiers in the Shaped phase, consumed by line breaking. Text between consecutive entries wraps as a unit: it either fits entirely on the current line or starts a fresh one, and the entry's range — the delimiter — collapses when the break is taken on it (its codepoints stay in the line range but produce no glyphs and no width), the way trailing whitespace hangs at word-level breaks. A unit wider than the box wraps inside itself, and its lines accept no further units. A zero-length entry is a pure boundary with nothing to collapse.

fields.name: virtualCodepoints
fields.summary: Virtual codepoints for synthesized glyphs (e.g., modifiers).

fields.name: virtualGlyphs
fields.summary: Pre-shaped glyph ids (with font) modifiers request for atlas rasterization when the id comes from OpenType shaping (GSUB), not a 1:1 codepoint lookup.

fields.name: virtualPositionedGlyphs
fields.summary: Virtual positioned glyphs injected by modifiers (ellipsis, list markers). Separate from positionedGlyphs to not affect hit testing / selection.

fields.name: bidiLevels
fields.summary: BiDi embedding levels per codepoint (UAX #9).

fields.name: scripts
fields.summary: Unicode script per codepoint (UAX #24).

fields.name: startMargins
fields.summary: Start margins per codepoint (for list items, indentation).

fields.name: baseDirection
fields.summary: The resolved base paragraph direction.

fields.name: shapingFontSize
fields.summary: Font size used during shaping (for scaling calculations).

fields.name: hasValidGlyphCache
fields.summary: Indicates whether [[glyphDataCache]] contains valid data.

fields.name: isRented
fields.summary: Indicates whether buffers are currently rented from the pool.

types.name: UniTextMeshGenerator
types.summary: Converts positioned glyphs into Unity mesh data for text rendering.
types.remarks: This is the final stage of the text processing pipeline. It takes [[PositionedGlyph]] data from [[TextProcessor]] and generates vertex, UV, color, and triangle data suitable for Unity's mesh system. Key features: Groups glyphs by rendering target to minimize draw calls: one segment per font (Texture2DArray atlas) Uses pooled buffers from [[ArrayPool{T}]] for zero allocations Provides callbacks for text modifiers to inject custom processing Typical usage: generator.SetRectOffset(rect); generator.GenerateMeshDataOnly(positionedGlyphs); var renderData = generator.CollectRenderData(); // Use renderData to render each segment generator.ReturnInstanceBuffers();

methods.name: FaceGlyphH
methods.summary: Height in em of the field a face quad samples: the glyph's for an outline face, the silhouette's for a colour face with a field, 0 for a colour face without one.

methods.name: TrackGlyphKey
methods.summary: Tracks a glyph key for atlas ref counting. Deduplicates automatically. Use for modifier glyphs that don't need cached entry data.

methods.name: UniTextMeshGenerator
methods.summary: Initializes a new instance of the [[UniTextMeshGenerator]] class.

params.name: fontProvider
params.description: The font provider for accessing font assets and materials.

params.name: uniTextBuffers
params.description: The shared buffer container from text processing.

exceptions.description: Thrown when fontProvider or uniTextBuffers is.

methods.name: ScaleGlyphQuad
methods.summary: Scales a glyph quad (4 vertices) around the cursor position and baseline. Used by SizeModifier, SmallCapsModifier, ScriptPositionModifier.

params.name: pivotX
params.description: Cursor position (pen X) — bearing and width scale proportionally from this pivot.

methods.name: ScaleFace
methods.summary: Scales the current face quad and records the factor into [[currentGlyphScale]]. Every per-glyph size change (size tag, small-caps, sub/superscript, ruby, font metric overrides) must pass through here rather than [[ScaleGlyphQuad]] directly — a scale the generator does not see leaves paint-layer offset and quad growth stuck at the base size.

methods.name: XScaleFace
methods.summary: Scales a face quad horizontally around the pen position — the fit / justification glyph-compression channel. Deliberately not folded into [[currentGlyphScale]]: paint-layer growth stays isotropic while the rendered glyph narrows.

methods.name: EnsureUvBuffer
methods.summary: Allocates and zero-clears a UV effect buffer (channel 2 or 3) if not already allocated.

params.name: channel
params.description: UV channel: 2 or 3.

methods.name: GlyphScale
methods.summary: Per-glyph scale for the face quad starting at baseIdx (1 when the glyph was never scaled). Read by paint layers at emit time.

methods.name: ReturnInstanceBuffers
methods.summary: Returns all instance buffers to the pool and clears the generated data flag.
methods.remarks: Must be called after mesh generation is complete and data has been applied to Unity meshes. Failing to call this method will result in buffer leaks.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases all pooled resources. Call when the generator is no longer needed.

methods.name: EnsureCapacity
methods.summary: Ensures the vertex and triangle buffers have capacity for additional data.
methods.remarks: Called by text modifiers when they need to add geometry beyond the base glyph quads. Automatically grows buffers using the pooled array system if needed.

params.name: additionalVertices
params.description: Number of additional vertices needed.

params.name: additionalTriangles
params.description: Number of additional triangle indices needed.

methods.name: ResetPerGlyphState
methods.summary: Resets the per-glyph state that [[onGlyph]] modifiers read and write — the claim race ([[fillClaimedThisGlyph]]/[[baseFaceClaimed]]), the claimed [[claimedFillSequence]]/[[claimedFillBlend]], and the tier-upgrade [[currentMaxGlyphExtent]]. Every emitter of a glyph quad (face, kashida, decoration line) calls this before firing onGlyph.

methods.name: AddSdfQuad
methods.summary: Records a quad (4 vertices at baseVertexIdx) of the current segment (SDF or color) to be drawn at layer sequence with blend. Triangles are written in sequence order by [[MaterializeQuadTriangles]], so painter order follows the layer stack; glyph-major ranges ([[paintOrders]]) group a glyph's quads together first, ordering layers within each glyph. The quad's owning cluster is read from its UV1 z channel (see [[Uvs1]]), which duplicate reservation copies from the source face.

methods.name: RequestTierUpgradeIfNeeded
methods.summary: Raises the current glyph's atlas pad tier when a modifier asked for more outward rim than the tier reserves — the glyph is re-rasterized smaller in its shared tile so the extra distance field (outline / shadow / bold) has room, plus [[TierSeamMarginNorm]] of AA-ramp headroom so the effect's outer edge samples inside computed field, not at the tile seam. Only the request is recorded here; the sweep re-rasterizes the tile and re-meshes every consumer of it at the new tier in the same frame (see UniTextBase_Parallel). Grow-only.
methods.remarks: Call immediately after [[onGlyph]]. The required rim is the face dilate (bold, from [[Uvs1]][[[faceBaseIdx]]].y) plus [[currentMaxGlyphExtent]] (the effects' outward extent) — so bold and effects stack regardless of modifier order.

methods.name: RequestTileSizeUpgradeIfNeeded
methods.summary: Records a grow-only atlas tile-size upgrade for the current glyph when a resolution modifier asked for more detail / a larger tile than the font default. The sweep relocates the shared tile to the larger class and re-meshes its consumers the same frame (see UniTextBase_Parallel). The glyph's atlas key ignores tile size, so all consumers share one tile at the max requested resolution. Call immediately after [[onGlyph]].

methods.name: ExpandQuad
methods.summary: Expands a 4-vertex quad outward along its current local axes: UV0 by delta (atlas-space, normalized by glyph height), positions by the matching distance in the quad's own UV0→pixel scale, so the SDF sample stays attached to the geometry whatever size the quad was built or scaled to.

methods.name: SetRectOffset
methods.summary: Sets the layout rectangle for text positioning.

params.name: rect
params.description: The rect defining the text layout bounds.

methods.name: SetVisibleBand
methods.summary: Bounds quad emission to a local-space vertical band (viewport culling). Geometry queries, selection and hit-testing are untouched — positioned glyphs exist for every paragraph; only mesh emission skips bands outside the window. Reset to infinite for no culling.

methods.name: IsLocalBandVisible
methods.summary: True when a local-space vertical span intersects the visible band — the one culling test every emission site shares (glyph paragraphs, virtual glyphs, decoration lines).

methods.name: GenerateMeshDataOnly
methods.summary: Generates mesh data (vertices, UVs, colors, triangles) from positioned glyphs. Groups by rendering target: SDF fonts in one segment (Texture2DArray), color separately.

methods.name: CollectRenderData
methods.summary: Collects raw render data (vertex/UV/triangle array slices + material/order metadata) for every segment produced by the latest mesh generation. Does not build Unity [[Mesh]] objects — consumers (canvas UpdateSubMeshes, world batcher) decide what to do with the raw data.
methods.remarks: Text and color quads live in the same pooled buffers ([[Vertices]], [[Uvs0]], [[Colors]], [[Triangles]]) as contiguous ranges: text faces first, colour faces next, then the effect and decoration quads appended at main-pass finalization. Each entry carries vertexOffset/vertexCount bounding only the vertices its triangles reference (a tight span, not the whole segment), with triangle indices relative to that span — consumers read exactly the slice, so interleaved layer runs do not duplicate the segment's vertex data per run. Array references remain valid only until the next [[GenerateMeshDataOnly]] / [[CollectRenderData]] cycle on the same generator (pooled buffers may be regrown or returned). Consumers must not retain references across frames.
methods.returns: Shared list of [[UniTextRenderData]] entries — the base segment's layer runs (text and color quads share one segment; the per-glyph mode in UV1.w picks the sampler) plus any sub-meshes appended by [[onCollectSubMeshes]] subscribers. The list is reused on the next call; consumers must use/copy immediately.

properties.name: HasColorFaceField
properties.summary: Whether the colour glyph currently in [[onGlyph]] carries a silhouette field for effects to sample; always false for an outline glyph.

properties.name: onMainPassComplete
properties.summary: Runs after every face quad — text and colour glyphs alike — and before main-pass finalization.

properties.name: onMainPassFinalize
properties.summary: Runs after [[onMainPassComplete]], with every face quad emitted, before triangle materialization.

properties.name: onGlyph
properties.summary: Runs for each glyph during mesh generation.

properties.name: onRebuildEnd
properties.summary: Runs after all mesh generation is complete.

properties.name: onRebuildStart
properties.summary: Runs before mesh generation starts.

properties.name: onCollectSubMeshes
properties.summary: Collects custom render-data segments before the base segments are appended.

properties.name: FontSize
properties.summary: Gets or sets the font size in points for mesh generation.

properties.name: RenderMode
properties.summary: Gets or sets the atlas mode (SDF or MSDF) for glyph lookup and material selection.

properties.name: HasGeneratedData
properties.summary: Gets a value indicating whether mesh data has been generated and is available.

properties.name: Vertices
properties.summary: Gets the vertex position buffer (X, Y, Z coordinates).

properties.name: Uvs0
properties.summary: Gets the primary UV buffer (texture coordinates and scale in W component).

properties.name: Colors
properties.summary: Gets the vertex color buffer.

properties.name: Triangles
properties.summary: Gets the triangle index buffer.

properties.name: Uvs1
properties.summary: Gets the UV1 buffer: x = aspect (glyphW/glyphH), y = faceDilate, z = per-glyph cluster index (monotonic per-line, transform-invariant), w = intra-glyph X fraction (0 on the left edge, 1 on the right — interpolated by GPU).

properties.name: Uvs2
properties.summary: Gets the UV2 buffer — the COVERAGE contract (TEXCOORD2).
properties.remarks: Layout (must match UniText_Coverage.hlsl, written by [[CoverageQuadOps]]): x = coverage mode + 16·cornerCode (see [[WithCorner]]), y = p0 (width/offset), z = p1 (mode-specific), w = softness. Unallocated reads as 0 → Fill + legacy field, so plain text pays nothing. Effect colour lives in the standard vertex [[Colors]] attribute with alpha pre-multiplied by the source face vertex alpha; offsets are applied via mesh vertex displacement, not UV. Not allocated by default — call [[EnsureUvBuffer]] before writing. Custom effects must not repurpose this channel on painted text.

properties.name: Uvs3
properties.summary: Gets the UV3 buffer — the PAINT contract (TEXCOORD3).
properties.remarks: Layout (must match the paint decode in the shader family, written by [[CoverageQuadOps]]): xy = paint coordinate in the mapping frame, z = gradient ramp row, w = paint kind code (0 solid, 1..3 gradient shapes, 4/5 texture). On a quad whose colour is sampled from a texture the CPU cannot recolour — a texture paint or a colour glyph — z instead carries a [[ColorMatrixAtlas]] row + 1 (≤ 0 = unfiltered). Unallocated reads as 0 → solid. Not allocated by default — call [[EnsureUvBuffer]] before writing. Custom effects must not repurpose this channel on painted text.

fields.name: DefaultSdfPadding
fields.summary: Base UV-space padding (normalized by glyph height) allocated around every face quad. Face and effect modifiers that expand the quad must subtract this baseline from their requested extent when computing the expansion delta.

fields.name: GlyphGeometryConsumerOrder
fields.summary: Order for callbacks that consume the completed glyph quad to derive additional geometry.

fields.name: currentCluster
fields.summary: The cluster index of the glyph currently being processed.

fields.name: currentGlyphId
fields.summary: Font glyph id of the glyph currently being processed — identifies which glyph a quad renders when the cluster alone is ambiguous (virtual glyphs).

fields.name: height
fields.summary: Height of the current glyph including padding.

fields.name: baselineY
fields.summary: Y coordinate of the text baseline for the current glyph.

fields.name: cursorX
fields.summary: X coordinate of the cursor position (pen position) for the current glyph.

fields.name: scale
fields.summary: Design-units → pixels for the current glyph's font.

fields.name: fontMetricFactor
fields.summary: FontSize * FontScale — converts normalized glyph metrics to UI-space units. Constant per font.

fields.name: defaultColor
fields.summary: Default vertex color applied to all glyphs.

fields.name: font
fields.summary: Current font being processed.

fields.name: offsetX
fields.summary: X offset from the rect origin.

fields.name: offsetY
fields.summary: Y offset from the rect origin.

fields.name: vertexCount
fields.summary: Current number of vertices in the mesh buffers.

fields.name: triangleCount
fields.summary: Current number of triangle indices in the mesh buffers.

fields.name: faceBaseIdx
fields.summary: Index of the first vertex of the face quad of the glyph currently being processed. Stable across all [[onGlyph]] invocations for a single glyph, even when modifiers append additional geometry that grows [[vertexCount]].

fields.name: DefaultFillSequence
fields.summary: Sequence assigned to a glyph face when no explicit fill claimed it — below every layer (default fill = bottom of the stack).

fields.name: claimedFillSequence
fields.summary: Set during [[onGlyph]] by the fill that claims the current glyph's base quad, to its [[LayerSequence]]; left at [[DefaultFillSequence]] when none does. The face quad is ordered at this sequence, so an explicit fill stacks the glyph at its layer position.

fields.name: claimedFillBlend
fields.summary: Blend mode paired with [[claimedFillSequence]] for the current glyph face.

fields.name: sequenceBias
fields.summary: Added to every layer sequence a modifier captures while it is set, lifting a whole stack — face, stroke, shadow, glow — into a higher band together instead of leaving each layer at its own style-stack position. Zero for shaped text; a virtual-glyph emitter raises it around its own emission and restores it afterwards. A layer folds it in where it captures the sequence, during [[onGlyph]] — never where it flushes, by which time the emitter has restored it.

fields.name: currentMaxGlyphExtent
fields.summary: Maximum UV-space padding requested for the current glyph by any modifier. Reset to 0 before each [[onGlyph]] invocation. Subscribers accumulate via max. Read after [[onGlyph]] to decide atlas tier upgrades.

fields.name: currentTileSizeBoost
fields.summary: Largest resolution boost (0–2 tile-size classes above the glyph's default) a resolution modifier requested for the current glyph. Reset to 0 before each [[onGlyph]]; accumulated via max, read after to request a grow-only atlas tile-size upgrade. See [[RequestTileSizeUpgradeIfNeeded]].

fields.name: currentGlyphScale
fields.summary: Product of every per-glyph scale applied to the current face quad (size, small-caps, sub/superscript, ruby, font metric overrides) via [[ScaleFace]]. Reset to 1 before each [[onGlyph]]; [[GlyphScale]] reads it back per quad once the glyph completes. Em → pixels for an emitted quad is [[fontMetricFactor]] times this: em geometry multiplies by it and absolute (px) geometry divides by it, so a px value keeps a constant on-screen size while the glyph scales.

fields.name: fillClaimedThisGlyph
fields.summary: Reset to before each [[onGlyph]]; a fill layer sets it when it claims (recolours) the glyph's base quad, so later fills on the same glyph stack as duplicates instead of fighting over the base.

fields.name: baseFaceClaimed
fields.summary: Set when a layer takes over rendering the current glyph's base face in its own sub-mesh — a texture fill, or a [[MaterialModifier]] in Replace mode. The base-mesh face quad must then not be recorded (it would sit at the claimed sequence as a transparent placeholder and stop the base mesh from slicing there, breaking layer order). Reset before each [[onGlyph]].

fields.name: suppressInheritedFill
fields.summary: Set by a virtual-glyph emitter (decoration line with its own paint) around its [[onGlyph]] so the inherited text fill stands down entirely — neither claiming the base nor stacking a duplicate over it. Unlike [[fillClaimedThisGlyph]] (which only loses the base race and still overlays), this fully suppresses base fills, letting the line's own paint replace the inherited one (CSS text-decoration-color). Non-base layers (shadow, glow, stroke) are unaffected and still decorate the line.

fields.name: isVirtualGlyph
fields.summary: True when the currently processed glyph is virtual (injected by a modifier — list marker, ellipsis dot — and has no [[ShapedGlyph]] behind it).

fields.name: currentPositionedIndex
fields.summary: Index into the positioned-glyph array of the glyph the current quad renders, or -1 when no positioned glyph stands behind it.

types.name: UniTextObjects
types.summary: ScriptableObject containing named inline objects (UI prefabs) for use with <obj=name> tags.
types.remarks: Create via Assets → Create → UniText → Objects. Reference from an [[AssetObjProvider]] on an [[ObjModifier]] to share a catalog of inline prefabs across multiple components.

types.name: UniTextRenderData
types.summary: Raw geometry slice describing a single text/color/sub-mesh render segment.
types.remarks: Holds references to pooled vertex/UV/color/index arrays plus offset+count into them. The consumer (canvas: [[UpdateSubMeshes]]; world: [[UniTextWorldBatcher]]) does whatever it needs with this data — either uploads into a reusable [[Mesh]] for CanvasRenderer, or copies into its combined-mesh buffers for world-space batching. Array references are valid only until the next collect cycle on the same generator — pooled buffers can be returned or regrown. Consumers must read/copy immediately and not retain references across frames.

fields.name: fontId
fields.summary: The font identifier this render data belongs to.

fields.name: materialOverride
fields.summary: Optional custom material. When, the renderer uses the default SDF/MSDF or color material for this [[fontId]].

fields.name: atlasOverride
fields.summary: Optional atlas binding for [[materialOverride]]. When, the custom material keeps its own texture and does not follow atlas replacements.

fields.name: sequence
fields.summary: The single draw-order axis — the emitting layer's [[LayerSequence]] (style-stack position). Every segment (base SDF runs, color, paint-layer sub-meshes, inline media, custom materials) sorts by this, so stacking follows the order layers appear in Styles. The base text / default fill sits at [[DefaultFillSequence]] (bottom).

fields.name: sortIndex
fields.summary: Stable sort key within the same [[sequence]] (lower renders first).

fields.name: blend
fields.summary: How this draw composites its premultiplied output with the rendered backdrop.

fields.name: vertices
fields.summary: Vertex positions array (pooled). Read [vertexOffset, vertexOffset+vertexCount).

fields.name: uvs0
fields.summary: UV0 array (pooled). Must always be valid when [[vertexCount]] > 0.

fields.name: uvs1
fields.summary: UV1 array (pooled). or ignored when [[hasUv1]] is false.

fields.name: uvs2
fields.summary: UV2 array (pooled). or ignored when [[hasUv2]] is false.

fields.name: uvs3
fields.summary: UV3 array (pooled). or ignored when [[hasUv3]] is false.

fields.name: colors
fields.summary: Vertex colors array (pooled).

fields.name: triangles
fields.summary: Triangle indices array (pooled). Indices are relative to [[vertexOffset]] — they index into this segment's vertex slice, not into the whole [[vertices]] array. Read [triangleOffset, triangleOffset+triangleCount).

fields.name: vertexOffset
fields.summary: Start index in [[vertices]]/[[uvs0]]/[[colors]] etc.

fields.name: vertexCount
fields.summary: Number of vertices in this segment (starting at [[vertexOffset]]).

fields.name: triangleOffset
fields.summary: Start index in [[triangles]].

fields.name: triangleCount
fields.summary: Number of triangle indices in this segment.

fields.name: hasUv1
fields.summary: When, [[uvs1]] is valid and should be uploaded.

fields.name: hasUv2
fields.summary: When, [[uvs2]] is valid and should be uploaded.

fields.name: hasUv3
fields.summary: When, [[uvs3]] is valid and should be uploaded.

types.name: UniTextSettings
types.summary: Global settings ScriptableObject for UniText configuration.
types.remarks: Access via Edit → Project Settings → UniText. Contains editor-only default configurations for new UniText components.

methods.name: Affects
methods.summary: Returns when a [[Changed]] payload identifies interestedMember or represents complete instance replacement.

methods.name: SetInstance
methods.summary: Manually replaces the singleton settings asset (used by tests and custom initialization paths). Raises [[Changed]] with [[Reset]] because every reactive member may differ.

params.name: settings
params.description: The settings instance to use.

properties.name: Paints
properties.summary: Gets or sets the project-wide named paint swatch catalog.

properties.name: GlobalStylePreset
properties.summary: Project-wide [[StylePreset]] applied to every [[UniTextBase]] component without per-component opt-in. Behaves as one extra entry appended after each component's local StylePresets list, so local Styles and per-component StylePresets register first and win parse-rule conflicts.
properties.remarks: Assigning fires [[Changed]] with [[GlobalStylePreset]]; subscribed components reconcile their runtime style bindings through that same state transition. Editing the preset's styles list at runtime (via the preset's own [[Styles]]) is delivered through the asset's own [[Changed]] event, picked up by every component that has it subscribed (local StylePresets entry or this global slot).

properties.name: SystemFont
properties.summary: Project-wide system font. Serves two roles, both via [[Default]]: the always-on final fallback that fills coverage gaps after the assigned fonts, and the primary for components with no Font and no Font Stack. When null, the OS default sans-serif fills both.

properties.name: SystemFontDisabled
properties.summary: Persisted mirror of [[Disabled]]. The setter pushes the value to the runtime flag; the saved value is pushed back on editor load (static constructor).

properties.name: EmojiDisabled
properties.summary: Persisted mirror of [[Disabled]]. The setter pushes the value to the runtime flag; the saved value is pushed back on editor load (static constructor).

properties.name: Instance
properties.summary: Gets the singleton settings instance, loading from Resources if needed.

properties.name: Dictionaries
properties.summary: Gets the configured word segmentation dictionaries.

properties.name: WorldBatcherShardTargetVertexCount
properties.summary: Target vertex capacity per shard mesh in the world-space batcher. A component's segments always share one shard, so this bounds how much unrelated text one structural rebuild re-bakes; a single component larger than the budget inflates its own shard instead of splitting.

properties.name: CaretBlinkTimeout
properties.summary: Seconds of inactivity before the caret stops blinking. Reads [[InstanceSilent]] — polled from the caret update loop, where a missing settings asset must degrade without per-tick error logs.

properties.name: CaretBlinkInterval
properties.summary: Caret blink half-period in seconds. Reads [[InstanceSilent]] (see [[CaretBlinkTimeout]]).

properties.name: Language
properties.summary: Gets or sets the project-wide BCP 47 language tag. Applied to any codepoint that has no component-level UniText.Language and no per-range <lang> override.

properties.name: DefaultLineHeightMode
properties.summary: Project-wide default line-height mode applied to every component without a per-range override. Mirrored to [[DefaultLineHeightMode]].

properties.name: LineHeightScale
properties.summary: Line height as a multiple of font size when [[DefaultLineHeightMode]] is [[Scaled]]. Mirrored to [[DefaultLineHeightScale]].

properties.name: FontNormalizeMetric
properties.summary: Project-wide default font normalization metric (CSS font-size-adjust), applied to each component's font provider on init. [[None]] matches platform defaults.

properties.name: FontNormalizeTarget
properties.summary: Target aspect for [[FontNormalizeMetric]] (metric ÷ font size); 0 matches the primary font.

events.name: Changed
events.summary: Occurs when a settings member has been mutated. The payload carries its generated [[StateMember]], allowing subscribers to select their own exact reaction. [[Reset]] means the settings instance itself was replaced. Serialized editor changes are reconciled through the same generated transitions as runtime properties.

types.name: UniTextSprites
types.summary: ScriptableObject containing named inline sprites for use with <sprite=name> tags.
types.remarks: Create via Assets → Create → UniText → Sprites. Reference from an [[AssetSpriteProvider]] on a [[SpriteModifier]] to share a catalog across multiple components without prefabbing each icon.

types.name: VerticalAlignment
types.summary: Specifies vertical text alignment within the layout bounds.

fields.name: Top
fields.summary: Align text to the top edge.

fields.name: Middle
fields.summary: Center text vertically.

fields.name: Bottom
fields.summary: Align text to the bottom edge.

types.name: VirtualGlyph
types.summary: A pre-shaped glyph a modifier hands to the rasterizer when its glyph id comes from OpenType shaping (GSUB) rather than a 1:1 codepoint lookup — e.g. shaped ruby, where Arabic joining forms and ligatures differ from the cmap glyph. Registered for atlas rasterization alongside virtual codepoints.

fields.name: fontId
fields.summary: Font the glyph id belongs to.

fields.name: glyphId
fields.summary: Shaped glyph id to rasterize.

fields.name: fieldExtent
fields.summary: Silhouette-field request for a colour glyph (see [[ColorGlyphField]]); 0 asks for the bitmap alone.

types.name: AnyMarkup
types.summary: Targets every visible markup tag, regardless of rule or modifier. Lowest specificity — the fallback.

types.name: BackslashEscapeRule
types.summary: Escapes a single ASCII punctuation character preceded by \. Example: \* becomes a literal * and is protected from any other parse rule.
types.remarks: Standalone rule — register via [[AddRule]] without a modifier. The escapable set follows CommonMark §2.4 — all ASCII punctuation: !"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\]^_`{|}~ Only isolated occurrences are protected. A paired inline matcher (e.g. **bold**) that started scanning before an inner \* will not respect the escape — that case requires matchers themselves to skip escaped characters when seeking their closing marker.
attributes: TypeDescription("Escapes a single character after '\\' (e.g. \\* becomes a literal *).")

types.name: ByModifier
types.summary: Targets markup whose modifier is of a chosen type.

properties.name: Modifier
properties.summary: Modifier signature matched by this selector.

types.name: ByRule
types.summary: Targets markup parsed by a rule with a given [[Identity]] (case-insensitive) — tag:b, marker:**, or a singleton's full type name. The most specific selector.
attributes: TypeDescription("Markup of a given rule (by Identity)")

properties.name: Identity
properties.summary: Case-insensitive parse-rule identity matched by this selector.

types.name: ChromeRule
types.summary: One styling rule for visible markup tag characters: a [[Selector]] choosing which markup it targets and the [[Style]] modifier (plus its [[Parameter]]) painted onto those tags. The tag characters are protected from the enclosing document style so only this styling shows. Across a list, rules with different modifier kinds compose; same-kind rules resolve by selector specificity, ties to the first listed.

properties.name: Selector
properties.summary: Markup selector determining which visible tag characters are targeted.

properties.name: Style
properties.summary: Modifier applied to matching visible tag characters.

properties.name: Parameter
properties.summary: Default parameter passed to the chrome modifier.

types.name: CodeSpanRule
types.summary: Protects content inside backtick-delimited code spans (e.g. `x`, ``x``, ```x```) from being processed by other parse rules. Follows CommonMark §6.1 balanced-run semantics: an N-backtick run is closed by the next N-backtick run of the same length.
types.remarks: Standalone rule — register via [[AddRule]] without a modifier. If no matching closing run is found, the rule does not consume the input (the backticks are treated as literal text). This matches CommonMark's non-forgiving close behavior.
attributes: TypeDescription("Prevents parse rules from matching inside `code spans` (balanced backtick runs).")

types.name: CompositeParseRule
types.summary: Combines multiple parse rules into a single rule.
types.remarks: Tries each child rule in order until one matches. Useful for grouping related rules or creating reusable rule sets.
attributes: TypeDescription("Combines multiple parse rules into one.")

methods.name: FindLeaf
methods.summary: The syntax-family lookup mirroring [[FindLeaf]]: returns root itself, or the first composite child (depth-first), of type T; null when none. Syntax-specific consumers address the family through here so composites are never invisible.

methods.name: Apply
methods.summary: Delegates to the first child with a wrapping form, so a composite that merges differently-typed rules (a tag with a marker) stays inline-applicable in the first listed child's syntax.

properties.name: Identity
properties.summary: The children carry the syntax identities; the composite itself has none.

properties.name: EscapePrefix
properties.summary: First child's escape prefix — the composite carries its children's escaping capability.

properties.name: CanWrap
properties.summary: Wrappable when any child is — mirrors [[Apply]]'s first-wrapping-child delegation.

properties.name: Priority
properties.summary: Highest child priority (including negative — a composite of auto-detection rules must not be promoted to explicit-markup priority 0), so longest-match ordering tries the composite as early as its strongest child. Without it the default 0 lets a shorter standalone marker (a * rule) preempt a composite that wraps a longer one (**), splitting the longer marker into the shorter.

types.name: Entry
types.summary: One authored range expression and its positional modifier parameters.

methods.name: Entry
methods.summary: Creates an authored range entry.

properties.name: Range
properties.summary: C#-style codepoint range expression such as 0..5 or ^10...

properties.name: Parameter
properties.summary: Explicit positional parameter layer forwarded to the modifier graph.

types.name: FixedRangeSource
types.summary: Serialized source for a small authored set of codepoint ranges. Runtime-generated or frequently changing sets belong in [[MutableRangeSource]].
attributes: TypeDescription("Applies the modifier to authored codepoint ranges without parsing markup.")

methods.name: FixedRangeSource
methods.summary: Creates an empty authored source.

methods.name: FixedRangeSource
methods.summary: Creates one fixed codepoint range with an exclusive end.

properties.name: Identity
properties.summary: Uses instance identity because two authored lists are independent sources.

properties.name: IsWholeText
properties.summary: Whether this source contains one entry covering the entire text.

types.name: IMarkupSelector
types.summary: Chooses which visible markup tags a [[ChromeRule]] styles. Selectors are tested against each matched markup occurrence (its rule and modifier); chrome rules of different modifier kinds all apply, and among same-kind rules the highest [[Specificity]] wins, ties resolving to the first listed. Implement to target markup by a dimension other than the built-in modifier/rule/any.

methods.name: Matches
methods.summary: Whether this selector targets the markup parsed by rule into modifier.

properties.name: Specificity
properties.summary: Tie-break weight when several selectors match the same markup. Higher wins. Use a larger value for a narrower selector so the specific rule beats the general one.

events.name: Changed
events.summary: Raised after configuration changes that can affect matching or specificity. Mutable custom implementations must raise this for every such change so an owning chrome rule can reconcile.

types.name: InlineTagRule
types.summary: [[TagRule]] with HTML void-element semantics: every <tag> or <tag=value> behaves as a single self-closing placeholder, the /> shorthand is no longer required, and any stray </tag> is silently stripped.
types.remarks: Use for inline-media tags (obj, sprite) where range semantics don't apply — the tag is always a single inline insertion, not a wrapper around following text.
attributes: TypeDescription("XML-like void tag: <name> always behaves as a self-closing single insertion.")

types.name: IRangePayloadValues
types.summary: Optional allocation-free lookup surface for payload types that want named Inspector bindings without reflection. Returning false is a binding failure rather than an empty value.

methods.name: TryGetRangeValue
methods.summary: Tries to read one stable named value from this immutable payload snapshot.

types.name: LineBreakParseRule
types.summary:
Replaces the void
tag with a soft line break (U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR): the line wraps but stays in the same paragraph, keeping the surrounding direction and taking no inter-paragraph spacing — like HTML
or a word-processor Shift+Enter. A paragraph break is a literal newline (Enter) instead. Matches
,
and
case-insensitively with HTML void-element semantics: no closing tag, no nested content.
attributes:
TypeDescription("Replaces the void
tag with a soft line break — wraps the line, stays in the paragraph.")

types.name: MarkdownLinkParseRule
types.summary: Parses Markdown-style links: [link text](https://example.com).

properties.name: DefaultParameter
properties.summary: Merged behind the parsed URL (the URL stays the opaque first value).

types.name: MarkdownListParseRule
types.summary: Parses Markdown-style lists (bulleted and numbered).
types.remarks: Supports unordered lists with -, *, + markers and ordered lists with 1., 2), etc. Nested lists are detected by indentation level. An item ends at the first line break unless the following line is indented deeper than the item's own indent (which extends the item to cover an indented continuation or a nested list). CommonMark-style lazy continuation across non-indented lines is not supported — a non-indented line after an item is treated as a separate paragraph. List syntax has no close marker: matched ranges carry closeStart = closeEnd = -1 (closed by design), so match consumers never mistake an item for an unclosed pair.
attributes: TypeDescription("Parses Markdown-style bullet and numbered lists.")

methods.name: TryMatch
methods.summary: Anchors at the line start but accepts a probe anywhere inside the leading indent or at the marker itself (walking back over spaces to verify the line start) — so the parser's trigger-char jump scan, which lands directly on the marker character, still matches indented items. The emitted range always spans from the line start.

properties.name: SpacesPerLevel
properties.summary: Number of spaces per indentation level for nested lists.
attributes: Tooltip("Number of spaces per indentation level for nested lists.")

types.name: MarkdownWrapRule
types.summary: Parses symmetric open/close markers in text (e.g., **text**, ~~text~~).
types.remarks: The marker string is configurable — any string can be used as a marker with any modifier. When [[DefaultParameter]] is set, matched ranges use it as the parameter value. Matching follows CommonMark §6.2 flanking rules (simplified to the marker occurrence's neighbours): a marker opens only when left-flanking (next char is not whitespace, and not punctuation unless preceded by whitespace/punctuation) and closes only when right-flanking (mirrored). Markers made of _ additionally never open or close inside a word, so snake_case_name stays literal. Stray markers in arithmetic (2 * 3) never open.
attributes: TypeDescription("Activates the modifier using symmetric wrap markers, e.g. **text**.")

types.name: ParseRule
types.summary: Base class for text parsing rules that identify modifier application ranges.
types.remarks: Parse rules scan text for markup (XML tags, Markdown, custom markers) and produce [[ParsedRange]] entries that specify where modifiers should be applied. Rules are matched in priority order (highest first). Use higher priority for explicit markup rules (tags, Markdown) and lower priority for auto-detection rules (raw URLs).

methods.name: Apply
methods.summary: Emits this rule's source syntax wrapping content — the inverse of parsing, used by the editing layer to apply a style and to reconstruct copied markup. Returns when the rule has no content-wrapping form (void, block, or composite rules), meaning it cannot be applied as an inline style.

properties.name: Priority
properties.summary: Gets the matching priority. Higher values are matched first. Default is 0. Use positive values for explicit markup, negative for auto-detection.

properties.name: EscapePrefix
properties.summary: The literal-escape capability: a rule that consumes an escape prefix to protect the following character from markup interpretation returns that prefix; '\0' (default) = the rule provides no escaping. Consumers (literal-paste serialization, escaping injection) check this contract instead of naming a concrete rule type, so a custom escaping rule participates by overriding it.

properties.name: ProvidesLiteralEscape
properties.summary: Whether this rule provides literal escaping — see [[EscapePrefix]].

properties.name: CanWrap
properties.summary: Whether [[Apply]] emits a content-wrapping form — i.e. the rule can express an inline style application. Rules that override [[Apply]] to return syntax must also override this; consumers gate on it instead of probing [[Apply]] with empty input.

properties.name: IsStandalone
properties.summary: Indicates whether this rule operates without a modifier (e.g., protection rules like noparse). When, the rule can be registered via UniText.RegisterRule without pairing it with a BaseModifier.

properties.name: SourceToken
properties.summary: The source-markup token this rule's syntax is externally known by — whatever form the syntax takes (color for a tag rule, a marker for a marker rule) — or for a markerless rule. Interop consumers (clipboard bindings) pair rules with format schemas by this token instead of testing syntax families.

properties.name: Identity
properties.summary: Stable identity shared by rule instances that match the same syntax, compared case-insensitively — pairs separately configured instances (style merging, [[ByRule]] chrome selectors). The default (full type name) is correct for configuration-free rules. A rule whose instances can be configured to match different syntaxes MUST qualify it ([[TagRule]] → "tag:" + name, marker rule → "marker:" + marker) or return (identity by reference only) — otherwise differently configured instances are falsely treated as the same rule. Called on hot paths — cache the string, don't rebuild it per access.

properties.name: MarkupTriggers
properties.summary: Characters of which at least one must start any match of this rule that alters the visible text — strips markup (tags, markers), replaces it, or inserts content. Empty = the rule never consumes text (style-only matches like raw-URL detection); (default) = unknown, callers must assume any text can be consumed. Literal-paste escaping protects exactly these characters, so under-reporting silently mutates pasted text.

properties.name: TypingTriggers
properties.summary: Characters whose insertion or removal can make this rule begin or complete a consuming markup match. The editable document parses typed syntax only when an edit contains one of these characters or touches its immediate boundary; empty means this rule has no source syntax, while conservatively parses every direct typing edit. Include closing delimiters and required separators, not only match starts.

properties.name: ScanTriggers
properties.summary: Characters of which at least one must be at the match position for [[TryMatch]] to succeed at all (consuming or style-only). Defaults to [[MarkupTriggers]] — override when the rule matches at characters beyond its consuming set (raw-URL scheme letters). The parser bakes the union into a jump table and skips runs of non-trigger text, so an accurate set here is a large parse speedup; disables the fast scan for the whole component.
